fields.Name: Alabama
fields.Info:
• Its Black Belt, named for its dark soil, crosses the middle of the state; the Tennessee River loops across the north and Mobile Bay opens onto the Gulf of Mexico
  • Its capital Montgomery lies on the Alabama River; Cheaha Mountain, the highest point, is at the southern end of the Appalachians

fields.Name: Alaska
fields.Info:
• The largest US state by area, holding Denali, North America's highest peak, and stretching west to the Aleutian Islands; it is separated from the lower 48 by Canada
  • Purchased from Russia in 1867; the Trans-Alaska Pipeline carries oil from Prudhoe Bay on the North Slope to Valdez

fields.Name: Arizona
fields.Info:
• Contains the Grand Canyon, carved by the Colorado River, on the Colorado Plateau, and the Sonoran Desert with its saguaro cacti in the south
  • Its Four Corners meets Utah, Colorado, and New Mexico; Meteor Crater lies near Flagstaff

fields.Name: Arkansas
fields.Info:
• Divided between the Ozark and Ouachita mountains in the north and west and the Mississippi Alluvial Plain (Delta) in the east
  • Hot Springs National Park is the oldest federal reserve, and Crater of Diamonds is the only US diamond mine open to the public

fields.Name: California
fields.Info:
• The most populous state, running from the Sierra Nevada and Death Valley to the Central Valley and a long Pacific coast; Mount Whitney is the highest point in the lower 48
  • The San Andreas Fault runs through it; Yosemite Valley and Lake Tahoe are in the Sierra Nevada

fields.Name: Colorado
fields.Info:
• The Continental Divide crosses its Rocky Mountains, which hold 58 peaks above 14,000 ft, or 4,267 m (the “fourteeners”); the Colorado River rises in Rocky Mountain National Park
  • Its eastern third is High Plains, and Pikes Peak rises above Colorado Springs
fields.Photo caption: Trains meeting in Glenwood Canyon on the Colorado River

fields.Name: Connecticut
fields.Info:
• A New England state on Long Island Sound, split by the Connecticut River, which gives it its name (from a Mohegan word meaning “long tidal river”)
  • One of the smallest states; its highest point is on the shoulder of Mount Frissell
fields.Photo caption: The Pearl Harbor Memorial (“Q”) Bridge over the Quinnipiac River, New Haven

fields.Name: Delaware
fields.Info:
• The second-smallest state, on the Delmarva Peninsula, with the Delaware Bay to its east; its curved northern border is the Twelve-Mile Circle around New Castle
  • Its highest point, at Ebright Azimuth, is the lowest state high point

fields.Name: Florida
fields.Info:
• A low, flat peninsula between the Atlantic and the Gulf of Mexico, with the Everglades, the largest subtropical wetland in the US, and the Florida Keys
  • Lake Okeechobee is the largest lake in the state; Brittons Hill, its highest point, is only 105 m

fields.Name: Georgia
fields.Info:
• The largest state east of the Mississippi by land area, running from the Blue Ridge and Appalachian foothills across the Piedmont to the coastal plain and the Sea Islands
  • The Okefenokee Swamp lies in its southeast; Atlanta sits on the Piedmont near the Chattahoochee River, and Brasstown Bald is the highest point

fields.Name: Hawaii
fields.Info:
• An island chain in the mid-Pacific formed over a hotspot, with Hawaii (the Big Island), Maui, Oahu, and Kauai; Mauna Kea is the tallest mountain from base to summit
  • Kilauea and Mauna Loa are active shield volcanoes; it is the only state entirely on islands and the southernmost
fields.Photo caption: Nā Pali Coast State Park, Kauaʻi

fields.Name: Idaho
fields.Info:
• A mountain state of the Rockies with the Sawtooth Range and Hells Canyon of the Snake River, the deepest gorge in North America; its narrow northern panhandle borders Canada
  • The Snake River Plain in the south is a major potato-growing area

fields.Name: Illinois
fields.Info:
• A flat prairie state, bounded by the Mississippi on the west and the Ohio on the south, with Chicago on Lake Michigan
  • Its Cahokia Mounds are the largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico; its highest point, Charles Mound, is in the north

fields.Name: Indiana
fields.Info:
• A mostly flat state with the Wabash River, the Indiana Dunes on Lake Michigan and karst caves and hills in the south
  • Indianapolis, near the centre, lies on the White River; the Ohio River forms its southern border
fields.Photo caption: A Lake Michigan beach beside steel mills

fields.Name: Iowa
fields.Info:
• A rolling farmland state bounded by the Mississippi River on the east and the Missouri River on the west, with the Loess Hills along the Missouri
  • Its soil is so productive that it grows more corn than any other state; its Driftless Area in the northeast escaped glaciation

fields.Name: Kansas
fields.Info:
• Lies in the Great Plains, with the Flint Hills tallgrass prairie; the geographic centre of the contiguous US is near Lebanon
  • The Arkansas River crosses it; the Kansas River flows into the Missouri at Kansas City

fields.Name: Kentucky
fields.Info:
• Mammoth Cave, the world's longest known cave system, lies in its karst region; the Cumberland Plateau and Appalachian coal fields are in the east
  • The Bluegrass region in its centre is limestone-rich pasture land; the Ohio River forms its northern border

fields.Name: Louisiana
fields.Info:
• Formed largely by the Mississippi Delta, with bayous, marshes, and barrier islands on the Gulf of Mexico; Driskill Mountain, its highest point, is only 163 m
  • Divided into parishes, not counties; its coast loses land quickly to erosion and subsidence
fields.Photo caption: An aerial view of Louisiana's wetland habitats

fields.Name: Maine
fields.Info:
• The easternmost state of the contiguous US, with a rugged, island-filled coast; Mount Katahdin is the northern end of the Appalachian Trail
  • Moosehead Lake is its largest; Acadia National Park lies on Mount Desert Island

fields.Name: Maryland
fields.Info:
• The Chesapeake Bay splits it in two; the Eastern Shore is on the Delmarva Peninsula and the west reaches into the Appalachian Allegheny Plateau
  • The Potomac River forms much of its southern border with Virginia; Washington, D.C. was carved from its territory

fields.Name: Massachusetts
fields.Info:
• A New England state with a coast on Cape Cod, Nantucket, and Martha's Vineyard, and the Berkshire Hills in the west; Mount Greylock is its highest point
  • The Connecticut River crosses its west-centre, the Pioneer Valley; Boston lies on Massachusetts Bay, and the Quabbin Reservoir supplies its water

fields.Name: Michigan
fields.Info:
• Composed of two peninsulas separated by the Straits of Mackinac; the state touches four of the five Great Lakes and has more coastline than any other state except Alaska
  • The Upper Peninsula, linked by the Mackinac Bridge, holds Isle Royale and the Porcupine Mountains
fields.Photo caption: Mackinac Island in the Straits of Mackinac

fields.Name: Minnesota
fields.Info:
• Called the “Land of 10,000 Lakes”, it holds Lake Itasca, the source of the Mississippi River, and the Boundary Waters on the Canadian border
  • Its Northwest Angle is the northernmost point of the lower 48; Lake of the Woods and Lake Superior border it
fields.Photo caption: Tilted rock beds in Jay Cooke State Park

fields.Name: Mississippi
fields.Info:
• Lies on the Mississippi Alluvial Plain (the Delta) in the west and the loess Natchez bluffs, with the Gulf Coast in the south
  • Its highest point, Woodall Mountain, is only 246 m; the Tombigbee and Pearl rivers cross it

fields.Name: Missouri
fields.Info:
• The Missouri River crosses the state and meets the Mississippi near St. Louis; the Ozark Plateau lies in the south and the Bootheel in the southeast
  • The Lake of the Ozarks is a reservoir in the Ozarks; like Tennessee, it borders eight states
fields.Photo caption: The Gateway Arch and the St. Louis riverfront

fields.Name: Montana
fields.Info:
• Split by the Continental Divide into a mountainous west and Great Plains east, with Glacier National Park on the Canadian border
  • The Missouri forms at Three Forks, and the Yellowstone flows north out of the park across the state; Granite Peak is the highest point
fields.Photo caption: Saint Mary Lake in Glacier National Park

fields.Name: Nebraska
fields.Info:
• Lies in the Great Plains, with the Sandhills, the largest sand-dune region in the western hemisphere, and the Platte River across it
  • Its Panhandle in the west contains Chimney Rock and Scotts Bluff, landmarks on the Oregon Trail
fields.Photo caption: Winter at Scotts Bluff National Monument

fields.Name: Nevada
fields.Info:
• The driest state, mostly within the Great Basin and Mojave Desert, with basin and range mountains and few rivers; Boundary Peak is the highest point
  • Hoover Dam impounds Lake Mead on the Colorado River at its southeastern corner; Lake Tahoe straddles its border with California
fields.Photo caption: Mountains west of Las Vegas in the Mojave Desert

fields.Name: New Hampshire
fields.Info:
• A New England state with the White Mountains, including Mount Washington, notorious for its extreme weather, and a very short Atlantic coast
  • Lake Winnipesaukee is its largest lake; the Old Man of the Mountain fell in 2003
fields.Photo caption: Lake Winnipesaukee and the Ossipee Mountains

fields.Name: New Jersey
fields.Info:
• A peninsula between the Hudson and Delaware rivers, the most densely populated state, with the Pine Barrens and the Jersey Shore
  • Its Palisades line the Hudson, and the Highlands and Kittatinny Mountains lie in the northwest

fields.Name: New Mexico
fields.Info:
• A Southwest state on the Rio Grande, with the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, the Chihuahuan Desert, and the Llano Estacado
  • Contains Carlsbad Caverns, White Sands, and Chaco Canyon; Four Corners is on its northwest border

fields.Name: New York
fields.Info:
• Includes Long Island, the Hudson River valley with the Catskills, the Adirondacks, and Lake Placid; Mount Marcy is its highest peak
  • Niagara Falls lies on its border with Ontario; the Finger Lakes are in the west of the state

fields.Name: North Carolina
fields.Info:
• Runs from the Outer Banks barrier islands across the Piedmont to the Blue Ridge Mountains; Mount Mitchell is the highest point east of the Mississippi
  • The Great Smoky Mountains and Cape Hatteras National Seashore are its major parks
fields.Photo caption: Dry Falls on the Cullasaja River, Nantahala National Forest

fields.Name: North Dakota
fields.Info:
• A Great Plains state in the centre of North America, with the Missouri River and the Badlands in the west; the Red River forms the eastern border
  • Called the “Peace Garden State” for the International Peace Garden on the Manitoba border; its Williston Basin holds the Bakken oil field

fields.Name: Ohio
fields.Info:
• Bordered by Lake Erie on the north and the Ohio River on the south, with rolling plains in the west and Appalachian foothills in the southeast
  • The Cuyahoga River flows north to Lake Erie at Cleveland; Campbell Hill, the highest point, is only 472 m

fields.Name: Oklahoma
fields.Info:
• Lies between the Great Plains and the Ozarks; its Panhandle is a narrow strip in the northwest, and Tornado Alley crosses it
  • The Red River forms its southern border with Texas; the Wichita Mountains rise in the southwest, and the Arkansas and Cimarron rivers cross it
fields.Photo caption: The Cathedral of Our Lady of Perpetual Help in Oklahoma City

fields.Name: Oregon
fields.Info:
• Divided by the Cascade Range into a wet west with the Willamette Valley and a dry east high desert; Mount Hood is its highest peak
  • Holds Crater Lake, the deepest US lake, and the Columbia River Gorge on the Washington border

fields.Name: Pennsylvania
fields.Info:
• Crossed by the Appalachian ridges and the Allegheny Plateau, with the Susquehanna, Delaware, and Ohio rivers; Pittsburgh lies at the junction of the Allegheny and Monongahela
  • The Poconos rise in the northeast and a short Lake Erie shore gives it the port of Erie; Mount Davis is its highest point

fields.Name: Rhode Island
fields.Info:
• The smallest state by area, mostly around Narragansett Bay, with Block Island offshore; its formal name is “State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations”
  • Its highest point, Jerimoth Hill, is only 247 m

fields.Name: South Carolina
fields.Info:
• Runs from the Blue Ridge through the Piedmont to the Sea Islands, marshy lowcountry, and the Grand Strand
  • Sassafras Mountain is its highest point; Charleston lies at the confluence of the Ashley and Cooper rivers

fields.Name: South Dakota
fields.Info:
• Divided by the Missouri River into a green east and a drier west; the Black Hills, sacred to the Lakota, rise in the west, home to Mount Rushmore
  • Also holds the Badlands and Harney Peak, now called Black Elk Peak, its highest point

fields.Name: Tennessee
fields.Info:
• A long east–west state from the Mississippi River in the west to the Great Smoky Mountains in the east, with the Cumberland Plateau and Nashville Basin in between
  • It borders eight states; Clingmans Dome, the highest point, is in the Smokies
fields.Photo caption: Gatlinburg, beside Great Smoky Mountains National Park

fields.Name: Texas
fields.Info:
• The largest state in the contiguous US, running from the Gulf Coast plain and Piney Woods through the Hill Country and Llano Estacado to the Trans-Pecos desert and Guadalupe Peak, its highest point
  • The Rio Grande forms its border with Mexico; the Big Bend is a great loop of that river
fields.Photo caption: The Franklin Mountains above El Paso, from the air

fields.Name: Utah
fields.Info:
• Divided among the Rocky Mountains' Wasatch Range, the Great Basin, and the Colorado Plateau, whose five national parks include Zion, Arches, and Bryce Canyon
  • Holds the Great Salt Lake and Bonneville Salt Flats; Kings Peak is its highest point

fields.Name: Vermont
fields.Info:
• A New England state of the Green Mountains, including Mount Mansfield, and Lake Champlain on its western border
  • The only New England state without an Atlantic coast; its name is from the French for “green mountain”

fields.Name: Virginia
fields.Info:
• Runs from the Tidewater and Chesapeake Bay across the Piedmont to the Blue Ridge, Shenandoah Valley, and Appalachians; Mount Rogers is its highest point
  • The Potomac forms its border with Maryland; the Great Dismal Swamp and Chincoteague Island are on its coast

fields.Name: Washington
fields.Info:
• Divided by the Cascade Range into a wet west with Puget Sound and the Olympic Peninsula and a dry east; Mount Rainier is its highest peak
  • The Columbia River and Grand Coulee Dam are in the east; Mount St. Helens erupted in 1980

fields.Name: West Virginia
fields.Info:
• The only state entirely within the Appalachians, with steep hills and coal fields; its Eastern Panhandle reaches toward Washington, D.C.
  • The New River Gorge and Harpers Ferry, where the Shenandoah meets the Potomac, are features; its highest point is Spruce Knob
fields.Photo caption: Spruce Knob, the highest point, in the distance

fields.Name: Wisconsin
fields.Info:
• Bordered by Lake Superior and Lake Michigan, with the Door Peninsula and the Driftless Area in the southwest; the Wisconsin River crosses it
  • Its Apostle Islands lie in Lake Superior; Timms Hill is the highest point
fields.Photo caption: Aztalan State Park, site of a Mississippian settlement

fields.Name: Wyoming
fields.Info:
• A high, dry state of the Rocky Mountains and Great Plains with the Continental Divide, Devils Tower, the first national monument, and the Tetons
  • Holds most of Yellowstone, the world's first national park; it is the least populous state

fields.Name: Amazon – Ucayali – Apurimac
fields.Info:
• The world's largest river by discharge, and its basin holds the largest rainforest
  • Called the Solimões above its meeting with the Rio Negro at Manaus; its most distant headwater is the Apurímac in Peru
  • Its length as the world's longest river is disputed with the Nile

fields.Name: Nile – Kagera
fields.Parent: Egypt, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Burundi, Uganda, Rwanda, and Sudan
fields.Info:
• Flows north to the Mediterranean, forming its delta in Egypt; the White Nile rises near Lake Victoria and the Blue Nile at Lake Tana
  • The Aswan High Dam impounds Lake Nasser; its two arms join at Khartoum, and Rwanda's Kagera is its farthest headwater
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Egypt, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Burundi, Uganda, and 2 more

fields.Name: Mississippi – Missouri
fields.Info:
• Drains most of the United States between the Rockies and the Appalachians into the Gulf of Mexico
  • Its Missouri tributary is longer than the Mississippi itself; the Ohio and Arkansas are other large tributaries
  • St. Louis, Memphis, and New Orleans stand on its banks, and it rises at Lake Itasca in Minnesota
fields.Length: Longest river-system in North America, 4th longest river in total (6,275 km)

fields.Name: Yangtze / Chang Jiang
fields.Info:
• The longest river in Asia, flowing from the Tibetan Plateau to the East China Sea at Shanghai
  • Its Three Gorges Dam is the world's largest power station; the river separates north and south China

fields.Name: Congo – Chambeshi
fields.Parent: Angola, Zambia, Republic of the Congo, and DR Congo
fields.Info:
• The world's deepest river, at about 220 metres, and Africa's second-longest after the Nile
  • Crosses the equator twice and ends in an Atlantic estuary; its Inga Falls holds large hydroelectric potential

fields.Name: Amur – Argun
fields.Info:
• Forms much of the border between Russia and China; its Chinese name is Heilong Jiang
  • Its kaluga sturgeon can grow over five metres; it flows to the Sea of Okhotsk

fields.Name: Ob – Irtysh
fields.Info:
• Flows north across Western Siberia into the Gulf of Ob and the Arctic Ocean
  • Novosibirsk, Siberia's largest city, lies on the Ob; the Irtysh is its longest tributary

fields.Name: Paraná – Grande
fields.Info:
• Joins the Paraguay and then the Uruguay to form the Río de la Plata estuary
  • The Itaipú Dam, shared by Brazil and Paraguay, and the Iguazú Falls on a tributary lie on its system

fields.Name: Yenisei – Angara – Selenge
fields.Info:
• The largest river to flow into the Arctic Ocean, dividing western from central Siberia
  • Its tributary the Angara drains Lake Baikal, and its source is in Mongolia's Selenge River

fields.Name: Yellow River / Huang He
fields.Info:
• Called “China's Sorrow” for its catastrophic floods and shifting course; its yellow colour comes from loess silt
  • Flows through the Loess Plateau and forms a great northern bend, the Ordos Loop

fields.Name: Mackenzie – Peace – Finlay
fields.Info:
• Canada's longest river system, flowing from Great Slave Lake to the Arctic Ocean
  • Named for the Scottish explorer Alexander Mackenzie; its delta is a vast wetland

fields.Name: Lena
fields.Info:
• The longest river entirely within Russia, flowing to the Laptev Sea
  • Its delta is one of the largest in the world; Yakutsk stands on its banks, and permafrost underlies its basin

fields.Name: Mekong
fields.Parent: China, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam
fields.Info:
• Flows through six countries from Tibet to the Mekong Delta in Vietnam
  • Called the “Nine Dragons” river in Vietnam; upstream dams in China threaten its fisheries and the Tonlé Sap's flow reversal
fields.Photo caption: Floating market, Cần Thơ, Mekong delta
fields.Locator: ##Countries::China, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam

fields.Name: Murray – Darling
fields.Info:
• Australia's longest river system, draining the Murray–Darling Basin, the country's food bowl
  • The Murray forms the boundary between New South Wales and Victoria; the Darling is its longest tributary

fields.Name: Niger
fields.Parent: Guinea, Mali, Niger, Benin, and Nigeria
fields.Info:
• The Niger is West Africa's principal river, flowing in a great arc from the Guinea Highlands through Mali, Niger, and Nigeria to the Gulf of Guinea
  • Its Inner Niger Delta in Mali is a vast seasonal floodplain near Timbuktu and Mopti
  • Its chief tributary, the Benue, joins it at Lokoja in Nigeria

fields.Name: Pearl / Zhu Jiang
fields.Info:
• Southern China's largest river system, formed by the Xi, Bei, and Dong rivers
  • Its delta holds Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Macau, one of the world's largest urban areas

fields.Name: Irrawaddy
fields.Info:
• Myanmar's principal river, flowing from the confluence of the N'mai and Mali rivers to the Andaman Sea
  • Its delta is Myanmar's rice bowl; Mandalay and Bagan lie on it

fields.Name: Saint Lawrence Seaway – Saint Louis
fields.Info:
• Connects the Great Lakes to the Atlantic, with Montreal and Quebec City on its banks
  • The Seaway allows ocean-going ships through locks and the Welland Canal to Lake Erie

fields.Name: Brahmaputra – Yarlung
fields.Info:
• Flows from Tibet's Yarlung Tsangpo through Assam, where it forms the world's largest river island, Majuli, into Bangladesh
  • It carries huge floods and meets the Ganges before the Bay of Bengal; known as the Jamuna in Bangladesh

fields.Name: Orinoco
fields.Info:
• Venezuela's chief river, flowing through the Llanos to a vast delta on the Atlantic
  • The Casiquiare canal, a natural channel, links it to the Amazon basin; Angel Falls lies in its basin
fields.Photo caption: A channel in the Orinoco delta

fields.Name: Padma – Ganges
fields.Info:
• The Ganges is Hinduism's sacred river, rising at Gangotri in the Himalayas, with Varanasi on its banks
  • Its main distributary in Bangladesh is the Padma, which joins the Meghna before the Bay of Bengal

fields.Name: Negro
fields.Info:
• The Amazon's largest left-bank tributary and the world's largest blackwater river
  • At Manaus its dark water runs beside the pale Solimões in the Meeting of Waters; a canal links it to the Orinoco

fields.Name: Tocantins – Araguaia
fields.Info:
• A river of central Brazil flowing north to the Pará estuary near Belém
  • The Araguaia encloses Bananal, one of the largest river islands in the world; the Tucuruí Dam lies on the Tocantins

fields.Name: Madeira – Mamoré – Grande
fields.Info:
• The Amazon's largest tributary, formed by the Mamoré and Beni rivers on the Bolivia–Brazil border
  • Its rapids were bypassed by the Madeira–Mamoré Railway

fields.Name: São Francisco
fields.Info:
• Brazil's longest river wholly within the country, called “Velho Chico” (Old Chico), flowing through the semi-arid Northeast
  • Its Sobradinho reservoir is one of the world's largest artificial lakes

fields.Name: Syr Darya – Naryn
fields.Info:
• Flows from the Tian Shan across Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Kazakhstan toward the Aral Sea; called the Jaxartes in antiquity
  • Its Naryn arm rises in Kyrgyzstan, and diversion for cotton irrigation helped shrink the Aral Sea

fields.Name: Salween / Nu Jiang
fields.Info:
• One of the last free-flowing large rivers in Asia, with a gorge in Yunnan and few navigable stretches
  • Flows through the Three Parallel Rivers World Heritage Site with the Yangtze and the Mekong, then along the Myanmar–Thai border

fields.Name: Shatt al-Arab – Euphrates
fields.Info:
• The Euphrates rises in Turkey, flows through Syria and Iraq, and joins the Tigris to form the Shatt al-Arab, the Iran–Iraq border
  • Ancient Babylon and Ur stood on the Euphrates; the Shatt reaches the Persian Gulf
fields.Length: Longest in the Middle East (3,596 km)

fields.Name: Rio Grande
fields.Info:
• Called the Río Bravo in Mexico; it forms much of the border between Texas and Mexico
  • Rises in the San Juan Mountains of Colorado and flows through New Mexico to the Gulf of Mexico
fields.Photo caption: An islet in the Rio Grande at Albuquerque, New Mexico

fields.Name: Indus
fields.Info:
• Its valley was home to the Harappan civilization of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa
  • Rises in Tibet and flows through Ladakh and Pakistan to the Arabian Sea near Karachi; the Indus Waters Treaty divides its tributaries between India and Pakistan

fields.Name: Yukon
fields.Info:
• Rises in British Columbia and flows through Yukon Territory and Alaska to the Bering Sea
  • Passes Whitehorse and Dawson City, the route of the Klondike Gold Rush

fields.Name: Nelson – Saskatchewan
fields.Info:
• Drains Lake Winnipeg to Hudson Bay, and the Saskatchewan rises in the Rockies
  • The Nelson has large hydroelectric dams supplying Manitoba

fields.Name: Danube
fields.Parent: Hungary, Austria, Germany, Slovakia, Moldova, Romania, and Bulgaria
fields.Info:
• Europe's second-longest river, flowing through ten countries from Germany's Black Forest to the Black Sea delta in Romania
  • Passes four capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, and Belgrade; the Iron Gates gorge lies on the Serbia–Romania border
fields.Photo caption: The Danube at Novi Sad, from Petrovaradin Fortress
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Hungary, Austria, Germany, Slovakia, Moldova, and 2 more

fields.Name: Amu Darya – Panj
fields.Info:
• Flows from the Pamirs to the Aral Sea; called the Oxus in antiquity
  • Forms much of the Afghan border with Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan; its water diversion helped dry up the Aral Sea

fields.Name: Zambezi
fields.Parent: Angola, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, and Namibia
fields.Info:
• Africa's fourth-longest river and the largest flowing into the Indian Ocean; Victoria Falls lie on it
  • The Kariba and Cahora Bassa dams form huge reservoirs
fields.Photo caption: Victoria Falls, between the upper and middle Zambezi

fields.Name: Volga
fields.Info:
• The longest river in Europe, flowing through Russia to the Caspian Sea
  • Volgograd, Kazan, and Nizhny Novgorod are major cities on it; it has a large delta at Astrakhan
fields.Photo caption: The Volga at the Zhiguli Mountains

fields.Name: Lake Erie
fields.Info:
• The shallowest and southernmost Great Lake, with Cleveland, Buffalo, and Toledo on its shores; it drains through the Niagara River and Niagara Falls into Lake Ontario
  • Its islands include Pelee Island and the Bass Islands; its Cuyahoga River famously caught fire in 1969
fields.Photo caption: The Lake Erie shore at Reno Beach, Ohio

fields.Name: Lake Winnipeg
fields.Info:
• Manitoba's huge lake, drained by the Nelson River to Hudson Bay; the Red and Saskatchewan rivers feed it
  • A remnant of glacial Lake Agassiz, it is one of the world's largest freshwater lakes

fields.Name: Lake Ladoga
fields.Info:
• Europe's largest lake, outflowing through the Neva River to the Gulf of Finland at Saint Petersburg
  • Valaam Monastery stands on its islands; the “Road of Life” across its ice supplied besieged Leningrad in World War II
fields.Locator: Region::Republic of Karelia and Leningrad Oblast##Country::Russia|Region::Republic of Karelia and Leningrad Oblast

fields.Name: Lake Baikal
fields.Info:
• The world's deepest and oldest lake, holding about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water, in a rift in Siberia
  • Its unique fauna include the Baikal seal, or nerpa; its outflow is the Angara River
fields.Photo caption: Lake Baikal's water is especially clear
fields.Locator: Region::Irkutsk Oblast and Republic of Buryatia##Country::Russia|Region::Irkutsk Oblast and Republic of Buryatia

fields.Name: Great Slave Lake
fields.Info:
• The deepest lake in North America, on whose shore Yellowknife is built; the Mackenzie River drains it
  • Named for the Slavey people; it freezes for much of the year

fields.Name: Lake Huron
fields.Info:
• The second-largest Great Lake by area, with Georgian Bay and Manitoulin Island, the world's largest freshwater island
  • Connected to Lake Michigan by the Straits of Mackinac and hydrologically one lake with it
fields.Photo caption: Lake Huron viewed from Arch Rock at Mackinac Island
fields.Locator: Region::Ontario and Michigan##Countries::Canada and United States|Region::Ontario and Michigan

fields.Name: Lake Michigan
fields.Info:
• The only Great Lake wholly in the US, bounded by Chicago, Milwaukee, and Green Bay
  • Joined to Lake Huron by the Straits of Mackinac; the Chicago River was reversed to flow away from it
fields.Photo caption: The northern lake and its islands from the International Space Station, 2022

fields.Name: Lake Malawi
fields.Info:
• Holds more fish species than any other lake, especially cichlids; in the East African Rift, bordering Malawi, Mozambique, and Tanzania
  • Also called Lake Nyasa; the Scottish explorer David Livingstone called it the “Lake of Stars”

fields.Name: Great Bear Lake
fields.Info:
• The largest lake entirely within Canada, lying on the Arctic Circle in the Northwest Territories
  • The Great Bear River drains it to the Mackenzie; Port Radium on its shore was a uranium mine

fields.Name: Caspian Sea
fields.Parent: Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan, and Russia
fields.Info:
• The world's largest inland body of water, shared by five countries: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, and Azerbaijan
  • Fed mainly by the Volga, it has no outlet and lies below sea level; its sturgeon provide much of the world's caviar and its Baku region is an oil centre
fields.Photo caption: The Caspian shore near Khezershahr, Iran

fields.Name: Lake Superior
fields.Info:
• The largest freshwater lake by surface area, the northernmost, and deepest of the Great Lakes
  • It borders Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Michigan, and the Canadian province of Ontario; the Apostle Islands lie in it
fields.Photo caption: Pictured Rocks on the Lake Superior shore
fields.Locator: Region::Ontario, Michigan, Wisconsin, and Minnesota##Countries::Canada and United States|Region::Ontario, Michigan, Wisconsin, and Minnesota

fields.Name: Lake Victoria
fields.Info:
• Africa's largest lake and the source of the White Nile at Jinja, Uganda; it is shared by Uganda, Kenya, and Tanzania
  • The British explorer John Hanning Speke named it in 1858 for Queen Victoria; the introduced Nile perch devastated its native cichlids

fields.Name: Lake Ontario
fields.Info:
• The smallest Great Lake by area and the last in the chain before the Saint Lawrence River; Toronto and Hamilton lie on it
  • Niagara Falls empties into it, and it never freezes completely

fields.Name: Lake Balkhash
fields.Info:
• A Kazakh lake that is fresh in the west and saline in the east, divided by the narrow Uzun-Aral strait
  • Fed by the Ili River; irrigation diversions threaten it
fields.Area: Largest lake in Central Asia (18,400 km²)
fields.Photo caption: Lake Balkhash from orbit: fresh water in the west, saline in the east
fields.Locator: Region::Karaganda Region, Almaty Region, and Jambyl Region##Country::Kazakhstan|Region::Karaganda Region, Almaty Region, and Jambyl Region

fields.Name: Lake Tanganyika
fields.Parent: Tanzania, Zambia, DR Congo, and Burundi
fields.Info:
• The longest freshwater lake in the world and the second deepest, after Baikal, in the East African Rift; shared by four countries
  • Its outflow, the Lukuga River, drains to the Congo; Kigoma and Bujumbura are its main ports
fields.Photo caption: The eastern shore near Kigoma, Tanzania

fields.Name: Crater Lake
fields.Info:
• The deepest lake in the US, filling the caldera of Mount Mazama, which erupted about 7,700 years ago
  • Wizard Island is a cinder cone in its centre; it lies in Oregon's Cascade Range

fields.Name: Lake Matano
fields.Info:
• The deepest lake in Indonesia and on an island, with anoxic depths that resemble ancient oceans
  • Part of the Malili lake system in Sulawesi, which has many endemic fish and shrimp

fields.Name: Lake Issyk Kul
fields.Info:
• A huge saline, warm lake in Kyrgyzstan that never freezes despite its altitude; its name means “warm lake”
  • The second-largest alpine lake in the world, after Titicaca, and it is endorheic

fields.Name: Lake O'Higgins-San Martín
fields.Info:
• A glacial Patagonian lake with different names in Chile (O'Higgins) and Argentina (San Martín)
  • Fed by glaciers of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field; among the deepest lakes in the Americas
fields.Locator: Region::Aysén and Santa Cruz##Countries::Chile and Argentina|Region::Aysén and Santa Cruz

fields.Name: Lake Vostok
fields.Info:
• The largest subglacial lake in Antarctica, beneath 3.7 km of ice at Russia's Vostok Station
  • Sealed for perhaps 15 million years, it was reached by Russian drilling in 2012

fields.Name: Great Salt Lake
fields.Info:
• The largest salt lake in the Western Hemisphere, a remnant of prehistoric Lake Bonneville in Utah
  • Its brine shrimp are famous; it has no outlet and has been shrinking; the Spiral Jetty by Robert Smithson lies on its shore

fields.Name: Lake Turkana
fields.Info:
• The world's largest permanent desert lake and largest alkaline lake, in northern Kenya's Rift Valley
  • Called the “Jade Sea” for its colour; its shores yielded early hominid fossils, including Turkana Boy

fields.Name: Lake Chad
fields.Info:
• A shallow lake on the Sahel edge shared by Chad, Cameroon, Niger, and Nigeria that has shrunk by about 90 percent since the 1960s
  • It has no outlet; its basin also spans the Bodélé Depression

fields.Name: Lake Van
fields.Info:
• Turkey's largest lake, a salty soda lake at 1,640 metres in the eastern highlands
  • The Armenian Church of the Holy Cross stands on Akdamar Island; the ancient Urartian capital Tushpa lay on its shore
fields.Photo caption: Akdamar Island and the 10th-century Armenian Cathedral of the Holy Cross, on Lake Van

fields.Name: South Aral Sea
fields.Info:
• What is left of the Aral Sea, which lost most of its water from Soviet diversion of the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers for cotton
  • Once the fourth-largest lake in the world, it split into a northern and southern part, with the southern basin largely dry by 2014
fields.Photo caption: The shrunken South Aral Sea from orbit
fields.Locator: Region::Karakalpakstan, Aktobe, and Kyzylorda##Countries::Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan|Region::Karakalpakstan, Aktobe, and Kyzylorda

fields.Name: Lake Eyre
fields.Info:
• Australia's lowest point at 15 metres below sea level, an ephemeral salt lake that fills only after heavy rains
  • Also known as Kati Thanda, it holds the largest drainage basin in the country; its salt flats hosted Donald Campbell's 1964 land speed record
fields.Photo caption: Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre from the air, turned pink by algae

fields.Name: Lake Urmia
fields.Info:
• Iran's largest lake, a hypersaline endorheic lake in the northwest that has shrunk dramatically since the 1990s
  • Home to the brine shrimp Artemia and once a pink flamingo habitat
fields.Area: Largest lake in the Middle East (6,000 km²)
fields.Locator: Region::East Azerbaijan and West Azerbaijan##Country::Iran|Region::East Azerbaijan and West Azerbaijan

fields.Name: Qinghai Lake
fields.Info:
• China's largest lake, a saline, alpine lake on the Tibetan Plateau; its Mongolian name Koko Nor means “blue lake”
  • Bar-headed geese and the naked carp breed here
fields.Area: Largest lake in East Asia (4,500 km²)

fields.Name: Lake Nasser
fields.Info:
• A giant reservoir on the Nile behind the Aswan High Dam, mostly in Egypt with its southern end in Sudan
  • Its creation forced the relocation of the Nubian temples, including Abu Simbel
fields.Locator: Region::Aswan Governorate and Northern State##Countries::Egypt and Sudan|Region::Aswan Governorate and Northern State

fields.Name: Lake Volta
fields.Info:
• The largest reservoir in the world by surface area, formed by the Akosombo Dam on the Volta River in Ghana
  • It floods much of the Volta basin and supplies Ghana's hydroelectricity
fields.Photo caption: Fishing boats at a lakeshore village

fields.Name: Lake Kariba
fields.Info:
• The world's largest reservoir by volume, behind the Kariba Dam on the Zambezi, shared by Zambia and Zimbabwe
  • It lies upstream of the Cahora Bassa reservoir in Mozambique
fields.Locator: Region::Southern Province (Zambia), Mashonaland West, and Matabeleland North##Countries::Zambia and Zimbabwe|Region::Southern Province (Zambia), Mashonaland West, and Matabeleland North

fields.Name: Bratsk Reservoir
fields.Info:
• Formed by the Bratsk Dam on the Angara River in Siberia, one of the world's largest reservoirs by volume
  • The city of Bratsk was relocated when it flooded
fields.Photo caption: The Bratsk Dam on the Angara

fields.Name: Manicouagan Reservoir
fields.Info:
• An annular lake in Quebec, the remains of a meteorite crater about 214 million years old, visible from space
  • Called the “Eye of Quebec”; its central island is René-Levasseur Island

fields.Name: Lake Onega
fields.Info:
• Europe's second-largest lake after Ladoga, in Russia's Karelia, connected to it by the Svir River
  • The Kizhi Pogost wooden churches and the ancient petroglyphs at Besov Nos are UNESCO sites on its shores
fields.Photo caption: Kizhi Pogost, on an island in Lake Onega
fields.Locator: Region::Republic of Karelia, Leningrad Oblast, and Vologda Oblast##Country::Russia|Region::Republic of Karelia, Leningrad Oblast, and Vologda Oblast

fields.Name: Lake Athabasca
fields.Info:
• A lake on the border of Alberta and Saskatchewan, fed by the Athabasca River from the oil sands
  • Drains via the Slave River into the Mackenzie system; Fort Chipewyan lies on its shore

fields.Name: Lake Taymyr
fields.Info:
• The northernmost large lake in Russia, on the Taymyr Peninsula in Siberia's Arctic
  • Frozen most of the year and fed by the Lower Taymyr River
fields.Area: Largest lake north of the Arctic Circle (4,560 km²)

fields.Name: Lake Nicaragua
fields.Info:
• The largest lake in Central America, containing the volcanic island of Ometepe and freshwater bull sharks
  • A Nicaragua Canal rivalling Panama's was once proposed across it; Granada stands on its northwestern shore
fields.Area: Largest lake in Central America (8,000 km²)

fields.Name: Lake Toba
fields.Info:
• The world's largest volcanic lake, in a caldera formed by a supereruption about 74,000 years ago on Sumatra
  • Samosir Island in its centre is the homeland of the Batak people

fields.Name: Lake Balaton
fields.Info:
• The largest lake in Central Europe, shallow and warm, and Hungary's summer resort
  • The Tihany Peninsula projects into it, and it is drained by the Sió canal
fields.Area: Largest lake in Central Europe (592 km²)

fields.Name: Lake Vänern
fields.Info:
• The largest lake in the EU, in southwestern Sweden, drained by the Göta River to the Kattegat
  • The Göta Canal links it to the Baltic; Läckö Castle stands on its shore
fields.Area: The largest lake in the EU (5,500 km²)
fields.Photo caption: From the Gamla Ekudden nature reserve
fields.Locator: Region::Västra Götaland and Värmland##Country::Sweden|Region::Västra Götaland and Värmland

fields.Name: Lake Mweru
fields.Info:
• A lake on the Zambia–DR Congo border fed by the Luapula River, the Congo's upper course
  • It drains through the Luvua River to the Lualaba; its name means “lake”
fields.Locator: Region::Luapula Province and Haut-Katanga##Countries::Zambia and DR Congo|Region::Luapula Province and Haut-Katanga

fields.Name: Lough Neagh
fields.Info:
• The largest lake in the British Isles, at the centre of Northern Ireland and bordering five of its six counties
  • It supplies much of Northern Ireland's water; eels are commercially fished in it
fields.Area: Largest lake on the British Isles (392 km²)

fields.Name: Lake Albert
fields.Info:
• A lake on the Uganda–DR Congo border in the Albertine Rift, named by the British explorer Samuel Baker in 1864 for Prince Albert
  • It feeds the Albert Nile, part of the White Nile; it is Africa's seventh-largest lake

fields.Name: Lake Taupo
fields.Info:
• New Zealand's largest lake, filling the caldera of the Taupō supervolcano, which erupted in about 232 CE
  • The Waikato River, New Zealand's longest, flows out of it
fields.Area: Largest lake in New Zealand (616 km²)
fields.Photo caption: Māori rock carvings at Mine Bay

fields.Name: Lake Murray
fields.Info:
• The largest lake in Papua New Guinea, in the Western Province, and a lowland lake fed by the Strickland River
  • The Suki people live around it

fields.Name: Lake Titicaca
fields.Info:
• The highest navigable lake in the world, at 3,812 metres, shared by Peru and Bolivia; the Uros live on reed islands
  • It is traditionally the birthplace of the Inca, and the giant frog is endemic to it
fields.Area: Largest lake in South America (8,400 km²)
fields.Locator: Region::Puno and La Paz##Countries::Peru and Bolivia|Region::Puno and La Paz

fields.Name: Lake Constance
fields.Info:
• Shared by Germany, Austria, and Switzerland at the Rhine's outflow from the Alps, with the island of Mainau
  • The lake has no legally fixed borders; Zeppelin airships were built at Friedrichshafen on its shore
fields.Area: 3rd largest lake in Central Europe (536 km²)

fields.Name: Lake Geneva
fields.Info:
• Shared by Switzerland and France on the Rhône, with Geneva and Lausanne on its shore and the Château de Chillon
  • The Rhône enters at its eastern end and leaves at Geneva, where the Jet d'Eau rises; the Lavaux vineyard terraces line its northern shore
fields.Area: 2nd largest lake in Central Europe (580 km²)
fields.Photo caption: Geneva, where the Rhône leaves the lake, from the air

fields.Name: Lake Saimaa
fields.Info:
• Finland's largest lake, a maze of channels in the Finnish Lakeland with Olavinlinna castle at Savonlinna
  • Home to the endangered Saimaa ringed seal, found nowhere else
fields.Photo caption: The frozen lake and its islands from the air
fields.Locator: Region::Southern Savonia, Northern Savonia, North Karelia, and South Karelia##Country::Finland|Region::Southern Savonia, Northern Savonia, North Karelia, and South Karelia

fields.Name: Lake Biwa
fields.Info:
• Japan's largest and oldest freshwater lake, in Shiga near Kyoto, with the “Eight Views of Ōmi” scenes
  • Its Chikubu Island holds a shrine, and the lake is named for its resemblance to a biwa, the Japanese lute

fields.Name: Gulf of Finland
fields.Info:
• The eastern arm of the Baltic Sea between Finland to the north and Estonia to the south, reaching Saint Petersburg at its head where the Neva River enters
  • Shallow and low in salt, it freezes over in winter; Helsinki, Tallinn, and Saint Petersburg lie on it

fields.Name: Gulf of Riga
fields.Info:
• A bay of the Baltic Sea between Latvia and Estonia, entered through the Irbe Strait and Suur Strait
  • The Daugava River enters it at Riga; Saaremaa island partly closes it off

fields.Name: Baltic Sea
fields.Parent: Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Russia, Poland, Sweden, Germany, and Denmark
fields.Info:
• A shallow, low-salinity brackish sea of northern Europe, connected to the North Sea by the Danish straits (the Øresund and Belts) and the Kiel Canal
  • Its arms include the Gulf of Bothnia, Gulf of Finland, and Gulf of Riga; Gotland, Öland, Bornholm, and the Åland Islands lie in it
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Poland, Lithuania, and 2 more

fields.Name: Gulf of Bothnia
fields.Info:
• The northern arm of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland, divided into the Bothnian Bay in the north and Bothnian Sea in the south
  • It is narrowest at the Kvarken strait, and its shores are still rising through post-glacial rebound

fields.Name: Inner Seas off the West Coast of Scotland
fields.Info:
• The waters between the Scottish mainland and the Inner Hebrides, including the Minch and the Sea of the Hebrides
  • Islands such as Skye, Mull, Islay, and Jura lie in them

fields.Name: Irish Sea
fields.Info:
• The sea between Great Britain and Ireland, connected to the Atlantic by the North Channel and Saint George's Channel
  • The Isle of Man lies in its centre; Liverpool, Dublin, and Belfast are on its shores

fields.Name: Bay of Biscay
fields.Info:
• A gulf of the Atlantic along the west coast of France and north coast of Spain, known for rough seas, and the Biscay Abyssal Plain
  • Bilbao, La Rochelle, and Bordeaux (via the Gironde estuary) lie on it

fields.Name: Celtic Sea
fields.Info:
• The part of the Atlantic south of Ireland and southwest of Britain, between the Irish Sea and the Bay of Biscay
  • It reaches the edge of the continental shelf; the Scilly Isles, Saint George's Channel, and the Bristol Channel open onto it

fields.Name: Bristol Channel
fields.Info:
• A large inlet of the Atlantic between south Wales and southwest England, with one of the highest tidal ranges in the world
  • The Severn, Taff, and Usk rivers enter it; Cardiff, Swansea, and Bristol lie on it

fields.Name: English Channel
fields.Info:
• The arm of the Atlantic between southern England and northern France, linking the Atlantic to the North Sea at the Strait of Dover
  • The Channel Islands lie in it; the Channel Tunnel crosses it, and its narrowest point is 33 km wide
fields.Photo caption: White Cliffs of Dover, on the English Channel

fields.Name: Kattegat
fields.Info:
• A sea area between Jutland (Denmark) and the west coast of Sweden, connecting the Baltic Sea to the Skagerrak
  • It is linked to the Baltic through the Øresund, Great Belt, and Little Belt; Copenhagen and Gothenburg lie near it

fields.Name: Skagerrak
fields.Info:
• A strait between Norway, Sweden, and Denmark's Jutland, joining the North Sea to the Kattegat
  • It reaches the deep Norwegian Trench; the Oslofjord opens onto it

fields.Name: North Sea
fields.Parent: Norway, Denmark, Germany, Netherlands, Belgium, France, and United Kingdom
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the Atlantic between Great Britain, Scandinavia, and the Low Countries, connected to the Baltic by the Skagerrak and to the Atlantic by the English Channel
  • It contains Dogger Bank and large oil and gas fields; the Wadden Sea forms its southeastern shore
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Norway, Belgium, Denmark, Netherlands, France, and 2 more

fields.Name: Alboran Sea
fields.Parent: United Kingdom, Algeria, Morocco, and Spain
fields.Info:
• The westernmost part of the Mediterranean Sea, between Spain and Morocco, bounded on the west by the Strait of Gibraltar
  • Alboran Island lies in the middle; Málaga and Melilla are on its shores

fields.Name: Adriatic Sea
fields.Parent: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania, Greece, Italy, Slovenia, and Croatia
fields.Info:
• An arm of the Mediterranean between the Italian Peninsula and the Balkans, ending in the north at Venice and the Gulf of Trieste
  • It is connected to the Ionian Sea by the Strait of Otranto; its eastern coast is rugged with many islands, and its western coast is flat
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Italy, Slovenia, Albania, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro

fields.Name: Strait of Gibraltar
fields.Info:
• The narrow strait between Spain and Morocco (about 14 km wide) connecting the Atlantic to the Mediterranean
  • The Rock of Gibraltar, a British territory, stands on its north side; Ceuta is a Spanish exclave on the south side

fields.Name: Aegean Sea
fields.Info:
• An arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey, connected to the Black Sea by the Dardanelles, Sea of Marmara, and Bosporus
  • It contains the Cyclades, Dodecanese, and Sporades island groups, with Crete as its southern limit

fields.Name: Ligurian Sea
fields.Info:
• The part of the Mediterranean between the Italian Riviera, Corsica, and the French Riviera, with Genoa at its head
  • The Gulf of Genoa is its northern extension

fields.Name: Tyrrhenian Sea
fields.Info:
• The part of the Mediterranean west of mainland Italy, between Corsica, Sardinia, and Sicily
  • Its floor holds the Marsili seamount, Europe's largest submarine volcano; Naples lies on it

fields.Name: Balearic Sea
fields.Info:
• The part of the Mediterranean between the Iberian Peninsula's east coast and the Balearic Islands
  • Barcelona, Valencia, and Palma lie on or near it

fields.Name: Ionian Sea
fields.Info:
• The part of the Mediterranean south of the Adriatic, between Greece and southern Italy
  • It contains the deepest point in the Mediterranean, in the Calypso Deep; the Ionian Islands lie on its east

fields.Name: Sea of Azov
fields.Info:
• The shallowest sea in the world, connected to the Black Sea by the Strait of Kerch, between Russia and Ukraine
  • The Don and Kuban rivers enter it; the Crimean Peninsula forms its western boundary

fields.Name: Marmara Sea
fields.Info:
• An inland sea entirely within Turkey, between the Bosporus and the Dardanelles, separating European and Asian Turkey
  • Istanbul lies at its northeast corner; the Marmara Islands lie within it

fields.Name: Black Sea
fields.Parent: Russia, Georgia, Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, and Ukraine
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea between Europe and Asia, connected to the Mediterranean via the Bosporus, Sea of Marmara, and Dardanelles, and to the Sea of Azov via the Kerch Strait
  • Its deep waters are anoxic below about 150 m; the Danube, Dnieper, and Dniester enter it, and the Crimean Peninsula juts into it
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Turkey, Russia, Ukraine, Romania, Bulgaria, and Georgia

fields.Name: Bay of Fundy
fields.Info:
• A bay on the Atlantic coast of North America between New Brunswick and Nova Scotia, with the highest tides in the world (up to about 16 m)
  • The Hopewell Rocks and the tidal bore of the Petitcodiac River are features; Chignecto Bay and the Minas Basin are its inner arms

fields.Name: Caribbean Sea
fields.Parent: Central America, northern South America, and the Antilles — some 28 countries and territories
fields.Info:
• A tropical sea of the western Atlantic, bordered by Central America, northern South America, and the Antilles
  • Its deepest point is in the Cayman Trough; it is linked to the Pacific by the Panama Canal
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Mexico, France, United Kingdom, Cuba, Belize, and 2 more

fields.Name: Hudson Bay
fields.Info:
• A large inland sea of northeastern Canada, connected to the Atlantic by Hudson Strait and to the Arctic Ocean by the Foxe Basin
  • James Bay is its southern arm; it is ice-covered for much of the year, and Churchill is the main port

fields.Name: Río de la Plata
fields.Info:
• A wide estuary on the southeast coast of South America formed by the Paraná and Uruguay rivers, between Argentina and Uruguay
  • Buenos Aires and Montevideo lie on it; it is up to about 220 km wide at its mouth

fields.Name: Labrador Sea
fields.Info:
• An arm of the North Atlantic between Labrador in Canada and southwestern Greenland, connected to Baffin Bay by the Davis Strait
  • It is a site of deep water formation; the Labrador Current flows through it

fields.Name: Gulf of Mexico
fields.Info:
• A large ocean basin of the western Atlantic, bordered by the US, Mexico, and Cuba, connected to the Atlantic by the Straits of Florida
  • The Mississippi River enters at its northern shore; the Yucatán Peninsula bounds it on the south; it is a major source of oil and gas

fields.Name: Coastal Waters of Southeast Alaska and British Columbia
fields.Info:
• The sheltered coastal channels of the Inside Passage, between the Alexander Archipelago of Alaska and British Columbia
  • Includes Hecate Strait, Dixon Entrance, and Queen Charlotte Sound

fields.Name: Gulf of Alaska
fields.Info:
• An arm of the northern Pacific on the southern coast of Alaska, between the Alaska Peninsula and the Alexander Archipelago
  • Kodiak Island, Prince William Sound, and Cook Inlet lie on it

fields.Name: Bering Sea
fields.Info:
• The northernmost part of the Pacific, between Siberia and Alaska, connected to the Arctic Ocean by the Bering Strait
  • It contains the Pribilof Islands and the Aleutian Islands' northern edge, and the wide Bering shelf is one of the richest fishing grounds

fields.Name: Gulf of Saint Lawrence
fields.Info:
• The outlet of the Saint Lawrence River into the Atlantic, in eastern Canada, surrounded by Quebec, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland
  • It has the Magdalen Islands and Anticosti Island, and connects to the Atlantic through the Cabot Strait and Strait of Belle Isle

fields.Name: Hudson Strait
fields.Info:
• A channel between Baffin Island (Nunavut) and northern Quebec linking Hudson Bay to the Atlantic
  • Its tides are large and it is ice-choked for much of the year

fields.Name: Laccadive Sea
fields.Info:
• A sea of the Indian Ocean off the southwest coast of India, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives, also called the Lakshadweep Sea
  • The Lakshadweep Islands and the Maldives are within or beside it

fields.Name: Bay of Bengal
fields.Parent: Bangladesh, Myanmar, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, and India
fields.Info:
• The northeast part of the Indian Ocean, bordered by India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and Myanmar
  • The Ganges–Brahmaputra and Irrawaddy rivers enter it; the Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie on its east

fields.Name: Sea of Okhotsk
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the western Pacific between the Russian mainland, Kamchatka, the Kuril Islands, and Sakhalin
  • One of the coldest seas outside the poles, it is covered by ice in winter; it links with the Sea of Japan via the Tatar and La Pérouse straits

fields.Name: Andaman Sea
fields.Parent: Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, India, and Myanmar
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the northeastern Indian Ocean, between the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Myanmar, Thailand, and the Malay Peninsula
  • The Irrawaddy delta enters it; the Strait of Malacca is its southern outlet

fields.Name: East China Sea
fields.Parent: South Korea, Japan, Taiwan, and China
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the western Pacific between China, Taiwan, Japan's Ryukyu Islands, and the Korean Peninsula
  • The Yangtze River enters it near Shanghai; the disputed Senkaku Islands lie in it

fields.Name: Yellow Sea
fields.Parent: North Korea, South Korea, and China
fields.Info:
• A shallow marginal sea between mainland China and the Korean Peninsula, named for the silt carried by the Yellow River
  • Bohai Bay is its northwest arm; Qingdao, Dalian, and Incheon lie on it

fields.Name: Gulf of Guinea
fields.Parent: Nigeria, Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, São Tomé and Principe, Liberia, Ivory Coast, Ghana, Togo, and Benin
fields.Info:
• The northeasternmost part of the tropical Atlantic, off the coast of West and Central Africa between Cape Palmas (Liberia) and Cape Lopez (Gabon)
  • It contains Bioko, São Tomé and Príncipe, and Annobón; the Niger Delta enters it, and the Bight of Benin and Bight of Biafra are its arms
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Ghana, Togo, Benin, Gabon, Ivory Coast, and 2 more

fields.Name: Arabian Sea
fields.Parent: Pakistan, India, Maldives, Somalia, Yemen, Oman, and Iran
fields.Info:
• The northwestern part of the Indian Ocean, between India, the Arabian Peninsula, and the Horn of Africa
  • The Indus enters it; it connects via the Gulf of Oman and Gulf of Aden, and its monsoon winds shaped ancient trade
fields.Locator: ##Countries::India, Pakistan, Iran, Oman, Yemen, and 2 more

fields.Name: Red Sea
fields.Parent: Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Djibouti, Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt, Israel, and Jordan
fields.Info:
• A seawater inlet of the Indian Ocean between Africa and Asia, connected to the Mediterranean via the Suez Canal and to the Gulf of Aden via the Bab-el-Mandeb
  • It lies in a rift; the Gulf of Suez and Gulf of Aqaba branch off its northern end around the Sinai Peninsula
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Egypt, Israel, Yemen, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and 2 more

fields.Name: Mozambique Channel
fields.Info:
• An arm of the Indian Ocean between Madagascar and mainland Africa, about 1,600 km long
  • The Comoros and several French scattered islands lie in it

fields.Name: Persian Gulf
fields.Parent: Oman, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Iraq, and Iran
fields.Info:
• A shallow marginal sea of the Indian Ocean between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula, connected by the Strait of Hormuz to the Gulf of Oman
  • The Shatt al-Arab, the outlet of the Tigris and Euphrates, enters it; it holds much of the world's oil, and Bahrain is an island in it
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, and 3 more

fields.Name: Gulf of Aden
fields.Info:
• A gulf of the Arabian Sea between Yemen and Somalia, linked to the Red Sea by the Bab-el-Mandeb
  • Aden lies on it, and Socotra is at its mouth; it is a major shipping lane

fields.Name: South China Sea
fields.Parent: China, Taiwan, Philippines, Brunei, Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia, and Vietnam
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the western Pacific, from Singapore and the Strait of Malacca to Taiwan, one of the busiest shipping routes on Earth
  • It contains the Spratly and Paracel Islands, disputed by several states; the Mekong and Pearl rivers enter it
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Indonesia, Cambodia, Malaysia, Taiwan, Vietnam, and 2 more

fields.Name: Gulf of Oman
fields.Parent: Iran, Pakistan, Oman, and United Arab Emirates
fields.Info:
• A gulf connecting the Arabian Sea to the Strait of Hormuz, bordered by Iran, Pakistan, Oman, and the UAE
  • Muscat and Chabahar lie on it
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Iran, Pakistan, United Arab Emirates, and 1 more

fields.Name: Bass Strait
fields.Info:
• A strait between the Australian mainland (Victoria) and Tasmania, connecting the Tasman Sea to the Southern Ocean
  • King Island and the Furneaux Group lie in it; it holds oil and gas fields

fields.Name: Gulf of Papua
fields.Info:
• A large gulf on the south coast of Papua New Guinea, opening onto the Coral Sea
  • The Fly, Kikori, and Purari rivers enter it; Port Moresby is on its eastern side

fields.Name: Tasman Sea
fields.Info:
• The part of the South Pacific between Australia and New Zealand, about 2,000 km wide
  • Lord Howe Island and Norfolk Island lie in it; it is named for the Dutch explorer Abel Tasman

fields.Name: Great Australian Bight
fields.Info:
• A large open bay of the Southern Ocean on the southern coast of Australia, from Western Australia to South Australia
  • The Nullarbor Plain's cliffs face it; it is a whale-calving area

fields.Name: Philippine Sea
fields.Parent: Federated States of Micronesia, Palau, Indonesia, Philippines, United States, Taiwan, and Japan
fields.Info:
• The largest sea in the world, in the western Pacific east of the Philippines, Taiwan, and Japan
  • It contains the Mariana Trench (the deepest point on Earth, the Challenger Deep) and the Izu, Bonin, and Mariana island chains
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Japan, United States, Indonesia, Palau, Micronesia, and 2 more

fields.Name: Torres Strait
fields.Info:
• A strait between Cape York Peninsula in Australia and New Guinea, linking the Arafura Sea and Coral Sea
  • About 274 islands lie in it, including Thursday Island; it is named for the Spanish navigator Luis Vaez de Torres

fields.Name: Bismarck Sea
fields.Info:
• A sea in the southwestern Pacific off the northeastern coast of New Guinea, part of Papua New Guinea
  • It is bounded by the Bismarck Archipelago, including New Britain and New Ireland

fields.Name: Timor Sea
fields.Info:
• A shallow sea of the Indian Ocean between Timor and northwest Australia
  • The Timor Trough lies on its northern edge, and it holds large offshore oil and gas fields

fields.Name: Gulf of Carpentaria
fields.Info:
• A shallow, almost enclosed gulf of northern Australia between Cape York and Arnhem Land, an arm of the Arafura Sea
  • Groote Eylandt lies in it, and it is bordered by Queensland and the Northern Territory

fields.Name: Arafura Sea
fields.Parent: Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and Australia
fields.Info:
• A shallow sea over the continental shelf between northern Australia and western New Guinea, linked to the Timor Sea on the west
  • The Gulf of Carpentaria opens from it; the Aru Islands lie on its edge

fields.Name: Solomon Sea
fields.Parent: Solomon Islands and Papua New Guinea
fields.Info:
• A sea in the southwestern Pacific between Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands
  • Its floor holds the New Britain Trench

fields.Name: Coral Sea
fields.Parent: Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Australia, France, and Papua New Guinea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the South Pacific off northeast Australia, bounded by Vanuatu, the Solomon Islands, and Papua New Guinea
  • It holds the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system on Earth
fields.Locator: ##Countries::France, Australia, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, and Papua New Guinea

fields.Name: Banda Sea
fields.Info:
• A deep sea in eastern Indonesia between Sulawesi, the Maluku Islands, and Timor
  • The Banda Islands, once the world's only source of nutmeg, lie in it

fields.Name: Celebes Sea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the western Pacific between the southern Philippines, Sulawesi, and Kalimantan
  • The Sulu Archipelago bounds it on the north; Mindanao lies to the northeast

fields.Name: Singapore Strait
fields.Info:
• A busy shipping channel between Singapore and the Indonesian Riau Islands, linking the Strait of Malacca and the South China Sea
  • About 84 km long, it is one of the world's busiest lanes

fields.Name: Ceram Sea
fields.Info:
• A sea in the Maluku Islands of eastern Indonesia, north of the Banda Sea, between the island of Seram and the Sula Islands
  • Buru Island lies on its western edge

fields.Name: Flores Sea
fields.Info:
• A sea in Indonesia between Sulawesi and the Lesser Sunda Islands, north of Flores
  • It is part of the Indonesian seaway that links the Pacific and Indian Oceans

fields.Name: Halmahera Sea
fields.Info:
• A sea in Indonesia between Halmahera and the Raja Ampat Islands off western New Guinea
  • It lies in the heart of the Coral Triangle

fields.Name: Java Sea
fields.Info:
• A shallow sea of Indonesia between Java, Borneo, Sumatra, and Sulawesi, on the Sunda Shelf
  • Jakarta lies on it; the Sunda Strait links it to the Indian Ocean

fields.Name: Makassar Strait
fields.Info:
• A strait between Borneo and Sulawesi, connecting the Celebes Sea to the Java Sea
  • It follows Wallace's Line, which divides Asian and Australasian fauna; it is very deep

fields.Name: Gulf of Boni
fields.Info:
• A large gulf on the southeast coast of Sulawesi, between the peninsulas of South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi
  • Also called Teluk Bone; it opens south onto the Flores Sea

fields.Name: Gulf of Tomini
fields.Info:
• A large gulf of northern Sulawesi in Indonesia, with the Togian Islands within
  • It lies between the northern and eastern peninsulas of Sulawesi

fields.Name: Sulu Sea
fields.Info:
• A body of water in the southwestern Philippines between Palawan, Mindanao, the Sulu Archipelago, and Borneo
  • Tubbataha Reef, a UNESCO site, lies in it

fields.Name: Molucca Sea
fields.Info:
• A sea in Indonesia between Sulawesi and the Maluku (Molucca) Islands, on the boundary of two tectonic plates
  • It connects the Celebes Sea to the Banda Sea; Halmahera bounds it on the east

fields.Name: Savu Sea
fields.Info:
• A sea in eastern Indonesia between the Lesser Sunda Islands and the Timor Sea
  • The islands of Sumba, Flores, Sawu, and Timor lie on its rim

fields.Name: Bali Sea
fields.Info:
• A small sea of Indonesia off the north coast of Bali, between Java and the Lesser Sunda Islands
  • It lies east of the Java Sea and north of the Lombok Strait

fields.Name: Barents Sea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean north of Norway and Russia, between Svalbard, Novaya Zemlya, and Franz Josef Land
  • The North Atlantic Current keeps its southern part ice-free; Murmansk lies on the Kola Peninsula's coast

fields.Name: Beaufort Sea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean north of Alaska and Yukon, bounded by the Canadian Arctic Archipelago
  • The Mackenzie Delta enters it; the Prudhoe Bay oil field lies on its shore

fields.Name: Kara Sea
fields.Info:
• A shallow marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean north of Siberia, between Novaya Zemlya and the Taymyr Peninsula
  • The Ob and Yenisei rivers enter it through long estuaries (the Gulf of Ob); it is icebound for much of the year

fields.Name: Norwegian Sea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the North Atlantic between Norway, Iceland, the Greenland Sea, and Svalbard
  • The Lofoten Islands and Faroe Islands border it; the Norwegian Current keeps Norway's coast ice-free

fields.Name: East Siberian Sea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean between the Laptev Sea and the Chukchi Sea, north of eastern Siberia
  • The New Siberian Islands and Wrangel Island bound it; the Kolyma and Indigirka rivers enter it

fields.Name: Chukchi Sea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean north of the Bering Strait, between Chukotka in Russia and Alaska
  • Wrangel Island and Point Barrow are on its edge

fields.Name: Kara Strait
fields.Info:
• A strait between Novaya Zemlya's south island and Vaygach Island, linking the Barents Sea and Kara Sea
  • It is ice-choked for most of the year

fields.Name: Laptev Sea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean north of Siberia, between the Taymyr Peninsula and the New Siberian Islands
  • The Lena River enters it, forming a huge delta; it is frozen for most of the year

fields.Name: Davis Strait
fields.Info:
• A strait between Baffin Island and the southwest coast of Greenland, linking Baffin Bay with the Labrador Sea
  • It is a major route for icebergs; the Cumberland Peninsula bounds it on the west

fields.Name: Baffin Bay
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean between Baffin Island (Canada) and Greenland
  • It connects to the Atlantic through the Davis Strait; the Smith, Jones, and Lancaster sounds open into it

fields.Name: White Sea
fields.Info:
• A southern inlet of the Barents Sea on the northwest coast of Russia, connected to the Baltic by the White Sea–Baltic Canal
  • Arkhangelsk lies on the Northern Dvina delta, and the Solovetsky Islands are in it

fields.Name: Northwest Passages
fields.Info:
• The sea lanes between the Atlantic and Pacific through the Arctic Archipelago of Canada
  • It is opening as sea ice shrinks; Roald Amundsen made the first complete transit in 1903–06 on the Gjøa

fields.Name: Greenland Sea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea between Greenland, Svalbard, Iceland, and the Norwegian Sea
  • It is a site of deep water formation; the East Greenland Current flows through it

fields.Name: Lincoln Sea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean north of Greenland and Ellesmere Island, the northernmost sea on Earth
  • It is permanently covered by thick pack ice

fields.Name: Atlantic Ocean
fields.Info:
• The second-largest ocean, separating the Americas from Europe and Africa, stretching from the Arctic to the Southern Ocean
  • The Mid-Atlantic Ridge runs down its centre; the Puerto Rico Trench is its deepest point

fields.Name: Pacific Ocean
fields.Info:
• The largest and deepest ocean, covering about a third of Earth's surface, between Asia and Australia and the Americas
  • The Mariana Trench, with the Challenger Deep, is its deepest point; the Ring of Fire surrounds it

fields.Name: Indian Ocean
fields.Info:
• The third-largest ocean, bounded by Africa, Asia, Australia, and the Southern Ocean
  • Its monsoon winds shaped trade; the Java Trench is its deepest point

fields.Name: Southern Ocean
fields.Info:
• The ocean around Antarctica, generally taken as south of 60°S, defined by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current
  • The International Hydrographic Organization proposed its limits in 2000

fields.Name: Arctic Ocean
fields.Info:
• The smallest and shallowest ocean, around the North Pole, covered by sea ice for much of the year
  • Its Lomonosov Ridge divides the Eurasian and Amerasian basins; it connects to the Pacific by the Bering Strait

fields.Name: Mediterranean Sea
fields.Parent: Southern Europe, the Levant, and North Africa — 21 countries
fields.Info:
• A sea connected to the Atlantic by the Strait of Gibraltar, between Europe, Africa, and Asia, and to the Red Sea by the Suez Canal
  • It contains Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica, Cyprus, and Crete; its subdivisions include the Adriatic, Aegean, Ionian, and Tyrrhenian seas
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Spain, France, Monaco, Italy, Malta, and 16 more

fields.Name: England
fields.Capital Info: Not a sovereign country
fields.Info:
• The largest and most populous part of the United Kingdom, mostly lowland, with the Pennines, Lake District, and Cornish peninsula
  • The Thames flows through London to the North Sea; the Severn and Humber are other major estuaries

fields.Name: Scotland
fields.Info:
• The northern part of Great Britain, split into the Highlands, Central Lowlands, and Southern Uplands, with over 790 islands
  • Includes the Hebrides, Orkney, and Shetland; Ben Nevis is its highest peak, and Loch Ness lies on the Great Glen fault

fields.Name: United Kingdom
fields.Capital Info: Sovereign country
fields.Info:
• Composed of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland; it occupies Great Britain, the northeast of the island of Ireland, and many smaller islands
  • Its closest mainland neighbour, France, lies across the English Channel; Ben Nevis is its highest peak

fields.Name: Northern Ireland
fields.Info:
• Occupies the northeast of the island of Ireland, bordering the Republic in the south and west, with Lough Neagh at its centre
  • Its Giant's Causeway is a UNESCO basalt-column site, and the Mourne Mountains hold its highest peak, Slieve Donard
fields.Photo caption: Derry Peace Bridge, over the River Foyle

fields.Name: France
fields.Info:
• The largest country in the EU, with Atlantic, Channel, and Mediterranean coasts, the Alps, Pyrenees, and Massif Central; Mont Blanc is its highest peak
  • Its Loire, Seine, Rhône, and Garonne rivers cross it; overseas regions include Guadeloupe and Réunion
fields.Borders: Andorra, Belgium, Brazil, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Monaco, Spain, Suriname, and Switzerland
fields.Photo caption: The Maison Carrée, a Roman temple in Nîmes

fields.Name: Wales
fields.Info:
• A constituent country of the UK on the western side of Great Britain, largely mountainous, with Snowdonia, whose peak Snowdon is its highest
  • The Brecon Beacons and Pembrokeshire coast are national parks; Cardiff is its capital
fields.Photo caption: Snowdon (Yr Wyddfa), the highest mountain in Wales

fields.Name: Georgia
fields.Info:
• A Caucasus country on the eastern shore of the Black Sea, with the Greater Caucasus along its northern border with Russia and the Lesser Caucasus in the south; Shkhara is its highest peak
  • The Kura (Mtkvari) River flows through Tbilisi; Abkhazia and South Ossetia are Russian-backed breakaway regions

fields.Name: Germany
fields.Info:
• The largest economy in Europe, with the North German Plain, the Alpine south, and the Rhine, Elbe, and Danube rivers; the Zugspitze is its highest peak
  • The Black Forest lies in the southwest; Berlin, in the northeast, is on the Spree, and the Jutland Peninsula separates its North Sea and Baltic coasts
fields.Borders: Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, France, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, and Switzerland
fields.Photo caption: The Reichstag, seat of the Bundestag, Berlin

fields.Name: Greece
fields.Info:
• A mountainous peninsula and over 6,000 islands including Crete and the Cyclades; Mount Olympus is its highest peak
  • The Pindus range forms its spine; the Peloponnese is joined to the mainland only by the Isthmus of Corinth, with the Aegean to the east and the Ionian Sea to the west
fields.Borders: Albania, Bulgaria, North Macedonia, and Turkey

fields.Name: Greenland
fields.Info:
• The world's largest island, about 80 percent covered by an ice sheet; a self-governing territory of Denmark
  • Most people live on the southwest coast around the capital Nuuk; Kaffeklubben Island off its north coast is the northernmost land on Earth
fields.Photo caption: Sermiligaaq, a village in East Greenland

fields.Name: Hungary
fields.Info:
• A landlocked basin country dominated by the Great Hungarian Plain (Puszta) and the Danube and Tisza rivers; Lake Balaton is central Europe's largest lake
  • Its capital Budapest is split by the Danube into Buda and Pest
fields.Borders: Austria, Croatia, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Ukraine

fields.Name: Albania
fields.Info:
• A Balkan country whose Albanian Alps (the Accursed Mountains) rise in the north and whose Adriatic coast meets the Strait of Otranto
  • Shares Lake Ohrid with North Macedonia and Lake Shkodër with Montenegro; its coast holds the ruins of Butrint and Apollonia
fields.Borders: Greece, Kosovo, Montenegro, and North Macedonia

fields.Name: Andorra
fields.Flag Note: Moldova (wider, coat of arms with eagle)
fields.Info:
• A mountainous microstate in the eastern Pyrenees, ruled by the Bishop of Urgell and the French head of state as co-princes
  • Its highest point is Coma Pedrosa; the Valira River drains its valleys south into Spain
fields.Photo caption: Andorra la Vella in its Pyrenean valley

fields.Name: Austria
fields.Info:
• A landlocked Alpine country whose Grossglockner is the highest peak and whose Danube flows through Vienna
  • Its Salzkammergut lakes and Tyrol Alps host Innsbruck and Salzburg
fields.Borders: Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Liechtenstein, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Switzerland

fields.Name: Azerbaijan
fields.Info:
• Lies on the western shore of the Caspian Sea, with its capital Baku on the Absheron Peninsula and an oil-rich coast
  • Its Nakhchivan exclave is separated from the mainland by Armenia; the Greater Caucasus rises along its northern border
fields.Borders: Armenia, Georgia, Iran, Russia, and Turkey

fields.Name: Belarus
fields.Info:
• A flat, forested landlocked country with the Pripet Marshes in the south and the Białowieża Forest on the Polish border, home to European bison
  • The Chernobyl fallout in 1986 contaminated its southeast; the Dnieper and Neman rivers cross it
fields.Borders: Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Russia, and Ukraine
fields.Photo caption: Strusta Lake in the Vitebsk Region

fields.Name: Belgium
fields.Info:
• A small country of lowland coastal plains, with the Ardennes highlands in the south and the Scheldt estuary at Antwerp
  • Divided between Flemish (Dutch) and Walloon (French) regions; Brussels, in the centre, hosts the EU's main institutions, and the Meuse flows past Namur and Liège
fields.Photo caption: The Palace of the Nation, seat of the Federal Parliament, Brussels

fields.Name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
fields.Info:
• A Balkan country with a tiny Adriatic coastline at Neum, cut by the Dinaric Alps, and drained by the Sava and Drina
  • Its Stari Most bridge at Mostar spans the Neretva; the country is split into the Federation and Republika Srpska
fields.Photo caption: Stari Most, the Old Bridge at Mostar

fields.Name: Bulgaria
fields.Info:
• A Balkan country between the Danube in the north and the Rila and Pirin mountains in the south; Musala is its highest peak
  • The Balkan Mountains (Stara Planina) cross it from west to east, ending at its Black Sea coast
fields.Borders: Greece, North Macedonia, Romania, Serbia, and Turkey

fields.Name: Croatia
fields.Info:
• A crescent-shaped country whose Adriatic coast holds over a thousand islands, Dubrovnik, and Split, and whose Pannonian plain lies inland
  • Its Plitvice Lakes are cascading karst lakes; Istria is a peninsula in the northwest
fields.Borders: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Hungary, Montenegro, Serbia, and Slovenia

fields.Name: Czech Republic
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country made of Bohemia and Moravia, bounded by the Ore, Bohemian, and Sudeten mountains, and drained by the Elbe and Vltava
  • Its capital Prague lies on the Vltava; Sněžka is its highest peak

fields.Name: Denmark
fields.Info:
• A low, flat country on the Jutland Peninsula and about 400 islands including Zealand and Funen, connected by bridges and ferries; Copenhagen is on Zealand
  • Its kingdom also includes Greenland and the Faroe Islands; the Øresund Bridge links it to Sweden
fields.Photo caption: Bay of Aarhus viewed from southern Djursland

fields.Name: Estonia
fields.Info:
• A flat, forested Baltic country with more than 2,000 islands, including Saaremaa and Hiiumaa, and Lake Peipus on the Russian border
  • Its capital Tallinn lies on the Gulf of Finland

fields.Name: Faroe Islands
fields.Flag Note: Iceland (blue background, red and white cross), Norway (red background, blue and white cross)
fields.Info:
• A group of 18 volcanic islands in the North Atlantic between Iceland and Norway, with steep cliffs and no trees
  • A self-governing territory of Denmark

fields.Name: Finland
fields.Info:
• Called the land of a thousand lakes (nearly 190,000), with vast forests and Arctic Lapland; Haltiatunturi is its highest point
  • Its Åland Islands lie between it and Sweden, and the Gulf of Bothnia is to the west

fields.Name: Iceland
fields.Flag Note: Norway (red background, blue cross), Faroe Islands (white background, red and blue cross)
fields.Info:
• A volcanic island on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge with glaciers, geysers, and hot springs; the Great Geysir gave the English word geyser its name
  • Its Vatnajökull is Europe's largest glacier by volume; Reykjavik is the northernmost national capital

fields.Name: Ireland
fields.Flag Note: Ivory Coast (green and orange flipped, narrower)
fields.Info:
• Occupies five-sixths of the island of Ireland, with a central lowland ringed by coastal hills and the River Shannon, the longest in the British Isles
  • Its Cliffs of Moher and Ring of Kerry face the Atlantic
fields.Photo caption: The Uragh Stone Circle, County Kerry

fields.Name: Italy
fields.Info:
• A boot-shaped peninsula in the Mediterranean, split by the Apennines with the Alps in the north, and the islands of Sicily and Sardinia
  • Its Po plain in the north is the main farmland; Mount Etna, Vesuvius, and Stromboli are its volcanoes
fields.Borders: Austria, France, San Marino, Slovenia, Switzerland, and Vatican City
fields.Photo caption: Mont Blanc (Monte Bianco) from the Aosta Valley

fields.Name: Latvia
fields.Info:
• A flat, forested Baltic country with the Gulf of Riga, the Daugava River, and the Gauja valley; its highest point is only 312 m
  • Its capital Riga is on the Daugava near the gulf
fields.Photo caption: Turaida Castle near Sigulda, built in 1214 under Albert of Riga

fields.Name: Liechtenstein
fields.Info:
• A tiny Alpine principality between Switzerland and Austria on the Rhine, one of two doubly landlocked countries with Uzbekistan
  • Its Rhine Valley forms its western border

fields.Name: Lithuania
fields.Info:
• The southernmost and largest Baltic country, flat with lakes and forests, and with the Curonian Spit shared with Russia's Kaliningrad
  • Its Neman River crosses it; its capital Vilnius is inland
fields.Photo caption: Trakai Island Castle, a residence of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania

fields.Name: Luxembourg
fields.Capital Info: Officially Luxembourg.
fields.Info:
• A small landlocked country in western Europe with the Ardennes in the north and the Moselle valley in the southeast
  • Its capital Luxembourg City sits on a rock spur above two gorges
fields.Photo caption: The Chamber of Deputies, Luxembourg City

fields.Name: North Macedonia
fields.Info:
• A landlocked Balkan country crossed by the Vardar River, with Lake Ohrid, one of Europe's deepest and oldest lakes, shared with Albania
  • Its capital Skopje lies on the Vardar; Mount Korab on the Albanian border is its highest peak
fields.Borders: Albania, Bulgaria, Greece, Kosovo, and Serbia
fields.Photo caption: Heraclea Lyncestis, founded by Philip II of Macedon

fields.Name: Malta
fields.Flag Symbolism: The George Cross, awarded by King George VI for Maltese courage under siege in WWII, sits in the canton.
fields.Info:
