• An archipelago of three inhabited islands (Malta, Gozo, and Comino) in the central Mediterranean, south of Sicily
  • Its Megalithic Temples and Valletta's fortifications are UNESCO sites
fields.Photo caption: The Grand Harbour from Valletta's Upper Barrakka Gardens

fields.Name: Moldova
fields.Flag Note: Andorra (narrower, coat of arms with motto)
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country between Romania and Ukraine, mostly rolling hills between the Prut and Dniester rivers
  • Its Transnistria strip on the Dniester's east bank is a Russian-backed breakaway region
fields.Photo caption: Orheiul Vechi, above the Răut valley

fields.Name: Monaco
fields.Flag Note: Indonesia (wider, brighter red), Poland (red and white flipped, wider)
fields.Info:
• The second-smallest country in the world, a city-state of about 2 km² on the French Riviera, mostly enclosed by France
  • Monte Carlo and its harbour are the main areas
fields.Photo caption: La Condamine, Fontvieille, and the Rock with the Prince's Palace

fields.Name: Montenegro
fields.Capital Info: Cetinje is an honorary capital.
fields.Info:
• A mountainous Adriatic country whose name means “black mountain”, with the Bay of Kotor and Lake Skadar
  • The Tara River Canyon is Europe's deepest
fields.Borders: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, and Serbia

fields.Name: Netherlands
fields.Capital Info: While Amsterdam is the official capital, The Hague is the seat of the executive and legislative branches.
fields.Info:
• Much of it lies below sea level, protected by dikes and the Delta Works, and much of the land is reclaimed polders
  • The Rhine, Meuse, and Scheldt meet the North Sea in its delta; Amsterdam is its capital though the government sits in The Hague
  • Its overseas territories include Aruba, Curaçao, and Sint Maarten in the Caribbean

fields.Name: Norway
fields.Flag Note: Iceland (blue background, red cross), Faroe Islands (white background, red and blue cross)
fields.Info:
• A long Atlantic coastline cut by fjords, including the Geirangerfjord and Sognefjord, with the Scandinavian Mountains inland
  • Holds the Arctic territories of Svalbard and Jan Mayen; the Lofoten islands lie above the Arctic Circle
  • Its North Sea oil and gas fields make it rich

fields.Name: Poland
fields.Flag Note: Indonesia (white and red flipped, brighter red), Monaco (white and red flipped, narrower)
fields.Info:
• Mostly on the flat North European Plain, with the Baltic coast in the north, the Tatra Mountains on the Slovak border and the Vistula river flowing through Kraków and Warsaw
  • Its Masurian Lakes lie in the northeast, and its western boundary follows the Oder–Neisse line set after World War II
fields.Borders: Belarus, Czech Republic, Germany, Lithuania, Russia, Slovakia, and Ukraine

fields.Name: Portugal
fields.Flag Symbolism: An armillary sphere, a navigational instrument, recalls the Age of Discovery; the shield's five small escutcheons evoke Christ's five wounds, ringed by seven castles for defeated Moorish strongholds.
fields.Info:
• Occupies the western edge of the Iberian Peninsula, split by the Tagus into a mountainous north and a flatter south, with the Algarve on the south coast
  • Also includes the Atlantic archipelagos of the Azores and Madeira

fields.Name: Romania
fields.Info:
• Ringed by the Carpathians, which enclose the Transylvanian Plateau, with the Danube forming its southern border and reaching the Black Sea in its delta
  • Regions include Wallachia, Moldavia, Transylvania, and Dobruja; Moldoveanu Peak is its highest point
fields.Borders: Bulgaria, Hungary, Moldova, Serbia, and Ukraine
fields.Photo caption: The Transfăgărăşan road over the Făgăraş Mountains

fields.Name: Russia
fields.Info:
• The largest country in the world by area, spanning eleven time zones from the Baltic to the Pacific, and split by the Ural Mountains into European and Asian parts
  • Contains Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake, the Siberian rivers Ob, Yenisei, and Lena, and Mount Elbrus, Europe's highest peak
  • Its exclave of Kaliningrad lies on the Baltic between Poland and Lithuania
fields.Borders: Azerbaijan, Belarus, China, Estonia, Finland, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Mongolia, North Korea, Norway, Poland, and Ukraine

fields.Name: San Marino
fields.Info:
• An enclave entirely inside Italy on Mount Titano, on the border of Emilia-Romagna and the Marche; the fifth-smallest country by area
  • Its three towers on the mountain and the old town are a UNESCO site
fields.Photo caption: Guaita, the first of the three towers on Monte Titano

fields.Name: Serbia
fields.Info:
• Belgrade lies at the confluence of the Sava and Danube; the north is the flat Vojvodina plain, and the south is mountainous
  • Kosovo declared independence from it in 2008; it is landlocked
fields.Borders: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Romania
fields.Photo caption: Ruins of Felix Romuliana, Galerius's palace

fields.Name: Slovakia
fields.Flag Note: Russia (no coat of arms), Slovenia (wider, smaller coat of arms)
fields.Info:
• A landlocked Central European country dominated by the Carpathians, whose High Tatras are the highest range in the Carpathians
  • Its capital Bratislava lies on the Danube, near the Austrian and Hungarian borders
fields.Borders: Austria, Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Ukraine

fields.Name: Slovenia
fields.Info:
• A small country between the Alps and the Adriatic, with Mount Triglav its highest peak and a short coast at Piran
  • Its Lake Bled and Postojna Cave are famous; the Kras plateau gave the world karst its name

fields.Name: Spain
fields.Flag Symbolism: The coat of arms includes the Pillars of Hercules wound with a banner reading “Plus Ultra” (“Further Beyond”).
fields.Info:
• Occupies most of the Iberian Peninsula, with a high central plateau (the Meseta), the Pyrenees and Sierra Nevada, and the Balearic and Canary Islands
  • Its exclaves Ceuta and Melilla lie in Morocco; Gibraltar, a British territory, sits at the southern tip of the peninsula
fields.Borders: Andorra, France, Gibraltar, Morocco, and Portugal

fields.Name: Sweden
fields.Info:
• The largest Nordic country, with the Scandinavian Mountains in the northwest, large lakes such as Vänern and Vättern, and a long Baltic coast
  • Stockholm is built on islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic; Kebnekaise is its highest peak, and its Gotland and Öland islands lie in the Baltic

fields.Name: Switzerland
fields.Capital Info: No official capital; Bern is the de facto capital.
fields.Info:
• A landlocked Alpine country, whose Alps hold the Matterhorn, Jungfrau, and Monte Rosa, its highest peak (Dufourspitze)
  • It contains the sources of the Rhine and Rhône, and lakes such as Geneva and Constance on its borders
fields.Borders: Austria, France, Germany, Italy, and Liechtenstein

fields.Name: Turkey
fields.Flag Symbolism: The star and crescent, adopted from Ottoman tradition, is popularly (if inaccurately) linked to a legendary reflection of the moon in a pool of blood after battle.
fields.Info:
• Straddles Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus and Dardanelles; its capital is Ankara though Istanbul is largest
  • Central Anatolia is a high plateau ringed by the Pontic and Taurus mountains; Mount Ararat, near the Armenian border, is its highest peak
fields.Borders: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Georgia, Greece, Iran, Iraq, and Syria

fields.Name: Ukraine
fields.Capital Info: Also known as Kiev.
fields.Info:
• The largest country wholly in Europe, mostly fertile black-earth steppe, with the Carpathians in the west and the Dnieper flowing to the Black Sea
  • Includes the Crimean Peninsula, annexed by Russia in 2014; the Chernobyl nuclear plant lies in its north
fields.Borders: Belarus, Hungary, Moldova, Poland, Romania, Russia, and Slovakia

fields.Name: Vatican City
fields.Info:
• The world's smallest independent state, an enclave inside Rome on the Vatican Hill
  • Contains St Peter's Basilica, the Sistine Chapel, and the Vatican Museums
fields.Photo caption: The obelisk in St. Peter's Square, brought from Egypt by Caligula

fields.Name: Armenia
fields.Info:
• A landlocked Caucasus country whose Lake Sevan is among the largest high-altitude lakes; Mount Ararat lies just across the border in Turkey
  • Mount Aragats is its highest point; the Aras River forms its borders with Turkey and Iran

fields.Name: Cyprus
fields.Flag Symbolism: A copper-colored silhouette of the island itself sits above crossed olive branches, symbolizing peace between its Greek and Turkish communities.
fields.Info:
• The third-largest Mediterranean island, with the Troodos Mountains and the Kyrenia range; divided since 1974 by the Green Line through Nicosia
  • The British keep sovereign base areas at Akrotiri and Dhekelia

fields.Name: Kazakhstan
fields.Capital Info: Known as Nur-Sultan until September 2022.
fields.Info:
• The largest landlocked country and ninth-largest by area, mostly steppe and desert, with the Altai and Tian Shan mountains on the east and south
  • Holds the Baikonur Cosmodrome (leased to Russia), part of the Caspian Sea coast and much of the Aral Sea basin
fields.Borders: China, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan
fields.Photo caption: Mausoleums of Rabiga Sultān Begim and Khoja Ahmad Yasawi in the city of Turkestan

fields.Name: Egypt
fields.Flag Note: Iraq (text instead of emblem), Yemen (no emblem)
fields.Info:
• A largely desert country whose population lives along the Nile Valley and Delta; the Sahara covers the rest
  • Controls the Suez Canal and Sinai Peninsula; its Lake Nasser lies behind the Aswan High Dam
fields.Photo caption: Cleopatra VII and Caesarion in relief, Temple of Dendera

fields.Name: Algeria
fields.Info:
• The largest country in Africa by area, over four-fifths covered by the Sahara, with the Atlas Mountains along its northern Mediterranean coast
  • Its Hoggar (Ahaggar) mountains rise in the south; the Roman city of Timgad lies in the north
fields.Borders: Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Tunisia, and Western Sahara
fields.Photo caption: The Arch of Trajan in the Roman ruins of Timgad

fields.Name: Angola
fields.Info:
• Has a coastal plain, a central plateau, and the Namib Desert in the south; its Cabinda exclave is separated from the rest by the Congo's mouth
  • An oil-rich country whose Kwanza and Cunene rivers flow west and south
fields.Borders: DR Congo, Namibia, Republic of the Congo, and Zambia

fields.Name: Benin
fields.Capital Info: While Porto-Novo is the official capital, Cotonou is the de facto seat of government.
fields.Info:
• A narrow West African country running from a short Atlantic coast north to the Niger River, with lagoons and swamps in the south
  • Its Pendjari and W national parks lie in the north; the Ganvié stilt village stands on Lake Nokoué
fields.Borders: Burkina Faso, Niger, Nigeria, and Togo

fields.Name: Botswana
fields.Info:
• A flat, landlocked country that is mostly Kalahari Desert, with the Okavango Delta, a giant inland delta, in the northwest
  • The Makgadikgadi Pans in the northeast are huge salt flats
fields.Borders: Namibia, South Africa, Zambia, and Zimbabwe

fields.Name: Burkina Faso
fields.Info:
• A landlocked Sahelian country whose river system, the Volta, gave it its old name Upper Volta
  • Mostly flat savanna, with the Sahara advancing in the north
fields.Borders: Benin, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Mali, Niger, and Togo

fields.Name: Cameroon
fields.Info:
• Called “Africa in miniature” for its varied landscapes, from the coast to Mount Cameroon, an active volcano, to the Sahel in the north
  • Its Lake Chad lies on the northern border
fields.Borders: Central African Republic, Chad, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Nigeria, and Republic of the Congo
fields.Photo caption: Unity Palace, the presidential residence, Yaoundé

fields.Name: Burundi
fields.Capital Info: Official capital was moved from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2019.
fields.Info:
• A small landlocked country with highlands descending to Lake Tanganyika on its southwestern border
  • The source of the Ruvyironza, a headwater of the Kagera and so of the Nile, lies in its south
fields.Photo caption: Independence Square and monument in Bujumbura

fields.Name: Cape Verde
fields.Info:
• A volcanic archipelago of ten islands off West Africa, split into windward and leeward groups; Fogo island has an active volcano
  • Mostly arid, its main islands include Santiago, Sal, and São Vicente

fields.Name: São Tomé and Príncipe
fields.Info:
• The second-smallest African country, two volcanic islands and small islets in the Gulf of Guinea, on the equator
  • São Tomé's Pico de São Tomé is its highest point; the islands' rainforest is famous for cocoa
fields.Photo caption: The Cathedral of Our Lady of Grace, São Tomé

fields.Name: Central African Republic
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country of savanna plateau between the Congo and Chad basins, bordered by the Ubangi River in the south
  • Its Dzanga-Sangha reserve protects forest elephants and gorillas
fields.Borders: Cameroon, Chad, DR Congo, Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, and Sudan
fields.Photo caption: Falls of Boali on the Mbali River

fields.Name: Chad
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country spanning the Sahara in the north, the Sahel, and the shrinking Lake Chad, with the Tibesti Mountains in the north
  • Its Aouzou Strip was disputed with Libya until 1994
fields.Borders: Cameroon, Central African Republic, Libya, Niger, Nigeria, and Sudan
fields.Photo caption: Landscape in Guéra in south-central Chad

fields.Name: Equatorial Guinea
fields.Capital Info: Official capital moved from Malabo, on Bioko Island, to Ciudad de la Paz (formerly Oyala), a planned city still under construction on the mainland, in January 2026.
fields.Info:
• Consists of the mainland region Río Muni, where the new capital Ciudad de la Paz stands, and the island of Bioko, home of the old capital Malabo; Annobón lies far to the southwest
  • The only Spanish-speaking country in Africa

fields.Name: Kenya
fields.Flag Symbolism: A Maasai shield and crossed spears, symbols of the defence of the nation, lie over black, red, and green stripes.
fields.Info:
• An East African country crossed by the equator and split by the Great Rift Valley; Mount Kenya is Africa's second-highest mountain
  • Its Lake Turkana, Lake Victoria, and the Maasai Mara reserve are prominent features
fields.Borders: Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda

fields.Name: Comoros
fields.Info:
• A volcanic archipelago in the Mozambique Channel of Grande Comore, Anjouan, and Mohéli; Mount Karthala is an active volcano
  • Mayotte, geographically part of the group, remains a French territory

fields.Name: Ivory Coast
fields.Capital Info: While Yamoussoukro is the official capital, Abidjan is the de facto seat of government.
fields.Info:
• A West African country on the Gulf of Guinea with a forested south and savanna north, the world's largest cocoa producer
  • Abidjan, on the Ébrié Lagoon, is its largest city; Yamoussoukro's Basilica of Our Lady of Peace is among the largest churches in the world
fields.Borders: Burkina Faso, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, and Mali

fields.Name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
fields.Info:
• Africa's second-largest country, holding most of the Congo Basin rainforest and the Congo River, with a short Atlantic outlet
  • Its eastern Rift Valley lakes and Virunga volcanoes are home to mountain gorillas
fields.Borders: Angola, Burundi, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia

fields.Name: Djibouti
fields.Info:
• A small Horn of Africa country on the Gulf of Aden and the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, with volcanic terrain
  • Lake Assal is Africa's lowest point at 155 m below sea level
fields.Photo caption: Lake Assal, the lowest point in Africa

fields.Name: Guinea-Bissau
fields.Info:
• A low-lying coastal country with mangrove swamps and the Bijagós Archipelago of about 80 islands
  • Its main rivers include the Corubal and Geba

fields.Name: Eritrea
fields.Info:
• A Red Sea country with the Dahlak Archipelago, arid coastal lowlands, and highlands around its capital Asmara
  • The Danakil Depression on its border with Ethiopia is among the hottest places on Earth
fields.Photo caption: The Mosque of the Companions, Massawa

fields.Name: Ethiopia
fields.Info:
• A landlocked highland country split by the Great Rift Valley, whose Lake Tana is the source of the Blue Nile
  • Its Danakil Depression is one of the lowest and hottest places on Earth; Ras Dashen is its highest peak
fields.Borders: Djibouti, Eritrea, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan
fields.Photo caption: Fasil Ghebbi, the royal enclosure at Gondar

fields.Name: Gabon
fields.Info:
• A small equatorial country on the Atlantic, over 80 percent rainforest, with the Ogooué River and Loango National Park
  • Its coastal plain gives way to the Crystal Mountains
fields.Borders: Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea, and Republic of the Congo

fields.Name: The Gambia
fields.Info:
• The smallest country on mainland Africa, a narrow strip on both banks of the Gambia River, surrounded by Senegal except for its short coast
  • Its Juffureh is tied to Kunta Kinte in Alex Haley's Roots

fields.Name: Lesotho
fields.Info:
• A mountainous kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, the highest country in the world by lowest point (1,400 m)
  • Its Maloti Mountains and Drakensberg escarpment feed the Orange River
fields.Photo caption: A village in the Maloti Mountains

fields.Name: Liberia
fields.Info:
• A West African coastal country with mangrove-lined shores and rainforest inland
  • Its capital Monrovia, named for James Monroe, lies on Cape Mesurado; the St. Paul and Cestos rivers cross its coastal plain
fields.Borders: Guinea, Ivory Coast, and Sierra Leone

fields.Name: Madagascar
fields.Info:
• The world's fourth-largest island, off southeast Africa, with a central highland plateau and rainforest on the east coast
  • Its spiny forests in the south and lemurs are found nowhere else

fields.Name: Malawi
fields.Info:
• A narrow, landlocked country dominated by Lake Malawi in the Great Rift Valley and drained by the Shire River
  • Sapitwa, on the Mulanje Massif, is its highest point
fields.Photo caption: Mountains in Northern Malawi during the rainy season

fields.Name: Mali
fields.Flag Note: Guinea (green and red flipped, slightly darker green)
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country spanning the Sahara in the north and the Sahel, crossed by the Niger River with its Inner Delta
  • Its Timbuktu and Djenné are historic Niger trade cities
fields.Borders: Algeria, Burkina Faso, Guinea, Ivory Coast, Mauritania, Niger, and Senegal

fields.Name: Mauritania
fields.Info:
• A Saharan country with a short Atlantic coast, the Banc d'Arguin, and the Richat Structure, the “Eye of the Sahara”
  • Its iron ore is carried by one of the world's longest trains
fields.Borders: Algeria, Mali, Senegal, and Western Sahara

fields.Name: Mauritius
fields.Info:
• A volcanic island in the Indian Ocean ringed by coral reefs; the country also includes Rodrigues and the Agaléga Islands
  • The Black River Gorges and the basalt peak of Le Morne Brabant are landmarks; it was the only home of the dodo
fields.Photo caption: A panoramic view of Mauritius Island

fields.Name: Morocco
fields.Info:
• A northwest African country with Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts, the Atlas and Rif mountains and the Sahara in the south; Toubkal is its highest peak
  • The Strait of Gibraltar separates it from Spain by only 14 km; Ceuta and Melilla on its coast are Spanish exclaves

fields.Name: Mozambique
fields.Flag Symbolism: An AK-47 rifle crossed with a hoe, above an open book, sits on a red star — the only national flag to depict a modern firearm.
fields.Info:
• Has a long Indian Ocean coastline, with the Zambezi crossing the country and the Limpopo in the south
  • Its Cahora Bassa is one of Africa's largest dams; its capital Maputo is in the far south
fields.Borders: Eswatini, Malawi, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe
fields.Photo caption: The Island of Mozambique, the former capital

fields.Name: Namibia
fields.Info:
• The Namib Desert runs along its Atlantic coast, holding the Sossusvlei dunes and the Skeleton Coast, and the Kalahari lies to the east
  • Its Etosha Pan is a huge salt pan; Fish River Canyon is the largest canyon in Africa; the Caprivi Strip extends northeast
fields.Borders: Angola, Botswana, South Africa, and Zambia

fields.Name: Niger
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country, mostly Sahara, with the Aïr Mountains and the Ténéré desert in the north and the Niger River crossing its southwest past Niamey
  • Lake Chad touches its southeast; the uranium mines at Arlit lie on the western edge of the Aïr
fields.Borders: Algeria, Benin, Burkina Faso, Chad, Libya, Mali, and Nigeria

fields.Name: Nigeria
fields.Info:
• Africa's most populous country, spanning coastal mangroves, the Niger Delta oil region, and the savanna of the north
  • The Niger and Benue rivers meet at Lokoja to form a Y-shape; its capital Abuja is in the centre, while Lagos is the largest city

fields.Name: Republic of the Congo
fields.Info:
• Also called Congo-Brazzaville, it lies on the north bank of the Congo River opposite Kinshasa, with a short Atlantic coast at Pointe-Noire
  • Mostly rainforest, with the Batéké Plateau in the south and vast swamps in the north
fields.Borders: Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, DR Congo, and Gabon

fields.Name: Rwanda
fields.Info:
• Called the “land of a thousand hills”; a small, mountainous country on the Albertine Rift, with Lake Kivu on its western border
  • Its Volcanoes National Park in the northwest protects mountain gorillas; the Kagera River forms much of the eastern border
fields.Borders: Burundi, DR Congo, Tanzania, and Uganda
fields.Photo caption: A reconstruction of the ancient King's Palace at Nyanza

fields.Name: Senegal
fields.Info:
• Its capital Dakar sits on Cap-Vert, Africa's westernmost point; the country wraps around The Gambia
  • The Senegal River forms its northern border; Gorée Island lies off Dakar
fields.Borders: Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Mauritania, and The Gambia

fields.Name: Seychelles
fields.Info:
• An Indian Ocean archipelago of granitic and coral islands, whose Vallée de Mai on Praslin holds the coco de mer, the world's largest seed
  • Has the smallest population of any African country; Aldabra is one of the largest coral atolls

fields.Name: Sierra Leone
fields.Info:
• A West African coastal country whose name means “lion mountains”, with a rugged peninsula on which Freetown sits
  • Its mangrove coast rises inland to the Loma Mountains, where Mount Bintumani is the highest point; Freetown has one of the largest natural harbours in the world

fields.Name: South Africa
fields.Flag Symbolism: A horizontal Y shape represents formerly divergent paths in the country's history converging into one, united way forward.
fields.Capital Info: No legally defined capital: the branches of government are split over three cities: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative) and Bloemfontein (judicial).
fields.Info:
• Lies at the southern tip of Africa, with a central plateau (highveld), the Drakensberg escarpment and Table Mountain at Cape Town
  • Has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein; it surrounds the kingdom of Lesotho and holds Kruger National Park and the Karoo
fields.Borders: Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Mozambique, Namibia, and Zimbabwe

fields.Name: Sudan
fields.Info:
• The White and Blue Niles join at Khartoum to form the Nile, which crosses its deserts
  • Its Red Sea coast holds Port Sudan; Nubian kingdoms of Kush built more pyramids than Egypt
fields.Borders: Central African Republic, Chad, Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Libya, and South Sudan
fields.Photo caption: The Western Deffufa, a mud-brick temple at Kerma

fields.Name: Eswatini
fields.Flag Symbolism: A Nguni shield and a pair of spears, laid over black and white feathers, echo traditional Swazi royal regalia.
fields.Capital Info: While Mbabane is the official, executive capital, Lobamba is the traditional, spiritual, and legislative capital.
fields.Info:
• A small landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, mostly highveld, middleveld, and lowveld, with mountains on the Mozambique border
  • Formerly named Swaziland until 2018

fields.Name: Tanzania
fields.Capital Info: While Dodoma is the official capital, Dar es Salaam is the de facto seat of government.
fields.Info:
• Holds Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak in Africa, and the Serengeti plains, with the Ngorongoro Crater
  • Its Zanzibar Archipelago lies in the Indian Ocean; Lakes Victoria, Tanganyika, and Malawi touch its borders
fields.Borders: Burundi, DR Congo, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, Uganda, and Zambia

fields.Name: Togo
fields.Info:
• A narrow West African country running from a short Gulf of Guinea coast to the Sahel, with the Togo Mountains in the centre
  • Its capital Lomé lies on the coast, next to the Ghana border

fields.Name: Tunisia
fields.Info:
• The northernmost country in Africa, with a Mediterranean coast, the Atlas Mountains in the northwest and the Sahara in the south
  • The site of ancient Carthage near Tunis; Jebel ech Chambi is its highest point

fields.Name: Uganda
fields.Info:
• A landlocked East African country, mostly a plateau, with Lake Victoria, the Nile's outflow at Jinja, and the Rwenzori Mountains in the west
  • Its Bwindi forest holds mountain gorillas; Lakes Albert, Edward, and Kyoga are in its rift valley
fields.Borders: DR Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, and Tanzania

fields.Name: Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic
fields.Capital Info: While Laayoune, also known as El Aaiún, is the declared capital, Tifariti is the de facto seat of government.
fields.Info:
• A partially recognized state claiming Western Sahara, a desert territory on Africa's Atlantic coast; Morocco controls most of it, behind a long sand wall
  • Its refugees live in camps in Algeria's Tindouf area; it claims Laayoune as its capital, while its government sits at Tifariti in the free zone
fields.Photo caption: El Aaiún refugee camp, near Tindouf, Algeria

fields.Name: Zambia
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country on the Zambezi River, sharing Victoria Falls with Zimbabwe; Lake Kariba lies on their border
  • Its Copperbelt in the north is a major copper-mining region; Lake Tanganyika touches its north
fields.Borders: Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Tanzania, and Zimbabwe

fields.Name: Zimbabwe
fields.Flag Symbolism: The Zimbabwe Bird, a soapstone sculpture found at the ruins of Great Zimbabwe, perches atop a red star.
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country between the Zambezi and the Limpopo, sharing Victoria Falls with Zambia; Lake Kariba is on their border
  • Named for the stone ruins of Great Zimbabwe; its highest point is Mount Nyangani in the Eastern Highlands
fields.Borders: Botswana, Mozambique, South Africa, and Zambia
fields.Photo caption: The Zambezi River in the Mana Pools National Park

fields.Name: Canary Islands
fields.Info:
• A Spanish archipelago of seven main islands in the Atlantic off the northwest coast of Africa, of volcanic origin
  • Mount Teide on Tenerife is the highest peak in Spain; the islands include Gran Canaria and Lanzarote
fields.Waters: North Atlantic Ocean

fields.Name: Afghanistan
fields.Info:
• A mountainous, landlocked country split by the Hindu Kush; its Wakhan Corridor is a narrow strip reaching China
  • Its Khyber Pass and Kabul and Kandahar routes made it the crossroads of Central and South Asia; Britain drew its Durand Line border with British India in 1893
  • The Buddhas of Bamiyan were carved into cliffs in its central highlands
fields.Borders: China, Iran, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan
fields.Photo caption: Tents of nomads in Badghis Province

fields.Name: Bahrain
fields.Info:
• An island country of about 30 islands in the Persian Gulf, whose largest, Bahrain Island, is linked to Saudi Arabia by the King Fahd Causeway
  • The site of the ancient Dilmun trade centre and pearl-diving beds

fields.Name: Bangladesh
fields.Flag Symbolism: A red disc on green evokes the sun rising over green fields; it sits just off-center toward the hoist so it appears centred when the flag flies.
fields.Info:
• A low-lying delta country on the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna, mostly flat and flood-prone, with the Sundarbans mangrove forest in the southwest
  • Its Chittagong Hill Tracts lie in the southeast; its coast is frequently hit by cyclones
fields.Photo caption: The Shaheed Minar in Dhaka, commemorating the martyrs of the 1952 Bengali language movement

fields.Name: Bhutan
fields.Flag Symbolism: Druk, the Thunder Dragon of Bhutanese legend, clutches jewels representing wealth.
fields.Info:
• A Himalayan kingdom whose highest peak, Gangkhar Puensum, is the world's highest unclimbed mountain; its valleys are steep and forested
  • Paro's Tiger's Nest monastery clings to a cliff, and its fortress-monasteries are called dzongs
fields.Photo caption: The dzong in the Paro valley, built in 1646

fields.Name: Brunei
fields.Info:
• A small oil-rich sultanate on the northern coast of Borneo, split into two parts by the Malaysian state of Sarawak
  • Its Temburong district is a forested exclave
fields.Photo caption: The Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque, Bandar Seri Begawan

fields.Name: China
fields.Info:
• The world's third- or fourth-largest country by area, from the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayas to the Gobi Desert and the eastern coastal plains
  • Its Yangtze and Yellow rivers flow east; Mount Everest lies on its border with Nepal
fields.Borders: Afghanistan, Bhutan, India, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, North Korea, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Vietnam
fields.Photo caption: The Forbidden City in Beijing, with the Gate of Divine Prowess at centre

fields.Name: Cambodia
fields.Flag Symbolism: A silhouette of Angkor Wat sits at the centre — the only national flag to depict a specific building.
fields.Info:
• A low country centred on the Tonlé Sap lake and the Mekong River, ringed by mountains; the lake reverses its flow with the monsoon
  • Angkor Wat lies north of the lake near Siem Reap

fields.Name: Indonesia
fields.Flag Note: Monaco (narrower, darker red), Poland (red and white flipped, darker red)
fields.Info:
• The world's largest archipelago, with over 17,000 islands including Java, Sumatra, Borneo (Kalimantan), Sulawesi and western New Guinea
  • Sits on the Ring of Fire, with the Krakatoa and Tambora volcanoes; its capital Jakarta is on Java
fields.Borders: Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, and Timor-Leste

fields.Name: India
fields.Info:
• The most populous country, bounded by the Himalayas in the north, the Thar Desert in the west and the Deccan Plateau in the south
  • Its Ganges and Brahmaputra drain the north, and it has the Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep island groups
fields.Borders: Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, Myanmar, Nepal, and Pakistan
fields.Photo caption: The Brihadisvara Temple, built by Chola monarch Rajaraja I between 1003 and 1010 CE

fields.Name: Hong Kong
fields.Info:
• A special administrative region of China on the southern coast, on the Pearl River estuary, made up of Hong Kong Island, Kowloon, and the New Territories
  • Victoria Harbour separates the island from Kowloon; it also includes over 200 islands

fields.Name: Iran
fields.Info:
• A high plateau ringed by the Zagros and Elburz mountains, containing the Dasht-e Kavir and Dasht-e Lut deserts and Mount Damavand
  • Has coasts on the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf; it controls the Strait of Hormuz
fields.Borders: Afghanistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Pakistan, Turkey, and Turkmenistan

fields.Name: Israel
fields.Flag Symbolism: A blue Star of David between two blue stripes evokes the tallit, the traditional Jewish prayer shawl.
fields.Capital Info: Disputed: claimed and controlled as the capital, but also claimed by Palestine; most embassies are in Tel Aviv.
fields.Info:
• A narrow country with a Mediterranean coast, the Negev Desert in the south and the Jordan River, Sea of Galilee, and Dead Sea in the east
  • The Dead Sea is the lowest point on land at about 430 m below sea level
fields.Borders: Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, and Syria
fields.Photo caption: Tel Megiddo, the ruins of a Canaanite and later Israelite city

fields.Name: Iraq
fields.Flag Note: Egypt (emblem instead of text), Yemen (no text)
fields.Info:
• Centred on the Mesopotamian plain between the Tigris and Euphrates, joining at the Shatt al-Arab to reach the Persian Gulf
  • Has a very short coast at the Gulf; its north has the Zagros foothills and Kurdistan
fields.Borders: Iran, Jordan, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Turkey
fields.Photo caption: Shanidar Cave, where Neanderthal remains were found

fields.Name: South Korea
fields.Info:
• Occupies the southern half of the Korean Peninsula, mountainous in the east, with Hallasan on Jeju Island its highest peak
  • The Han River flows through Seoul; the Korean Demilitarized Zone near the 38th parallel forms the northern border

fields.Name: North Korea
fields.Info:
• Occupies the northern half of the Korean Peninsula, mountainous, with Paektu, a volcano on the Chinese border, its highest point
  • The Korean Demilitarized Zone, near the 38th parallel, separates it from South Korea; the Yalu and Tumen rivers form its border with China

fields.Name: Jordan
fields.Info:
• A mostly desert country with the Jordan Valley and Dead Sea on its west, and a short Red Sea coast at Aqaba
  • Home of Petra, carved into rose-red rock, and of Wadi Rum's desert canyons
fields.Borders: Iraq, Israel, Palestine, Saudi Arabia, and Syria
fields.Photo caption: The Oval Forum of Jerash (1st century CE), a city of the Decapolis

fields.Name: Japan
fields.Flag Symbolism: Hinomaru, the red sun disc, represents Amaterasu, the sun goddess of Japanese myth.
fields.Info:
• An island arc of four main islands (Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Shikoku) and thousands of smaller ones, with many volcanoes and earthquakes; Mount Fuji is its highest peak
  • Its Sea of Japan lies to the west and Pacific Ocean to the east

fields.Name: Lebanon
fields.Flag Symbolism: A cedar tree, the biblically referenced Cedar of Lebanon, stands for eternity and steadiness.
fields.Info:
• A narrow Mediterranean country with the Lebanon Mountains, the Beqaa Valley, and the Cedars, its national emblem
  • Beirut lies on a cape midway along the coast; the Litani River drains the Beqaa to the sea, and Qurnat as Sawda' is the highest point

fields.Name: Laos
fields.Info:
• A landlocked, mountainous country much of whose western border follows the Mekong River, with the Plain of Jars in the north
  • Its Annamite range forms the border with Vietnam
fields.Borders: Cambodia, China, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam
fields.Photo caption: Ruins of Muang Khoun, bombed in the 1960s

fields.Name: Kyrgyzstan
fields.Info:
• A mountainous landlocked country dominated by the Tian Shan, holding Lake Issyk-Kul, one of the largest alpine lakes
  • Its high pastures are used by nomads with yurts; the Fergana Valley lies partly in its southwest
fields.Photo caption: Tian Shan Mountains in East Kyrgyzstan

fields.Name: Kuwait
fields.Info:
• A small, flat desert country at the head of the Persian Gulf, with the island of Failaka and oil fields
  • Its border with Iraq was drawn by Britain in the 1920s
fields.Photo caption: Kuwait City and the Kuwait Towers

fields.Name: Myanmar
fields.Info:
• Bordered by the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea, with the Irrawaddy River flowing south through the centre to a large delta near Yangon
  • Its Bagan plain holds thousands of Buddhist temples, and the Shwedagon Pagoda stands in Yangon; it is also called Burma
  • Hkakabo Razi in the far north is the highest peak in Southeast Asia
fields.Borders: Bangladesh, China, India, Laos, and Thailand

fields.Name: Mongolia
fields.Info:
• A high landlocked country of steppe and the Gobi Desert between Russia and China, with the Altai mountains in the west
  • Its capital Ulaanbaatar is among the coldest national capitals

fields.Name: Maldives
fields.Info:
• The lowest-lying country in the world, made of 26 coral atolls in the Indian Ocean, with a highest point of about 2 m
  • Threatened by sea-level rise

fields.Name: Malaysia
fields.Info:
• Split between Peninsular Malaysia and the states of Sabah and Sarawak on Borneo, separated by the South China Sea
  • Mount Kinabalu, on Borneo, is its highest peak

fields.Name: Oman
fields.Flag Symbolism: The khanjar dagger and crossed swords, Oman's national emblem, sit in the canton.
fields.Info:
• Occupies the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, with the Hajar Mountains and Dhofar's frankincense region near the Rub' al Khali
  • Its Musandam peninsula is an exclave on the Strait of Hormuz, cut off by the United Arab Emirates and known for its fjord-like inlets
fields.Borders: Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, and Yemen
fields.Photo caption: Ruins of Khor Rori, built between 100 BCE and 100 CE

fields.Name: Nepal
fields.Flag Symbolism: The world's only non-rectangular national flag; its sun and crescent moon symbolize hope that the nation will last as long as they do.
fields.Info:
• Home to Mount Everest and holding eight of the world's 14 peaks over 8,000 metres, along its border with China
  • The Kathmandu Valley lies between the Himalayas and the Terai lowlands; the Buddha was born at Lumbini in the Terai

fields.Name: Palestine
fields.Capital Info: Disputed: claimed as the capital but controlled by Israel; Ramallah is the administrative centre.
fields.Flag Note: Sudan (red/white/black, green arrow), Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (with star and crescent)
fields.Info:
• Comprises the West Bank, west of the Jordan River, and the Gaza Strip on the Mediterranean, with East Jerusalem claimed as its capital
  • Its West Bank holds Bethlehem and Jericho, one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities
fields.Photo caption: Mount Gerizim, near Nablus, the Samaritans' holiest site

fields.Name: Pakistan
fields.Info:
• Contains K2, the second-highest mountain, in the Karakoram, and the Indus River valley of Mohenjo-daro
  • Its Balochistan is a dry western plateau, and the Thar Desert lies on its eastern border with India; it borders the Arabian Sea

fields.Name: Qatar
fields.Info:
• A small peninsula jutting north into the Persian Gulf from Saudi Arabia, mostly flat desert
  • Rich from the North Field, the world's largest natural gas field, shared with Iran
fields.Photo caption: A partially restored section of the ruined town of Zubarah

fields.Name: Saudi Arabia
fields.Flag Symbolism: The Shahada (the Islamic declaration of faith) sits above a sword; the flag is never flown at half-mast, since the text is considered sacred.
fields.Info:
• Occupies most of the Arabian Peninsula, with the Red Sea coast, Hejaz mountains, and the Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter), the largest sand desert
  • Home to the holy cities of Mecca and Medina; its capital Riyadh lies in the Najd plateau
  • Holds much of the world's oil, mostly in the east near the Persian Gulf
fields.Borders: Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, United Arab Emirates, and Yemen
fields.Photo caption: Qasr al-Farid, a rock-cut tomb at Hegra

fields.Name: Singapore
fields.Info:
• A city-state on Singapore Island and about 60 islets at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, separated from Malaysia by the Johor Strait
  • One of the world's busiest ports on the Strait of Singapore; much of its land is reclaimed

fields.Name: Syria
fields.Info:
• Its capital Damascus is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities; the Euphrates crosses the northeast and the Anti-Lebanon range is on the west
  • The ruins of Palmyra and Aleppo's citadel are UNESCO sites; the Golan Heights on its southwest border are occupied by Israel
fields.Borders: Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, and Turkey

fields.Name: Taiwan
fields.Info:
• A mountainous island off the southeast coast of China, separated from it by the Taiwan Strait; Yu Shan (Jade Mountain) is its highest peak
  • Also governs Penghu, Kinmen, and Matsu; formerly called Formosa, from the Portuguese Ilha Formosa

fields.Name: Sri Lanka
fields.Flag Symbolism: A lion holding a sword represents the Sinhalese majority; the orange and green bars stand for Tamil and Muslim minorities, framed by four bo leaves for Buddhist virtues.
fields.Capital Info: Colombo is often referred to as the capital but Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, a suburb of Colombo, is the official, legislative capital.
fields.Info:
• A teardrop-shaped island off the southern tip of India, from which it is separated by the Palk Strait and Adam's Bridge
  • Its central highlands produce tea; Pidurutalagala is its highest peak; it was Ceylon until 1972
fields.Photo caption: Sigiriya, the rock fortress of King Kashyapa

fields.Name: Tajikistan
fields.Info:
• Over 90 percent mountainous, with the Pamir range and Ismoil Somoni Peak; the Fedchenko Glacier is among the longest outside the poles
  • Its Panj River forms the border with Afghanistan; the Fergana Valley reaches its north

fields.Name: Thailand
fields.Info:
• Its shape is like an elephant's head, with mountains in the north and the Chao Phraya River flowing to the Gulf of Thailand
  • The narrow Kra Isthmus joins it to the Malay Peninsula; Doi Inthanon is its highest point
fields.Photo caption: Wat Phra Prang Sam Yod, a 13th-century Khmer temple in Lopburi

fields.Name: Timor-Leste
fields.Info:
• Occupies the eastern half of the island of Timor, plus the exclave of Oecusse and the islands of Atauro and Jaco
  • Its central mountains rise to Tatamailau (Mount Ramelau); it is the only Southeast Asian country with a mostly Catholic population

fields.Name: United Arab Emirates
fields.Info:
• A federation of seven emirates on the southeastern Persian Gulf, including Abu Dhabi, by far the largest, and Dubai
  • Fujairah faces the Gulf of Oman; its Liwa Oasis lies on the Rub' al Khali

fields.Name: Turkmenistan
fields.Info:
• Most of it is the Karakum Desert, where the burning Darvaza gas crater is called the “Gates of Hell”
  • Its western coast lies on the Caspian Sea; the Amu Darya forms part of its northeast boundary
fields.Photo caption: The Darvaza gas crater in the Karakum Desert

fields.Name: Yemen
fields.Capital Info: Also spelled as Sana'a.
fields.Info:
• Occupies the southwestern Arabian Peninsula, with the Red Sea coast, the Yemeni highlands around Sana'a and the desert Rub' al Khali to the northeast
  • Its Socotra island, with its dragon's blood trees, lies far off in the Arabian Sea; it controls the Bab-el-Mandeb strait with Djibouti

fields.Name: Vietnam
fields.Info:
• A long, S-shaped country along the east coast of mainland Southeast Asia, with the Red River delta in the north and the Mekong Delta in the south
  • The Annamite Range runs along its border with Laos; Ha Long Bay is famous for its limestone karst

fields.Name: Uzbekistan
fields.Info:
• One of the two doubly landlocked countries, with the Kyzylkum desert and the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers
  • The Silk Road cities of Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva lie here; the Aral Sea shrank dramatically in its northwest
fields.Borders: Afghanistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan

fields.Name: Fiji
fields.Info:
• An archipelago of over 300 islands, mostly volcanic, the largest of which are Viti Levu and Vanua Levu
  • The International Date Line bends around it

fields.Name: Papua New Guinea
fields.Flag Symbolism: A bird of paradise and the Southern Cross constellation appear across a flag split diagonally into red and black.
fields.Info:
• Occupies the eastern half of New Guinea plus islands including New Britain, Bougainville, and New Ireland, in a country with over 800 languages
  • Its central highlands rise to Mount Wilhelm; the Sepik and Fly rivers are the main rivers

fields.Name: Australia
fields.Flag Note: New Zealand (red stars, two fewer stars)
fields.Info:
• The world's sixth-largest country and the only one that is also a continent, mostly desert in its interior (the Outback), with Uluru and the Great Barrier Reef
  • Its Great Dividing Range runs down the east; its lowest point is Lake Eyre and highest Mount Kosciuszko
fields.Photo caption: The Great Barrier Reef from the air

fields.Name: Solomon Islands
fields.Info:
• A double chain of volcanic islands, including Guadalcanal, Malaita, and Santa Isabel, east of Papua New Guinea
  • Guadalcanal holds the capital Honiara and Mount Popomanaseu, its highest point

fields.Name: Argentina
fields.Info:
• Home to Aconcagua, the highest peak outside Asia, and stretches from the Pampas grassland to Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego
  • Its Iguazú Falls lie on the Brazilian border; it disputes the Falkland Islands with Britain
fields.Borders: Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay

fields.Name: Bolivia
fields.Capital Info: While Sucre is the constitutional capital, La Paz is the seat of government.
fields.Flag Note: Ghana (star instead of coat of arms)
fields.Info:
• A landlocked Andean country with the world's highest administrative capital (La Paz) and constitutional capital at Sucre
  • Holds the Salar de Uyuni, the largest salt flat, Lake Titicaca, and the Altiplano; it lost its coast to Chile in the War of the Pacific
fields.Borders: Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, and Peru

fields.Name: Brazil
fields.Flag Symbolism: A band of stars mirrors Rio de Janeiro's night sky on the day the republic was proclaimed (1889), one star per state; “Ordem e Progresso” (“Order and Progress”) is a positivist motto.
fields.Info:
• The largest country in South America and fifth-largest in the world, containing most of the Amazon rainforest and the Pantanal wetland
  • The Brazilian Highlands cover its east and centre, and the Iguazú Falls lie on the Argentine border; its planned capital Brasília is in the interior
fields.Borders: Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, France, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Uruguay, and Venezuela

fields.Name: Chile
fields.Info:
• A narrow ribbon between the Andes and the Pacific, about 4,300 km long, containing the Atacama Desert, the driest non-polar desert, and Patagonia
  • Includes Easter Island, Tierra del Fuego, and the Juan Fernández Islands far offshore

fields.Name: Colombia
fields.Info:
• The only South American country with coasts on both the Pacific and Caribbean, split by three Andean ranges
  • Its Amazon south and the Llanos plains lie east of the Andes; Bogotá sits on a high plateau
fields.Borders: Brazil, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela
fields.Photo caption: Capitolio Nacional, seat of the Congress

fields.Name: Ecuador
fields.Info:
• Named for the equator, which crosses it; the Andes' Avenue of Volcanoes includes Cotopaxi and Chimborazo, the farthest point from Earth's centre
  • The Galápagos Islands lie about 1,000 km west in the Pacific
fields.Photo caption: Ingapirca, an Inca outpost and temple of the Sun (Inti)

fields.Name: Guyana
fields.Info:
• The only English-speaking country in South America, with coastal lowlands, rainforest, and the Guiana Highlands
  • Its Kaieteur Falls is among the world's highest single-drop waterfalls; it has a border dispute over the Essequibo region with Venezuela

fields.Name: Paraguay
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country split by the Paraguay River into the Gran Chaco in the west and the fertile east; it lost territory to Brazil and Argentina in the War of the Triple Alliance (1864–70)
  • The Itaipú Dam on the Paraná is shared with Brazil, and the Chaco region was disputed with Bolivia in the Chaco War (1932–35)

fields.Name: Peru
fields.Info:
• Divided by the Andes into a dry Pacific coast, the highlands, and the Amazon lowlands, with the source of the Amazon in its Andes
  • Home of Machu Picchu near Cusco, the Nazca Lines, and Lake Titicaca on the Bolivian border
fields.Borders: Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador

fields.Name: Suriname
fields.Flag Symbolism: A single star at the centre stands for the unity of the country's varied population.
fields.Info:
• Over 90 percent forested, on the Guiana Shield, with its Central Suriname Nature Reserve a UNESCO site
  • The only South American country with Dutch as its official language; its coast is a low, swampy plain

fields.Name: Uruguay
fields.Info:
• The second-smallest South American country, mostly rolling grassland, on the Río de la Plata, bordered by Argentina and Brazil
  • Montevideo, its capital, holds nearly half its people; its national drink is mate
fields.Photo caption: A street in Colonia del Sacramento

fields.Name: Venezuela
fields.Info:
• Home of Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, and Lake Maracaibo, South America's largest lake; the Orinoco crosses its Llanos
  • Its Guiana Highlands hold tepuis; it holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, in the Orinoco Belt

fields.Name: Cook Islands
fields.Info:
• Fifteen Pacific islands in two groups: a volcanic southern group around Rarotonga, the largest, and a northern group of coral atolls
  • Self-governing in free association with New Zealand
fields.Photo caption: A motu in the Aitutaki lagoon

fields.Name: Federated States of Micronesia
fields.Info:
• Four states — Chuuk, Kosrae, Pohnpei, and Yap — spread over 2,700 km of the western Pacific, mostly atolls and volcanic islands
  • Nan Madol on Pohnpei is a ruined city built on artificial islets
fields.Photo caption: A view of Kolonia Town from Sokehs Ridge in Pohnpei

fields.Name: Guam
fields.Info:
• The largest island in Micronesia, in the western Pacific, the southernmost of the Mariana Islands, a US territory
  • It has a northern limestone plateau and a southern volcanic area; Hagåtña is its capital

fields.Name: Vanuatu
fields.Info:
• A Y-shaped chain of about 80 volcanic islands in the South Pacific, with active volcanoes such as Yasur on Tanna
  • Its Pentecost Island is the home of land diving, which inspired bungee jumping

fields.Name: Canada
fields.Info:
• The world's second-largest country, with the Canadian Shield, the Rocky Mountains, the Great Lakes, and the Arctic Archipelago
  • Has ten provinces and three territories; it holds the world's longest coastline and shares the longest international border with the United States

fields.Name: United States of America
fields.Info:
• The third- or fourth-largest country, spanning North America from the Atlantic to the Pacific, plus Alaska and Hawaii
  • Holds the Grand Canyon, Yellowstone, the Rocky Mountains, and the Mississippi River; its highest point is Denali and its lowest is Death Valley

fields.Name: Mexico
fields.Flag Symbolism: An eagle devouring a serpent while perched on a cactus depicts the Aztec founding legend of Tenochtitlan.
fields.Info:
• A country bridging North and Central America, with the Sierra Madre Oriental and Occidental, the Baja California peninsula, and the Yucatán
  • Its capital, Mexico City, lies in a high basin; its Río Bravo (Rio Grande) marks the US border
fields.Photo caption: Teotihuacan: the Pyramid of the Sun and the Avenue of the Dead

fields.Name: Puerto Rico
fields.Info:
• The easternmost island of the Greater Antilles, between the Atlantic and the Caribbean, an unincorporated US territory
  • Its central mountains, Cordillera Central, rise to Cerro de Punta; El Yunque is a national rainforest
fields.Photo caption: A ball court (batey) at the Tibes Indigenous Ceremonial Center, near Ponce

fields.Name: Cuba
fields.Info:
• The largest island in the Caribbean, with the Sierra Maestra mountains in the southeast and the Isle of Youth to the south
  • The US holds a base at Guantánamo Bay; the island lies 145 km from Florida
fields.Borders: United States (Guantánamo Bay Naval Base only)

fields.Name: Dominican Republic
fields.Info:
• Occupies the eastern two-thirds of Hispaniola, with the Cordillera Central and Pico Duarte, the highest peak in the Caribbean
  • Lago Enriquillo is a saltwater lake below sea level; its capital Santo Domingo is the oldest European city in the Americas
fields.Photo caption: Santa María la Menor, the oldest cathedral in the Americas, Santo Domingo

fields.Name: Haiti
fields.Info:
• Occupies the western third of Hispaniola, rugged and heavily deforested, with Pic la Selle its highest peak
  • Its capital Port-au-Prince was devastated by the 2010 earthquake
fields.Photo caption: Citadelle Laferrière (1805–1822), the largest fortress in the Americas

fields.Name: Jamaica
fields.Info:
• A mountainous Caribbean island, the third-largest of the Greater Antilles, with the Blue Mountains reaching over 2,200 m
  • Its Dunn's River Falls and Montego Bay draw tourists

fields.Name: Trinidad and Tobago
fields.Info:
• Two islands just off Venezuela, with Trinidad a continental island geologically part of South America
  • The Pitch Lake is the world's largest natural asphalt lake; Tobago has a coral reef and rainforest reserve

fields.Name: Bermuda
fields.Info:
• A British territory of about 181 small islands in the North Atlantic, roughly 1,000 km east of North Carolina, with the northernmost coral reefs in the Atlantic
  • The Gulf Stream keeps its climate mild; the islands are linked by causeways and bridges
fields.Photo caption: One of Bermuda's pink-sand beaches at Astwood Park

fields.Name: Guadeloupe
fields.Info:
• A French overseas region of islands in the Leeward Islands of the Caribbean, made up of Basse-Terre and Grande-Terre, shaped like a butterfly
  • Basse-Terre has the active La Soufrière volcano; the Saintes and Marie-Galante are smaller islands

fields.Name: The Bahamas
fields.Info:
• An archipelago of about 700 islands and thousands of cays in the Atlantic, east of Florida and north of Cuba
  • Nassau lies on New Providence; San Salvador is where Columbus is thought to have first landed

fields.Name: Barbados
fields.Info:
• A coral-limestone island in the eastern Caribbean, the easternmost of the Lesser Antilles, with a rugged Atlantic coast
  • Its highest point is Mount Hillaby; it is ringed by beaches on its Caribbean side

fields.Name: Belize
fields.Flag Symbolism: Fifty leaves ring the coat of arms; two loggers flank a mahogany tree, recalling the colonial timber trade.
fields.Info:
• Lies on the Caribbean coast of Central America, with the second-largest barrier reef in the world and the Great Blue Hole
  • Its Maya Mountains and rainforest hold the Maya sites of Caracol and Lamanai
fields.Photo caption: The Belize Barrier Reef from the air

fields.Name: Costa Rica
fields.Info:
• A narrow isthmus between the Caribbean and the Pacific with a spine of volcanic mountains and rainforest; its Poás and Arenal volcanoes are active
  • Has no army; its Monteverde cloud forest and Nicoya Peninsula are famous
fields.Photo caption: The ruined church at Ujarrás (1686–1693), Orosí Valley

fields.Name: El Salvador
fields.Flag Note: Nicaragua (different coat of arms, slightly lighter blue)
fields.Info:
• The smallest and most densely populated Central American country, on the Pacific with many volcanoes and frequent earthquakes
  • The only Central American country with no Caribbean coast

fields.Name: Guatemala
fields.Info:
• A mountainous country with volcanoes along the Pacific, including Tajumulco, the highest peak in Central America, and the Petén rainforest
  • Contains the Maya ruins at Tikal and Lake Atitlán ringed by volcanoes
fields.Borders: Belize, El Salvador, Honduras, and Mexico

fields.Name: Honduras
fields.Info:
• A mountainous Central American country with coasts on the Caribbean and a short Pacific coast at the Gulf of Fonseca
  • Its Bay Islands lie in the Caribbean; the Copán ruins are a Maya site
fields.Photo caption: The Fortaleza de San Fernando de Omoa

fields.Name: Nicaragua
fields.Flag Note: El Salvador (different coat of arms, slightly darker blue)
fields.Info:
• The largest country in Central America, with the volcanic chain along the Pacific side and the wet Mosquito Coast on the Caribbean
  • Lake Nicaragua holds freshwater sharks and Ometepe island, which has two volcanoes

fields.Name: Panama
fields.Info:
• A narrow isthmus joining North and South America; its canal links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans
  • Volcán Barú is its highest point; the Darién Gap on the Colombian border is a roadless jungle
fields.Photo caption: A Panamax ship in transit through the Miraflores locks, Panama Canal

fields.Name: Antigua and Barbuda
fields.Info:
• A Caribbean nation of low-lying limestone and volcanic islands; Antigua has the Shekerley Mountains and Barbuda is flat
  • Antigua's English Harbour and Nelson's Dockyard are a UNESCO site

fields.Name: Dominica
fields.Flag Symbolism: A Sisserou parrot, found only on Dominica, stands on a cross of yellow, black, and white.
fields.Info:
• A rugged volcanic Caribbean island called the “Nature Isle”, with rainforest and the Boiling Lake, a flooded fumarole
  • Its highest point is Morne Diablotins

fields.Name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
fields.Info:
• Its main island has the active La Soufrière volcano, which erupted in 1979 and 2021
  • The Grenadines, a chain of small islands including Bequia and Mustique, stretch south toward Grenada

fields.Name: Somalia
fields.Info:
• Occupies the tip of the Horn of Africa, with the longest coastline on mainland Africa, along the Gulf of Aden and Indian Ocean
  • Its northern region of Somaliland declared independence in 1991; the Juba and Shebelle rivers are its only permanent rivers

fields.Name: Zanzibar
fields.Info:
• A semi-autonomous archipelago in the Indian Ocean off the coast of Tanzania, made up of Unguja and Pemba
  • Zanzibar City's Stone Town is a UNESCO site; the islands were once major spice producers

fields.Name: Ghana
fields.Flag Note: Bolivia (coat of arms instead of star)
fields.Info:
• A West African country with a Gulf of Guinea coast, the Volta River and Lake Volta, one of the world's largest reservoirs
  • Its Ashanti region is a forested gold-producing plateau
fields.Borders: Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, and Togo
fields.Photo caption: Elmina Castle, built by the Portuguese in 1482

fields.Name: Guinea
fields.Flag Note: Mali (red and green flipped, slightly brighter green)
fields.Info:
• A West African country whose Fouta Djallon highlands are the source of the Niger, Gambia, and Senegal rivers
  • Holds the world's largest bauxite reserves
fields.Borders: Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Mali, Senegal, and Sierra Leone

fields.Name: New Zealand
fields.Info:
• Consists of the North and South Islands, separated by Cook Strait, plus Stewart Island; the Southern Alps rise to Aoraki (Mount Cook)
  • Sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, with the volcanic plateau of the North Island and fiords in the southwest

fields.Name: French Polynesia
fields.Info:
• A French overseas collectivity of 118 islands in the South Pacific in five groups, including the Society Islands and the Marquesas
  • Tahiti is the largest island; Bora Bora and Moorea are famous

fields.Name: Philippines
fields.Info:
• An archipelago of over 7,000 islands, the largest being Luzon and Mindanao, on the Pacific Ring of Fire, with Mount Pinatubo and Mayon Volcano
  • Its capital Manila lies on Luzon; Palawan and the Chocolate Hills of Bohol are well known
fields.Photo caption: Malacañang Palace, the president's residence, Manila

fields.Name: Kosovo
fields.Flag Symbolism: Six stars stand for Kosovo's six major ethnic groups, above a gold silhouette of the country's outline.
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country in the central Balkans, between Serbia, Albania, Montenegro, and North Macedonia, mostly highland basins
  • Its Kosovo Polje and the Metohija basin are the main plains; recognized by about half the world's states
fields.Borders: Albania, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia

fields.Name: Libya
fields.Info:
• A vast, mostly Saharan country on the Mediterranean, with the Jebel Akhdar highlands, Cyrenaica, and Tripolitania
  • Its Fezzan region in the southwest is a desert of oases; it controls part of the Gulf of Sidra
fields.Borders: Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Niger, Sudan, and Tunisia
fields.Photo caption: The Atiq Mosque at Awjila, the oldest in the Sahara

fields.Name: Palau
fields.Info:
• Its Rock Islands are a UNESCO site of limestone mushroom islets, and its Jellyfish Lake holds harmless stingless jellyfish
  • An archipelago of over 500 islands in the western Pacific; Babeldaob is the largest
fields.Photo caption: The Rock Islands from the air

fields.Name: Saint Lucia
fields.Info:
• A volcanic Caribbean island known for the twin Pitons, a UNESCO site, and the Sulphur Springs at Soufrière, a drive-in volcano
  • Lies in the Windward Islands between Martinique and Saint Vincent
fields.Photo caption: Gros Islet and Rodney Bay from Pigeon Island

fields.Name: Bali
fields.Info:
• An island of the Lesser Sunda Islands, east of Java across the Bali Strait, dominated by volcanoes including the active Mount Agung
  • Known for Hindu temples such as Tanah Lot and Uluwatu, terraced rice fields, and beach resorts at Kuta
fields.Waters: Bali Sea and Indian Ocean

fields.Name: Grenada
fields.Flag Symbolism: A nutmeg pod, the island's chief export, sits in the hoist; seven stars stand for its parishes.
fields.Info:
• A volcanic Caribbean island, the Spice Isle, with the crater lake Grand Étang and nutmeg plantations; Carriacou lies to the north
  • Its capital St. George's curves around a horseshoe-shaped harbour; Mount St. Catherine is its highest point
fields.Photo caption: St. George's, the capital, from above

fields.Name: British Virgin Islands
fields.Info:
• A British territory in the Caribbean of about 60 islands, east of Puerto Rico, with Tortola, Virgin Gorda, Anegada, and Jost Van Dyke
  • It is a major yachting destination; the US Virgin Islands lie to the west
fields.Photo caption: Ruins of St. Phillip's Church, Tortola

fields.Name: Turks and Caicos Islands
fields.Info:
• A British territory in the Atlantic, southeast of the Bahamas, made up of two island groups separated by the Turks Island Passage
  • Providenciales is its tourist centre; Grand Turk has the capital

fields.Name: Cayman Islands
fields.Info:
• A British territory in the western Caribbean of three islands, Grand Cayman, Cayman Brac, and Little Cayman, south of Cuba
  • The Cayman Trench, the deepest point in the Caribbean, lies south of them

fields.Name: Anguilla
fields.Info:
• A British territory in the northern Leeward Islands of the Caribbean, a flat, coral island north of Saint Martin
  • It is about 26 km long, with white beaches

fields.Name: Azores
fields.Info:
• A Portuguese archipelago of nine volcanic islands in the mid-Atlantic, about 1,400 km west of Lisbon, on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
  • Mount Pico on Pico Island is Portugal's highest peak; its capital is Ponta Delgada on São Miguel
fields.Waters: North Atlantic Ocean

fields.Name: Curaçao
fields.Info:
• A constituent country of the Netherlands in the southern Caribbean, about 65 km north of Venezuela
  • It is one of the ABC Islands; its capital, Willemstad, has colourful Dutch colonial buildings

fields.Name: French Guiana
fields.Info:
• A French overseas region on the northeast coast of South America, bordered by Suriname and Brazil, mostly rainforest
  • The Guiana Space Centre at Kourou launches rockets near the equator; the Îles du Salut lie offshore
fields.Photo caption: Devil's Island, one of the Îles du Salut

fields.Name: Gibraltar
fields.Info:
• A British territory at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula, on the Strait of Gibraltar, dominated by the Rock of Gibraltar
  • It has a land border with Spain; the airport runway crosses the main road
fields.Photo caption: Gibraltar from the air, looking north-west

fields.Name: Guernsey
fields.Info:
• A Crown dependency and the second-largest of the Channel Islands, in the English Channel off the coast of Normandy
  • It includes Alderney, Sark, Herm, and other small islands

fields.Name: Isle of Man
fields.Info:
• A self-governing Crown dependency in the Irish Sea between Great Britain and Ireland
  • Its highest point is Snaefell; the Isle of Man TT motorcycle races and its tailless cats are known
fields.Photo caption: Douglas and the south of the island from the air

fields.Name: Jersey
fields.Info:
• A Crown dependency and the largest of the Channel Islands, in the English Channel about 22 km from the coast of Normandy
  • It has a large tidal range and sheltered harbours; St Helier is its capital
fields.Photo caption: Fields in Saint Clement from the air

fields.Name: Kiribati
fields.Flag Symbolism: A frigatebird flies over a rising sun and ocean waves, evoking the nation's scattered Pacific atolls.
fields.Info:
• A Pacific nation of 33 coral atolls straddling the equator and the International Date Line, including Banaba, Tarawa, and Kiritimati
  • Highly threatened by sea-level rise

fields.Name: Macau
fields.Info:
• A special administrative region of China on the western side of the Pearl River estuary, made up of a peninsula and the islands of Taipa and Coloane
  • It is one of the most densely populated places on Earth, with casinos on the Cotai Strip

fields.Name: Madeira
fields.Info:
• A Portuguese archipelago in the Atlantic west of Morocco, consisting of Madeira, Porto Santo, and uninhabited islets
  • The main island's capital is Funchal; the islands are mountainous, with laurel forests and levada irrigation channels
fields.Waters: North Atlantic Ocean

fields.Name: Marshall Islands
fields.Info:
• A Pacific nation of 29 atolls and five islands in two chains, the Ratak and the Ralik; Majuro is the capital
  • The US tested nuclear bombs at Bikini and Enewetak atolls

fields.Name: Nauru
fields.Capital Info: No official capital; the Yaren District is the de facto capital.
fields.Info:
• The world's smallest republic and third-smallest country, a single raised coral island in Micronesia
  • Phosphate mining stripped its interior, so the population lives on a narrow coastal belt

fields.Name: New Caledonia
fields.Info:
• A French sui generis collectivity in the southwest Pacific, about 1,200 km east of Australia, whose main island, Grande Terre, is ringed by the world's second-largest barrier reef
  • It has the Loyalty Islands to the east and the Isle of Pines to the south, and a large nickel industry
fields.Photo caption: Red laterite hills in the south of Grande Terre

fields.Name: Niue
fields.Info:
• A single raised coral island, one of the world's largest, with steep limestone cliffs and no rivers
  • Called the “Rock of Polynesia”; it is in free association with New Zealand
fields.Photo caption: A stone arch at the Limu Pools

fields.Name: Northern Cyprus
fields.Info:
• A de facto state occupying the northern third of Cyprus, east of the Green Line, with the Kyrenia Mountains along the north coast
  • Recognized only by Turkey; Nicosia (Lefkoşa) is divided by the Green Line

fields.Name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
fields.Info:
• The smallest sovereign state in the Americas by area and population, two volcanic islands separated by a 3 km channel called The Narrows
  • Mount Liamuiga on St Kitts is its highest peak; Brimstone Hill Fortress is a UNESCO site
fields.Photo caption: Nevis, seen from Saint Kitts's southeastern peninsula

fields.Name: Samoa
fields.Info:
• Two main volcanic islands, Upolu and Savai'i, in the central South Pacific, with coral reefs and lava fields
  • It moved across the International Date Line in 2011, to be on the same side as New Zealand and Australia
fields.Photo caption: The To Sua Ocean Trench, Upolu

fields.Name: Somaliland
fields.Info:
• A self-declared state on the southern coast of the Gulf of Aden in northern Somalia
  • Hargeisa is its capital; Berbera on the Gulf of Aden is its port; recognized only by Israel (since 2025)

fields.Name: South Sudan
fields.Info:
• A landlocked country in the Nile Basin, holding the Sudd, one of the world's largest wetlands
  • Its capital Juba lies on the White Nile; the Imatong Mountains are its highest range
fields.Borders: Central African Republic, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Sudan, and Uganda

fields.Name: Tuvalu
fields.Info:
• The world's fourth-smallest country, a nine-island chain of atolls in the Pacific, highly threatened by sea-level rise
  • Its highest point is only about 4.6 metres; its internet domain, .tv, is a major source of revenue
fields.Photo caption: A jetty and beach at Funafuti atoll

fields.Name: United States Virgin Islands
fields.Info:
• An unincorporated US territory in the Caribbean, of St Thomas, St John, and St Croix, and many small islets, east of Puerto Rico
  • Virgin Islands National Park covers much of St John; Crown Mountain on St Thomas is its highest point

fields.Name: Åland Islands
fields.Info:
• A demilitarized, autonomous Swedish-speaking archipelago of over 6,000 islands in the Baltic, between Sweden and Finland
  • Belongs to Finland; its main island is Fasta Åland, with the capital Mariehamn

fields.Name: South Ossetia
fields.Info:
• A breakaway region on the southern slopes of the Greater Caucasus in northern Georgia, bordering Russia's North Ossetia at the Roki Tunnel
  • Its capital is Tskhinvali; since 2017 it has styled itself the Republic of South Ossetia–State of Alania and is recognized by only a few states

fields.Name: American Samoa
fields.Info:
• A US territory in the South Pacific of five volcanic islands and two coral atolls, east of Samoa
  • The main island Tutuila has Pago Pago Harbor, one of the deepest natural harbours in the Pacific

fields.Name: Northern Mariana Islands
fields.Info:
• A US commonwealth of 14 islands in the western Pacific, north of Guam, in the Mariana Islands chain
  • Saipan is the largest island; Tinian and Rota are the other main ones, and the Mariana Trench lies to the east
fields.Photo caption: Our Lady of Mount Carmel Cathedral, Chalan Kanoa
fields.Waters: Philippine Sea and Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Aruba
fields.Info:
• A constituent country of the Netherlands in the southern Caribbean, about 29 km north of Venezuela, one of the ABC Islands
  • It is arid, with cacti and divi-divi trees, and it lies outside the hurricane belt

fields.Name: Abkhazia
fields.Info:
• A breakaway region on the Black Sea coast of northwestern Georgia, between the Caucasus Mountains and the sea, bordering Russia at the Psou River
  • Sukhumi is its capital; Lake Ritsa and the New Athos cave are in it

fields.Name: Sint Maarten
fields.Info:
• A constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, on the southern half of the island of Saint Martin in the northeastern Caribbean
  • Its Princess Juliana airport is famous for planes flying low over Maho Beach

fields.Name: Tonga
fields.Info:
• An archipelago of about 170 islands in the South Pacific in three main groups, Tongatapu, Ha'apai, and Vava'u
  • Known for the giant Ha'amonga 'a Maui trilithon and for the 2022 Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai volcanic eruption

fields.Name: Transnistria
fields.Info:
• A breakaway strip of Moldova on the east bank of the Dniester River, along the border with Ukraine, about 200 km long and narrow
  • It is not recognized by any UN member; Tiraspol is its main city

fields.Name: Sardinia
fields.Info:
• The second-largest island in the Mediterranean, west of the Italian mainland, separated from Corsica by the Strait of Bonifacio
  • Its nuraghi, Bronze Age stone towers, dot the island; Cagliari is its capital
fields.Waters: Tyrrhenian Sea and Mediterranean Sea

fields.Name: Kaliningrad Oblast
fields.Info:
• A Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea between Poland and Lithuania, with no land border with the rest of Russia
  • Its Curonian Spit and Vistula Lagoon lie on the coast; the city was Königsberg until 1946

fields.Name: Martinique
fields.Info:
• A French overseas region, an island in the eastern Caribbean in the Windward Islands, dominated by the volcano Mont Pelée
  • Its 1902 eruption destroyed the town of Saint-Pierre; Fort-de-France is its capital

fields.Name: Java
fields.Info:
• The most populous island in the world, with the Indonesian capital Jakarta on its northwest coast
  • A chain of volcanoes runs along its length, including Merapi and Bromo; the Borobudur temple stands near Yogyakarta
fields.Waters: Java Sea and Indian Ocean

fields.Name: Corsica
fields.Info:
• A mountainous French island in the Mediterranean north of Sardinia, with Monte Cinto its highest peak
  • Its capital Ajaccio was the birthplace of Napoleon Bonaparte; the Strait of Bonifacio separates it from Sardinia
fields.Waters: Ligurian Sea, Tyrrhenian Sea, and Mediterranean Sea

fields.Name: European Union
fields.Info:
• A political and economic union of 27 European countries, from Ireland to Cyprus and from Finland to Malta, with the Schengen Area and common market
  • Its seats include Brussels, Luxembourg, and Strasbourg; its territory spans the Atlantic to the Black Sea

fields.Name: Gulf of Thailand
fields.Info:
• A shallow inlet of the South China Sea bordered by Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, and Malaysia
  • The Chao Phraya River enters it at Bangkok; the Kra Isthmus separates it from the Andaman Sea

fields.Name: Micronesia
fields.Info:
• A subregion of Oceania in the western Pacific, made up of thousands of small islands north of the equator, including Palau, the Marshall Islands, Guam, and Kiribati
  • Its islands are mostly coral atolls, with high volcanic islands like Pohnpei and Guam

fields.Name: Denmark Strait
fields.Info:
• A strait between Iceland and Greenland linking the Greenland Sea and Atlantic, about 480 km long
  • Beneath it is the world's largest waterfall by height, a submarine cataract where cold water plunges south

fields.Name: Balkan Peninsula
fields.Parent: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Slovenia, and Turkey
fields.Info:
• A large peninsula in southeastern Europe, bounded by the Adriatic, Ionian, Aegean, Sea of Marmara, and Black seas
  • Its northern boundary is usually taken as the Sava and Danube rivers; it includes Greece, Bulgaria, and the former Yugoslavia
fields.Photo caption: The southern Balkan Peninsula and the Aegean from orbit
fields.Waters: Adriatic Sea, Ionian Sea, Aegean Sea, Sea of Marmara, and Black Sea

fields.Name: Bering Strait
fields.Info:
• A narrow strait between the Chukchi Peninsula of Russia and the Seward Peninsula of Alaska, about 82 km wide, joining the Pacific and Arctic oceans
  • The Diomede Islands lie in it, and the International Date Line passes between them
fields.Photo caption: Little Diomede Island, Alaska, in the Bering Strait

fields.Name: Dead Sea
fields.Info:
• A salt lake on the border of Jordan, Israel, and the West Bank, in the Jordan Rift Valley
  • Its shore is the lowest point on land, about 430 m below sea level; it is about ten times saltier than the ocean, so swimmers float
fields.Photo caption: Salt on the Dead Sea shore

fields.Name: Sea of Japan
fields.Parent: Russia, Japan, South Korea, and North Korea
fields.Info:
• A marginal sea of the western Pacific between Japan, Russia, and the Korean Peninsula
  • It is called the East Sea in Korea; the Tsushima, Tsugaru, La Pérouse, and Tatar straits connect it
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Russia, North Korea, South Korea, and 1 more

fields.Name: Aral Sea
fields.Info:
• A once-large lake between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan that has shrunk drastically since the 1960s because Soviet irrigation diverted the Amu Darya and Syr Darya
  • It has split into a small northern Aral Sea (Kazakhstan) and a nearly dry southern basin; Moynaq was a port on it
fields.Photo caption: Stranded ships at Moynaq, on the former shore

fields.Name: Gulf of California
fields.Info:
• An inlet of the Pacific between the Baja California peninsula and mainland Mexico, also called the Sea of Cortés
  • It is a young rift; the Colorado River enters at its head; La Paz and Guaymas lie on it

fields.Name: Polynesia
fields.Parent: United States, France, Chile, New Zealand, Tuvalu, Tonga, and Samoa
fields.Info:
• A subregion of Oceania forming a triangle between Hawaii, New Zealand, and Easter Island, with thousands of islands in the central and southern Pacific
  • It includes Samoa, Tonga, Tahiti, and the Cook Islands; the Polynesian people share related languages
fields.Photo caption: Moai at Ahu Tongariki, Easter Island
fields.Locator: ##Countries::United States, France, Chile, New Zealand, Tuvalu, and 2 more

fields.Name: Melanesia
fields.Parent: France, Indonesia, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Papua New Guinea, and Fiji
fields.Info:
• A subregion of Oceania in the southwestern Pacific, northeast of Australia, including New Guinea, the Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Fiji, and New Caledonia
  • Its name means “black islands”; the islands are largely volcanic and rich in minerals
fields.Locator: ##Countries::France, Indonesia, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Papua New Guinea, and Fiji

fields.Name: Scandinavia
fields.Info:
• A region of northern Europe including Norway, Sweden, and Denmark, and often Finland and Iceland, defined by shared languages and cultures
  • The Scandinavian Peninsula, with the Scandinavian Mountains, forms its core

fields.Name: Sea of Galilee
fields.Info:
• A freshwater lake in northern Israel, the lowest freshwater lake on Earth, in the Jordan Rift Valley
  • The Jordan River flows through it; Tiberias lies on its western shore, and it is also called Lake Tiberias or Kinneret

fields.Name: Sumatra
fields.Info:
• The sixth-largest island in the world, in western Indonesia, crossed by the equator and the Barisan Mountains along its west coast
  • Lake Toba, a huge volcanic caldera lake, lies in the north; the Strait of Malacca separates it from the Malay Peninsula
fields.Waters: South China Sea, Java Sea, Indian Ocean, Bay of Bengal, Andaman Sea, and Strait of Malacca

fields.Name: Sicily
fields.Info:
• The largest island in the Mediterranean, separated from mainland Italy by the narrow Strait of Messina
  • Mount Etna, Europe's highest active volcano, rises on its east coast; Palermo is its capital
fields.Waters: Tyrrhenian Sea, Ionian Sea, and Strait of Sicily

fields.Name: Mayotte
fields.Info:
• A French overseas department in the Comoros archipelago in the Mozambique Channel, between Madagascar and Africa
  • It consists of Grande-Terre and Petite-Terre, ringed by a coral reef and lagoon
fields.Photo caption: Lake Dziani, a volcanic crater lake on Petite-Terre

fields.Name: Réunion
fields.Info:
• A French overseas department, a volcanic island in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar, in the Mascarene Islands
  • Piton de la Fournaise, one of the world's most active volcanoes, and Piton des Neiges, its highest point, rise on the island
fields.Photo caption: Shri Maha Kalikambal Temple in Saint-Denis, Réunion

fields.Name: Falkland Islands
fields.Info:
• A British territory in the South Atlantic, about 480 km east of Patagonia, made up of East Falkland and West Falkland and hundreds of small islands
  • Its sheep farming and wildlife, including penguins, are notable; Argentina claims them as the Islas Malvinas

fields.Name: Europe
fields.Info:
• Covers the western fifth of the Eurasian landmass, bordered by the Arctic Ocean, the Atlantic, the Mediterranean and (by convention) the Ural Mountains
  • The second-smallest continent by area; its highest peak is Mount Elbrus in the Caucasus

fields.Name: North America
fields.Info:
