• The northern continent of the Western Hemisphere, bounded by the Arctic, Atlantic, and Pacific oceans, and linked to South America by the Isthmus of Panama
  • It includes Canada, the US, Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean; Denali is its highest peak and Greenland its largest island

fields.Name: South America
fields.Info:
• The southern continent of the Western Hemisphere, between the Pacific and the Atlantic, containing the Andes, the Amazon Basin, and Patagonia
  • Its highest peak is Aconcagua; it has the Amazon River and the Atacama Desert
fields.Photo caption: Gran Roque, Los Roques Archipelago, Venezuela

fields.Name: Asia
fields.Info:
• The largest and most populous continent, covering the eastern four-fifths of Eurasia, from the Arctic to the tropical Indian Ocean
  • It contains the Himalayas with Mount Everest, the Tibetan Plateau, Siberia, and the world's largest peninsulas

fields.Name: Africa
fields.Info:
• The second-largest continent, split by the equator, with the Sahara in the north, the Rift Valley in the east and the Congo Basin in the centre
  • Its highest peak is Kilimanjaro; the Nile is its longest river; it is joined to Asia by the Isthmus of Suez
fields.Photo caption: Aksum Obelisk, symbol of the Aksumite civilization

fields.Name: Oceania
fields.Info:
• The region of the central and southern Pacific, including Australia, New Zealand, and the islands of Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia
  • Australia is the largest landmass; the definition of the continent varies, and it is sometimes called Australasia

fields.Name: Antarctica
fields.Info:
• The southernmost continent, centred on the South Pole and almost entirely covered by an ice sheet, surrounded by the Southern Ocean
  • The Transantarctic Mountains divide East and West Antarctica; Vinson Massif is its highest peak and the Antarctic Treaty governs it
fields.Photo caption: An aerial view of McMurdo Station, the largest research station in Antarctica

fields.Name: Saint Martin
fields.Info:
• The northern half of the island of Saint Martin in the northeastern Caribbean, a French collectivity, sharing the island with Sint Maarten
  • It is separated from Anguilla by the Anguilla Channel

fields.Name: Wallis and Futuna
fields.Info:
• A French territory in the South Pacific, made up of the Wallis Islands and the Futuna and Alofi islands, about 240 km apart
  • It lies between Fiji and Samoa

fields.Name: Akrotiri and Dhekelia
fields.Info:
• Two British Sovereign Base Areas on the island of Cyprus: Akrotiri on the southwest coast and Dhekelia on the southeast, surrounding the Cyprus village of Pyla
  • They contain military bases retained when Cyprus became independent
fields.Photo caption: Episkopi Bay on the west coast of Akrotiri

fields.Name: Svalbard
fields.Info:
• A Norwegian archipelago in the Arctic Ocean between mainland Norway and the North Pole, the largest island being Spitsbergen
  • Longyearbyen is its main settlement; the Global Seed Vault is on Spitsbergen, and polar bears roam it

fields.Name: Bougainville
fields.Info:
• An autonomous region of Papua New Guinea, the northernmost of the Solomon Islands chain, made up of Bougainville and Buka islands
  • Mount Balbi is an active volcano; the Panguna copper mine was a key cause of its conflict

fields.Name: Jeju
fields.Info:
• A volcanic island off the southern coast of South Korea in the Korea Strait, with Hallasan, South Korea's highest peak, at its centre
  • Known for lava tubes, waterfalls, and its haenyeo women divers
fields.Photo caption: Hallasan and its crater lake, Jeju
fields.Waters: Yellow Sea, East China Sea, and Korea Strait

fields.Name: Andes
fields.Parent: Chile, Argentina, Peru, Venezuela, Ecuador, Colombia, and Bolivia
fields.Info:
• The longest continental mountain range in the world, running along the western edge of South America from Venezuela to Tierra del Fuego
  • It includes Aconcagua, the highest peak outside Asia, and the Altiplano plateau; it results from the subduction of the Nazca Plate
fields.Photo caption: The southern, Patagonian part from orbit
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Chile, Argentina, Peru, Venezuela, Ecuador, and 2 more

fields.Name: Himalayas
fields.Parent: China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Bhutan
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain range on Earth, between the Indian subcontinent and the Tibetan Plateau, containing Mount Everest and most of the world's 8,000-metre peaks
  • Formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates; it is the source of the Indus, Ganges, and Brahmaputra rivers
fields.Photo caption: The Himalayas from the International Space Station
fields.Locator: ##Countries::China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, and 2 more

fields.Name: Alps
fields.Parent: France, Switzerland, Italy, Monaco, Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany, and Slovenia
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain range entirely in Europe, arcing through France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria, and Slovenia
  • Mont Blanc is its highest peak; the Matterhorn, Eiger, and Jungfrau are famous, and it is the source of the Rhine, Rhône, and Po
fields.Locator: ##Countries::France, Switzerland, Italy, Monaco, Liechtenstein, and 3 more

fields.Name: Rocky Mountains
fields.Info:
• A major mountain range of western North America stretching from British Columbia to New Mexico, whose crest forms the Continental Divide
  • Mount Elbert in Colorado is its highest peak; Yellowstone and Banff are national parks in it
fields.Photo caption: Valley of the Ten Peaks and Moraine Lake, Banff National Park, Canada

fields.Name: Appalachian Mountains
fields.Info:
• An old, eroded mountain range in eastern North America, from Newfoundland to Alabama, running roughly parallel to the Atlantic coast
  • The Appalachian Trail follows it; Mount Mitchell in North Carolina is its highest peak
fields.Photo caption: Looking southwest from Mount Mitchell, North Carolina

fields.Name: Ural Mountains
fields.Info:
• A mountain range in Russia and Kazakhstan running north–south, traditionally the boundary between Europe and Asia
  • Its highest peak is Mount Narodnaya; it is rich in minerals, and Yekaterinburg lies on its eastern slope

fields.Name: Atlas Mountains
fields.Info:
• A mountain range across northwestern Africa, in Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia, separating the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts from the Sahara
  • Its highest peak is Toubkal in Morocco's High Atlas; the Berber peoples live in the range

fields.Name: Caucasus Mountains
fields.Info:
• A mountain range between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea, regarded as part of the boundary between Europe and Asia
  • Its Greater Caucasus includes Mount Elbrus; the Lesser Caucasus lies to the south in Georgia and Armenia

fields.Name: Carpathian Mountains
fields.Parent: Hungary, Poland, Austria, Ukraine, Czech Republic, Slovakia, and Romania
fields.Info:
• A crescent-shaped range of Central and Eastern Europe, over 1,500 km long, through Slovakia, Poland, Ukraine, and Romania
  • Its Tatra Mountains and Transylvanian Alps are the highest sections; the Danube cuts through it at the Iron Gates
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Hungary, Poland, Austria, Ukraine, Czech Republic, and 2 more

fields.Name: Pyrenees
fields.Info:
• A mountain range on the border between France and Spain, running from the Bay of Biscay to the Mediterranean, with Andorra in its middle
  • Aneto in Spain is its highest peak; the Roncesvalles Pass is one of its famous passes

fields.Name: Great Dividing Range
fields.Info:
• The longest mountain range in Australia, running down the eastern coast from Queensland to Victoria
  • It separates coastal rivers from those flowing inland toward the Murray–Darling Basin; Mount Kosciuszko in its Snowy Mountains is the highest point on the mainland
fields.Photo caption: The Three Sisters, Blue Mountains, New South Wales
fields.Locator: Region::Queensland, New South Wales, and Victoria##Country::Australia|Region::Queensland, New South Wales, and Victoria

fields.Name: Sierra Nevada
fields.Info:
• A mountain range in California, running along the eastern side of the state, with Mount Whitney the highest peak in the contiguous US
  • Yosemite Valley and Lake Tahoe are in the range; its eastern edge is a huge fault-block escarpment
fields.Photo caption: Satellite view: tule fog fills the Central Valley, and the snow-covered range runs along its east side

fields.Name: Apennine Mountains
fields.Info:
• The mountain range running down the length of the Italian Peninsula, from Liguria to Calabria and Sicily
  • Its highest peak is Corno Grande in the Gran Sasso massif; it divides the Adriatic and Tyrrhenian watersheds

fields.Name: Zagros Mountains
fields.Info:
• A long mountain range in Iran, Iraq, and Turkey, running northwest to southeast along the western side of the Iranian plateau
  • It was formed by the collision of the Arabian and Eurasian plates; its oil-rich foothills flank the Persian Gulf and its highest peak is Mount Dena

fields.Name: Hindu Kush
fields.Info:
• A mountain range stretching through Afghanistan and Pakistan, west of the Karakoram and connected to the Pamirs
  • Its highest peak is Tirich Mir in Pakistan; the Khyber and Salang passes cross it

fields.Name: Tian Shan
fields.Info:
• A large mountain system in Central Asia, in Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and China's Xinjiang, north of the Tarim Basin and the Taklamakan Desert
  • Its highest peak is Jengish Chokusu (Victory Peak); Issyk-Kul lies within it
fields.Locator: Region::Xinjiang, Chuy, and Osh##Countries::China, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan|Region::Xinjiang, Chuy, and Osh

fields.Name: Altai Mountains
fields.Info:
• A mountain range in Central and East Asia where Russia, Kazakhstan, China, and Mongolia meet
  • Its highest peak is Belukha; it is a source of the Irtysh and Ob rivers
fields.Photo caption: Belukha, the highest peak of the Altai

fields.Name: Drakensberg
fields.Info:
• The eastern escarpment of the South African plateau, running along the border with Lesotho and through KwaZulu-Natal
  • Its highest peak is Thabana Ntlenyana in Lesotho; Mafadi is South Africa's highest; the Amphitheatre is a famous cliff

fields.Name: Scandinavian Mountains
fields.Info:
• A mountain range running through the Scandinavian Peninsula, along the border of Norway and Sweden, and reaching north to Finland
  • Galdhøpiggen in Norway is its highest peak; its western side plunges to the fjords

fields.Name: Balkan Mountains
fields.Info:
• A mountain range running across Bulgaria from Serbia to the Black Sea, also called the Stara Planina
  • Botev Peak is its highest; the Shipka Pass crosses it
fields.Photo caption: The main ridge in Central Balkan National Park, Bulgaria

fields.Name: Cascade Range
fields.Info:
• A volcanic mountain range of the Pacific Northwest from British Columbia to northern California, part of the Ring of Fire
  • Its peaks include Mount Rainier, Mount Hood, and Mount St. Helens; it causes a rain shadow east of it
fields.Photo caption: Peaks above the clouds, with Mount Rainier in the foreground
fields.Locator: Region::British Columbia, Washington, Oregon, and California##Countries::Canada and United States|Region::British Columbia, Washington, Oregon, and California

fields.Name: Brooks Range
fields.Info:
• A mountain range in northern Alaska, extending into Yukon, above the Arctic Circle, separating the North Slope from the interior
  • Its highest peak is Mount Isto; the Gates of the Arctic National Park protects part of it
fields.Photo caption: The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge coastal plain, looking south to the range
fields.Locator: Region::Alaska and Yukon##Countries::United States and Canada|Region::Alaska and Yukon

fields.Name: Karakoram
fields.Info:
• A mountain range on the border of Pakistan, China, and India, with K2 the second-highest peak on Earth
  • It has some of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions, including the Baltoro and Siachen glaciers

fields.Name: Kunlun Mountains
fields.Info:
• A mountain range in western China, north of the Tibetan Plateau, and south of the Tarim Basin
  • Its highest peak is Kunlun Goddess (Liushi Shan); Chinese mythology treats it as a home of immortals
fields.Photo caption: Snow peaks above a river valley in the range
fields.Locator: Region::Qinghai, Xinjiang, and Tibet##Country::China|Region::Qinghai, Xinjiang, and Tibet

fields.Name: Ethiopian Highlands
fields.Info:
• A rugged mountain mass in Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Somalia, the largest continuous area of elevation above 1,500 m in Africa
  • The Blue Nile rises here at Lake Tana; Ras Dashen is its highest peak, in the Simien Mountains
fields.Photo caption: Landscape at Wunenia near Gondar, Ethiopia

fields.Name: Serra do Mar
fields.Info:
• A coastal mountain range along the Atlantic coast of southeastern Brazil, from Espírito Santo to Santa Catarina
  • It forms a steep escarpment above São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro; Pico Paraná is its highest point
fields.Locator: Region::Santa Catarina, Paraná, São Paulo, and Rio Grande do Sul##Country::Brazil|Region::Santa Catarina, Paraná, São Paulo, and Rio Grande do Sul

fields.Name: Southern Alps
fields.Info:
• The mountain range running the length of New Zealand's South Island, with Aoraki (Mount Cook) as its highest peak
  • The Fox and Franz Josef glaciers descend from it, and the Alpine Fault runs along its western edge
fields.Photo caption: The Southern Alps from the air

fields.Name: Mount Everest
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain on Earth above sea level, in the Mahalangur Himalayas on the border of Nepal and Tibet (China)
  • Its Tibetan name is Chomolungma and its Nepali name Sagarmatha; the Khumbu Icefall and the South Col are on the standard Nepalese route
  • Lhotse lies just south, joined to it by the South Col, and Makalu 19 km to the southeast
fields.Photo caption: Looking north to the peak from an aircraft over Bhutan
fields.Locator: Region::Koshi Province and Tibet##Countries::Nepal and China|Region::Koshi Province and Tibet

fields.Name: K2
fields.Info:
• The second-highest mountain on Earth, in the Karakoram on the Pakistan–China border; also called Mount Godwin-Austen or Chogori
  • Its Baltoro Glacier is one of the longest outside the polar regions; it is known for being harder to climb than Everest
fields.Photo caption: K2, in the Karakoram on the Pakistan–China border
fields.Locator: Region::Xinjiang and Gilgit-Baltistan##Countries::Pakistan and China|Region::Xinjiang and Gilgit-Baltistan

fields.Name: Kangchenjunga
fields.Info:
• The third-highest mountain on Earth, on the Nepal–Sikkim (India) border in the eastern Himalayas
  • Its name means “five treasures of the snow”, for its five summits
fields.Locator: Region::Koshi Province and Sikkim##Countries::Nepal and India|Region::Koshi Province and Sikkim

fields.Name: Denali
fields.Info:
• The highest peak in North America, in the Alaska Range, and the centrepiece of Denali National Park
  • Formerly called Mount McKinley; its name is Koyukon Athabaskan for “the high one”

fields.Name: Aconcagua
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain outside Asia and in the Southern Hemisphere, in the Andes of Mendoza Province, Argentina, near the Chilean border
  • One of the Seven Summits; the Polish Glacier and the Horcones Valley are among its climbing routes
fields.Photo caption: The peak from a flight between Buenos Aires and Santiago

fields.Name: Mount Elbrus
fields.Info:
• The highest peak in Europe by most definitions, a dormant volcano in the western Caucasus of southern Russia
  • It has two summits; one of the Seven Summits, it lies north of the Georgian border
fields.Locator: Region::Karachay-Cherkess Republic and Kabardino-Balkaria##Country::Russia|Region::Karachay-Cherkess Republic and Kabardino-Balkaria

fields.Name: Puncak Jaya
fields.Info:
• The highest peak in Oceania, in the Sudirman Range of the Indonesian province of Papua on the island of New Guinea
  • Also called Carstensz Pyramid; one of the Seven Summits in some lists, and one of the few equatorial glaciated peaks
fields.Photo caption: The Carstensz peaks, including Puncak Jaya, in the Sudirman Range

fields.Name: Mont Blanc
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain in the Alps and in Western Europe, on the border of France and Italy
  • The Mont Blanc Tunnel beneath it links Chamonix and Courmayeur; its summit ownership is disputed between the two countries
fields.Locator: Region::Haute-Savoie and Aosta Valley##Countries::France and Italy|Region::Haute-Savoie and Aosta Valley

fields.Name: Matterhorn
fields.Info:
• A pyramid-shaped peak in the Pennine Alps on the Swiss–Italian border, above Zermatt
  • Its Italian name is Monte Cervino; its four faces face the compass points, and it is one of the best-known Alpine peaks
fields.Locator: Region::Valais and Aosta Valley##Countries::Switzerland and Italy|Region::Valais and Aosta Valley

fields.Name: Mount Fuji
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain in Japan, an active stratovolcano on Honshu, near Tokyo
  • Its nearly symmetric cone appears in Katsushika Hokusai's Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji; the Fuji Five Lakes lie at its base
fields.Locator: Region::Shizuoka Prefecture and Yamanashi Prefecture##Country::Japan|Region::Shizuoka Prefecture and Yamanashi Prefecture

fields.Name: Mount Kenya
fields.Info:
• The second-highest mountain in Africa, an extinct volcano straddling the equator in central Kenya
  • It has glaciers despite its location on the equator; its peaks include Batian, Nelion, and Lenana
fields.Locator: Region::Nyeri, Kirinyaga, and Meru counties##Region::Nyeri, Kirinyaga, and Meru counties

fields.Name: Mount Ararat
fields.Info:
• The highest peak in Turkey, a dormant volcano in the far east of the country near the borders with Armenia and Iran
  • Traditionally identified as the landing place of Noah's Ark; it consists of Greater and Lesser Ararat

fields.Name: Mount Olympus
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain in Greece, near the Gulf of Thermaikos in Thessaly and Macedonia
  • In Greek mythology it was the home of the twelve Olympian gods; its highest peak is Mytikas
fields.Locator: Region::Central Macedonia and Thessaly##Country::Greece|Region::Central Macedonia and Thessaly

fields.Name: Mount Etna
fields.Info:
• The largest and one of the most active volcanoes in Europe, on the east coast of Sicily near Catania
  • Its height changes with eruptions; it is a stratovolcano and a UNESCO site

fields.Name: Mount Vesuvius
fields.Info:
• A stratovolcano on the Bay of Naples in Campania, southern Italy, which overlooks Naples and Pompeii
  • Its eruption in 79 CE buried Pompeii and Herculaneum; it is the only active volcano on mainland Europe and is on the rim of the older Monte Somma caldera

fields.Name: Mount St. Helens
fields.Info:
• An active stratovolcano in the Cascade Range in Washington State, in the Pacific Northwest of the United States
  • Its 1980 eruption removed the top of the mountain, leaving a horseshoe-shaped crater and the Spirit Lake area

fields.Name: Krakatoa
fields.Info:
• A volcanic island in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra in Indonesia
  • Its 1883 eruption was one of the most violent in recorded history and destroyed most of the island; Anak Krakatau (“child of Krakatoa”) has grown in its caldera since 1927
fields.Photo caption: The volcanic island seen from the sea

fields.Name: Mount Rainier
fields.Info:
• The highest peak in the Cascade Range and in Washington State, a glacier-clad stratovolcano south of Seattle
  • It has the largest glacier system in the contiguous US; Mount Rainier National Park surrounds it
fields.Photo caption: The summit, Columbia Crest, at centre

fields.Name: Popocatépetl
fields.Info:
• An active stratovolcano in central Mexico, southeast of Mexico City, in the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt
  • Its name is Nahuatl for “smoking mountain”; it stands beside the dormant Iztaccíhuatl (“white woman”)
fields.Photo caption: The north side from Paso de Cortés
fields.Locator: Region::State of Mexico and Puebla##Country::Mexico|Region::State of Mexico and Puebla

fields.Name: Cotopaxi
fields.Info:
• One of the highest active volcanoes in the world, in the Andes of Ecuador south of Quito
  • It has a nearly symmetrical, glacier-capped cone; it is part of the Avenue of Volcanoes

fields.Name: Chimborazo
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain in Ecuador and an extinct stratovolcano in the Andes
  • Because of Earth's equatorial bulge, its summit is the farthest point on the surface from the Earth's centre, though not the highest above sea level
fields.Photo caption: Rising above the city of Riobamba

fields.Name: Mount Kosciuszko
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain on mainland Australia, in the Snowy Mountains of the Great Dividing Range in New South Wales
  • Named for the Polish general Tadeusz Kościuszko by the explorer Paweł Strzelecki in 1840

fields.Name: Table Mountain
fields.Info:
• A flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town in South Africa, edged by Devil's Peak and Lion's Head
  • It is covered by a cloud called the “tablecloth” when southeasterly winds blow; it is part of Table Mountain National Park

fields.Name: Mount Sinai
fields.Info:
• A mountain in the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt, in the south near Saint Catherine's Monastery
  • Traditionally identified as the biblical mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments; also called Jabal Musa

fields.Name: Mount Whitney
fields.Info:
• The highest summit in the contiguous United States, in the Sierra Nevada on the border of Inyo and Tulare counties, California
  • It lies about 135 km from Badwater Basin in Death Valley, the lowest point in North America

fields.Name: Eiger
fields.Info:
• A peak in the Bernese Alps of Switzerland above Grindelwald, next to the Mönch and the Jungfrau
  • Its north face, the Eigerwand, is one of the most famous climbing challenges in the Alps

fields.Name: Sahara
fields.Parent: Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan, Tunisia, and Western Sahara
fields.Info:
• The largest hot desert in the world, covering much of North Africa from the Atlantic to the Red Sea, about the size of the United States
  • It includes the Libyan Desert, the Tibesti and Ahaggar Mountains, and the Ténéré; the Nile is its only river to cross
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, and 6 more

fields.Name: Gobi Desert
fields.Info:
• A large cold desert of northern China and southern Mongolia, in the rain shadow of the Himalayas
  • Fossils of dinosaur eggs and Velociraptor were found here; the Silk Road crossed its edges
fields.Photo caption: Camels crossing the dunes of the Gobi

fields.Name: Kalahari Desert
fields.Parent: Botswana, South Africa, Angola, and Namibia
fields.Info:
• A semi-arid sandy savanna across Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa, in southern Africa
  • The Okavango Delta lies on its northern edge and the Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park in its south; it is home to the San people

fields.Name: Atacama Desert
fields.Info:
• A plateau along the Pacific coast of northern Chile, the driest non-polar desert on Earth
  • Parts have received no rain for decades; it holds the Valle de la Luna, the El Tatio geysers, and the ALMA observatory
fields.Photo caption: Valle de la Luna, near San Pedro de Atacama, Chile

fields.Name: Arabian Desert
fields.Parent: Iraq, Yemen, Jordan, Oman, Saudi Arabia, and United Arab Emirates
fields.Info:
• A vast desert covering most of the Arabian Peninsula, including the Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter), the largest sand desert
  • The Nafud and Dahna deserts are its other main parts
fields.Photo caption: Dunes of the Rub' al Khali
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Iraq, Yemen, Jordan, Oman, Saudi Arabia, and United Arab Emirates

fields.Name: Mojave Desert
fields.Info:
• A desert of southeastern California and parts of Nevada, Utah, and Arizona, between the Sierra Nevada and the Colorado River
  • Joshua Tree National Park and Death Valley National Park are in or beside it; Las Vegas lies in it

fields.Name: Sonoran Desert
fields.Info:
• A hot desert of the southwestern US and northwestern Mexico, covering Arizona, California, and Sonora
  • It is the home of the saguaro cactus; the Colorado River delta lies at its western edge
fields.Photo caption: Saguaro cacti in Agua Fria National Monument, Arizona
fields.Locator: Region::Sonora, Baja California, Arizona, and California##Countries::United States and Mexico|Region::Sonora, Baja California, Arizona, and California

fields.Name: Namib Desert
fields.Info:
• A coastal desert along the Atlantic coast of Namibia, one of the oldest deserts in the world
  • It contains the Sossusvlei dunes and the Skeleton Coast; fog from the Benguela Current provides most of its moisture
fields.Photo caption: The Namib coast seen from orbit

fields.Name: Thar Desert
fields.Info:
• A large arid region on the border of India and Pakistan, mostly in Rajasthan
  • It is also called the Great Indian Desert; Jaisalmer, Bikaner, and Jodhpur lie on its edges
fields.Locator: Region::Sindh, Punjab, Rajasthan, and Haryana##Countries::India and Pakistan|Region::Sindh, Punjab, Rajasthan, and Haryana

fields.Name: Great Victoria Desert
fields.Info:
• The largest desert in Australia, in Western Australia and South Australia, with sand dunes and salt lakes
  • Named for Queen Victoria; it was the site of British nuclear tests at Maralinga in the 1950s
fields.Photo caption: The desert and the Great Australian Bight from orbit
fields.Locator: Region::Western Australia and South Australia##Country::Australia|Region::Western Australia and South Australia

fields.Name: Taklamakan Desert
fields.Info:
• A desert in China's Xinjiang, in the Tarim Basin between the Tian Shan and the Kunlun Mountains
  • Its name is often translated “go in and you won't come out”; the Silk Road split around it

fields.Name: Chihuahuan Desert
fields.Info:
• The largest desert in North America, in northern Mexico and the southwestern US, including Texas's Big Bend and New Mexico
  • White Sands National Park lies in it; the Rio Grande flows along its edge
fields.Photo caption: The Chihuahuan Desert in Big Bend National Park, Texas

fields.Name: Karakum Desert
fields.Info:
• A desert covering about 70 percent of Turkmenistan, east of the Caspian Sea, with the Karakum Canal crossing it
  • The Darvaza gas crater, the “Gates of Hell”, lies in it
fields.Photo caption: Camels grazing in the Karakum, Turkmenistan

fields.Name: Simpson Desert
fields.Info:
• A desert in central Australia, in the Northern Territory, Queensland, and South Australia, with the world's longest parallel sand dunes
  • The Finke River basin and Lake Eyre lie nearby
fields.Photo caption: Parallel dunes of the Simpson Desert from orbit
fields.Locator: Region::Northern Territory, South Australia, and Queensland##Country::Australia|Region::Northern Territory, South Australia, and Queensland

fields.Name: Death Valley
fields.Info:
• A desert valley in eastern California near the Nevada border, the hottest and driest place in North America
  • Badwater Basin is the lowest point in North America, about 86 m below sea level

fields.Name: Niagara Falls
fields.Info:
• A group of three waterfalls on the Niagara River at the border between Ontario and New York, about 25 km north of Buffalo
  • The Horseshoe Falls (Canadian) is the largest of the three; the falls empty into a gorge that leads to Lake Ontario
fields.Photo caption: American Falls (left) and Horseshoe Falls (right), from the Skylon Tower
fields.Locator: Region::Ontario and New York##Countries::Canada and United States|Region::Ontario and New York

fields.Name: Victoria Falls
fields.Info:
• A large waterfall on the Zambezi River on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe, one of the largest curtains of falling water in the world
  • Its local name is Mosi-oa-Tunya, “the smoke that thunders”; a bridge crosses the gorge below the falls
fields.Photo caption: The falls on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border
fields.Locator: Region::Southern Province (Zambia) and Matabeleland North##Countries::Zambia and Zimbabwe|Region::Southern Province (Zambia) and Matabeleland North

fields.Name: Iguazu Falls
fields.Info:
• A group of about 275 waterfalls on the Iguazú River on the border between Argentina and Brazil
  • The Devil's Throat (Garganta del Diablo) is the largest; the river joins the Paraná just downstream, near the Paraguayan border
fields.Locator: Region::Misiones and Paraná##Countries::Argentina and Brazil|Region::Misiones and Paraná

fields.Name: Angel Falls
fields.Info:
• The world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, in Canaima National Park in southeastern Venezuela, dropping from the Auyán-tepui
  • It is named for the pilot Jimmie Angel; its Pemon name is Kerepakupai Merú
fields.Photo caption: The falls dropping from the tepui

fields.Name: Yosemite Falls
fields.Info:
• The highest waterfall in Yosemite National Park in California, in three sections: the Upper Fall, the middle cascades, and the Lower Fall
  • It is fed by snowmelt and usually runs dry in late summer
fields.Photo caption: Upper and Lower Falls in winter

fields.Name: Sutherland Falls
fields.Info:
• A waterfall in Fiordland National Park in New Zealand, one of the highest in the country, near Milford Sound
  • It is on the Milford Track and falls in three leaps from Lake Quill

fields.Name: Gullfoss
fields.Info:
• A waterfall on the Hvítá River in southwestern Iceland, a two-step cascade into a canyon
  • It is part of the Golden Circle route with Geysir and Þingvellir

fields.Name: Boyoma Falls
fields.Info:
• A series of seven cataracts on the Lualaba River (upper Congo) near Kisangani in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
  • Formerly known as Stanley Falls, after the explorer Henry Morton Stanley

fields.Name: Crete
fields.Info:
• The largest island of Greece, on the southern edge of the Aegean Sea, with mountain ranges including the White Mountains and Mount Ida
  • Home of the Minoan palace at Knossos; the Samaria Gorge is a famous hiking route
fields.Photo caption: Its mountainous spine, seen from orbit
fields.Waters: Sea of Crete and Mediterranean Sea

fields.Name: Tasmania
fields.Info:
• An island state of Australia, south of the mainland across the Bass Strait
  • Wild highlands and rainforest cover much of its west; its capital is Hobart, on the Derwent River beneath Mount Wellington
fields.Waters: Bass Strait, Tasman Sea, and Southern Ocean

fields.Name: Kyushu
fields.Info:
• The third-largest island of Japan, in the southwest, with many active volcanoes including Aso and Sakurajima
  • Its cities include Fukuoka and Nagasaki; it lies across the Kanmon Strait from Honshu
fields.Waters: East China Sea, Seto Inland Sea, and Philippine Sea

fields.Name: Shikoku
fields.Info:
• The smallest of Japan's four main islands, between Honshu and Kyushu on the Seto Inland Sea
  • Its 88-temple pilgrimage circuit is famous; the Great Seto Bridge and Akashi Kaikyō links connect it to Honshu
fields.Waters: Seto Inland Sea and Philippine Sea
fields.Locator: Region::Ehime Prefecture, Kōchi Prefecture, Tokushima Prefecture, and Kagawa Prefecture##Country::Japan|Region::Ehime Prefecture, Kōchi Prefecture, Tokushima Prefecture, and Kagawa Prefecture

fields.Name: Borneo
fields.Info:
• The third-largest island in the world, divided between Indonesia (Kalimantan), Malaysia (Sabah and Sarawak), and Brunei
  • Mount Kinabalu is its highest peak; it holds one of the oldest rainforests on Earth, home to orangutans
fields.Waters: Sulu Sea, Celebes Sea, Makassar Strait, Java Sea, and South China Sea

fields.Name: Sulawesi
fields.Info:
• An orchid-shaped island of Indonesia east of Borneo, across the Makassar Strait, with four peninsulas separated by gulfs
  • The Gulf of Boni and Gulf of Tomini are between its arms; Wallace's Line runs just west of it
fields.Waters: Celebes Sea, Molucca Sea, Banda Sea, Java Sea, and Makassar Strait

fields.Name: New Guinea
fields.Info:
• The second-largest island in the world, divided between Indonesia's western provinces and independent Papua New Guinea in the east
  • Its central highlands rise to Puncak Jaya; the Sepik and Fly rivers are the main rivers
fields.Photo caption: The island's rainforest canopy, seen from orbit
fields.Waters: Bismarck Sea, Solomon Sea, Gulf of Papua, Coral Sea, Torres Strait, Arafura Sea, and Ceram Sea

fields.Name: Hispaniola
fields.Info:
• The second-largest island in the Caribbean, shared by Haiti in the west and the Dominican Republic in the east
  • Pico Duarte is its highest peak; Lake Enriquillo is the Caribbean's largest lake
fields.Photo caption: The island from the International Space Station
fields.Waters: Atlantic Ocean and Caribbean Sea

fields.Name: Socotra
fields.Info:
• An island in the Arabian Sea off the Horn of Africa, belonging to Yemen, with many endemic plants such as the dragon's blood tree
  • It is part of the Socotra Archipelago, a UNESCO natural site
fields.Waters: Arabian Sea

fields.Name: Easter Island
fields.Flag Symbolism: A reimiro, a crescent-shaped pectoral ornament traditionally worn by Rapa Nui chiefs.
fields.Info:
• A remote volcanic island in the southeastern Pacific, about 3,500 km west of Chile, one of the most isolated inhabited places
  • Its moai statues stand along the coast; the Rano Kau crater has a freshwater lake
fields.Photo caption: An ahu, a platform of moai
fields.Waters: South Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Galápagos Islands
fields.Info:
• A volcanic archipelago in the Pacific about 1,000 km west of Ecuador, straddling the equator
  • Its unique species, such as giant tortoises and finches, inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection
fields.Photo caption: The volcanic islands seen from orbit
fields.Waters: Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Baffin Island
fields.Info:
• The largest island in Canada and fifth-largest in the world, in the Arctic Archipelago, mostly in Nunavut
  • It has glaciers, fjords, and mountains; Iqaluit, the capital of Nunavut, lies on its southeast coast
fields.Photo caption: Its icy coastline, seen from orbit
fields.Waters: Baffin Bay, Davis Strait, Hudson Strait, and Foxe Basin

fields.Name: Strait of Hormuz
fields.Parent: Iran, Oman, and United Arab Emirates
fields.Info:
• A narrow strait between Iran and Oman's Musandam peninsula, linking the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman
  • About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it; it is about 39 km wide at its narrowest

fields.Name: Strait of Malacca
fields.Info:
• A narrow strait between the Malay Peninsula and the Indonesian island of Sumatra, linking the Andaman Sea and the South China Sea
  • One of the busiest shipping lanes; it is only about 2.8 km wide at the Phillips Channel

fields.Name: Bosporus
fields.Info:
• A narrow strait through Istanbul, linking the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara and dividing European and Asian Turkey
  • The Bosphorus Bridge, Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge, and Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge span it
fields.Photo caption: The strait from the International Space Station

fields.Name: Dardanelles
fields.Info:
• A narrow strait in northwestern Turkey linking the Aegean Sea to the Sea of Marmara, separating the Gallipoli peninsula from Asia
  • About 61 km long, it was known as the Hellespont, where Leander swam and Xerxes bridged it
fields.Photo caption: The 1915 Çanakkale Bridge across the strait

fields.Name: Strait of Magellan
fields.Info:
• A navigable passage between the southern tip of mainland South America and Tierra del Fuego, linking the Atlantic and Pacific
  • It is named for Ferdinand Magellan, who sailed it in 1520; Punta Arenas lies on it
fields.Photo caption: Satellite image of the strait and Tierra del Fuego

fields.Name: Drake Passage
fields.Info:
• The stretch of sea between Cape Horn (Chile) and the South Shetland Islands of Antarctica, linking the Atlantic and Pacific
  • It is known for some of the roughest seas on Earth; it is named for Sir Francis Drake
fields.Photo caption: Cape Horn, at the passage's northern edge

fields.Name: Strait of Dover
fields.Info:
• The narrowest part of the English Channel, between Dover in England and Cap Gris-Nez in France, about 33 km wide
  • The Channel Tunnel and the world's busiest shipping lane pass through it
fields.Photo caption: The strait from the Space Shuttle, 2000

fields.Name: Bab-el-Mandeb
fields.Info:
• A strait between Yemen, Djibouti, and Eritrea, linking the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden
  • Its name means “gate of tears”; Perim Island lies in it; it is about 29 km wide

fields.Name: Iberian Peninsula
fields.Parent: Spain, Portugal, France, Andorra, and Gibraltar
fields.Info:
• A peninsula in southwestern Europe, separated from France by the Pyrenees, containing Spain and Portugal
  • It is bounded by the Atlantic and Mediterranean, and the Strait of Gibraltar separates it from Africa; the Meseta is its central plateau
fields.Waters: Balearic Sea, Mediterranean Sea, North Atlantic Ocean, and Bay of Biscay

fields.Name: Scandinavian Peninsula
fields.Info:
• The largest peninsula in Europe, containing Norway and Sweden and part of Finland
  • The Scandinavian Mountains run along its western side; the Gulf of Bothnia and the Baltic bound it on the east
fields.Waters: Norwegian Sea, Barents Sea, Gulf of Bothnia, Baltic Sea, Kattegat, Skagerrak, and North Sea

fields.Name: Arabian Peninsula
fields.Parent: Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, and Iraq
fields.Info:
• The world's largest peninsula, in Southwest Asia, bounded by the Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and the Persian Gulf
  • Its interior is mostly desert, including the Rub' al Khali; it holds a large share of the world's oil
fields.Waters: Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, Arabian Sea, Gulf of Aden, and Red Sea
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and 4 more

fields.Name: Anatolian Peninsula
fields.Info:
• The peninsula of western Asia forming most of Turkey, also called Asia Minor, bounded by the Black, Aegean, and Mediterranean seas
  • Its central plateau is ringed by the Pontic and Taurus mountains
fields.Photo caption: The Karacaören reservoir in the Taurus Mountains
fields.Waters: Mediterranean Sea, Aegean Sea, Sea of Marmara, and Black Sea

fields.Name: Korean Peninsula
fields.Info:
• A peninsula in East Asia between the Sea of Japan and the Yellow Sea, divided into North and South Korea
  • Mountainous in the east, with lower plains and a heavily indented coast in the west
fields.Waters: Sea of Japan, Korea Strait, and Yellow Sea

fields.Name: Yucatán Peninsula
fields.Info:
• A large limestone peninsula in southeastern Mexico, separating the Gulf of Mexico from the Caribbean Sea
  • It has no surface rivers but many cenotes (sinkholes); it was the heart of the Maya civilization
fields.Waters: Caribbean Sea, Bahía de Campeche, and Gulf of Mexico

fields.Name: Kamchatka Peninsula
fields.Info:
• A peninsula in the Russian Far East, between the Sea of Okhotsk and the Pacific Ocean, with one of the highest densities of volcanoes on Earth
  • Its highest peak is the active Klyuchevskaya Sopka; Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky is its main city
fields.Photo caption: Clouds along the east coast, seen from orbit
fields.Waters: Sea of Okhotsk

fields.Name: Jutland
fields.Info:
• A peninsula of northern Europe forming the mainland of Denmark and part of northern Germany, between the North Sea and the Baltic
  • Its northern tip, Skagen, divides the Skagerrak from the Kattegat; the Limfjord cuts across it
fields.Waters: Kattegat, North Sea, and Skagerrak
fields.Locator: Region::North Denmark, Central Denmark, Southern Denmark, and Schleswig-Holstein##Countries::Denmark and Germany|Region::North Denmark, Central Denmark, Southern Denmark, and Schleswig-Holstein

fields.Name: Crimea
fields.Info:
• A peninsula on the northern coast of the Black Sea, joined to Ukraine by the narrow Isthmus of Perekop, and to Russia by the Kerch Strait Bridge
  • Sevastopol is its main port; it borders the Sea of Azov and its southern coast has the Crimean Mountains
fields.Photo caption: Satellite image of the Crimean Peninsula
fields.Waters: Sea of Azov and Black Sea

fields.Name: Sinai Peninsula
fields.Info:
• A triangular peninsula in Egypt between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the land bridge between Africa and Asia
  • It is bounded by the Gulf of Suez and Gulf of Aqaba; Mount Sinai and Saint Catherine's Monastery lie in its south
fields.Waters: Mediterranean Sea, Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea, and Gulf of Suez

fields.Name: Kola Peninsula
fields.Info:
• A peninsula in northwestern Russia, mostly north of the Arctic Circle, between the Barents Sea and the White Sea
  • Murmansk lies on it; the Khibiny mountains are rich in minerals
fields.Photo caption: Snow patches across the peninsula, seen from orbit
fields.Waters: Barents Sea and White Sea

fields.Name: Sahel
fields.Parent: Senegal, Mauritania, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Nigeria, Chad, Sudan, and Eritrea
fields.Info:
• A semi-arid belt across Africa south of the Sahara, from the Atlantic coast of Senegal to the Red Sea in Sudan and Eritrea
  • It lies between the Sahara and the savanna to the south; Lake Chad and the Niger bend are in it
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Senegal, Mauritania, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, and 4 more

fields.Name: Caucasus
fields.Info:
• A region between the Black Sea and Caspian Sea, at the boundary of Europe and Asia, made up of the Greater Caucasus range and Transcaucasia
  • It includes Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Russia's North Caucasus; Mount Elbrus is its highest peak
fields.Photo caption: Mount Kazbek above the Gergeti Trinity Church
fields.Locator: Countries::Russia, Georgia, Azerbaijan, and Armenia##Countries::Russia, Georgia, Azerbaijan, and Armenia

fields.Name: Mesoamerica
fields.Parent: Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Costa Rica
fields.Info:
• A cultural region of southern Mexico and Central America where pre-Columbian civilizations such as the Olmec, Maya, and Aztec developed
  • It spans from the Valley of Mexico to Costa Rica; maize agriculture and pyramids are its hallmarks
fields.Locator: Countries::Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras, and 2 more##Countries::Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras, and 2 more

fields.Name: Maghreb
fields.Parent: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, and Mauritania
fields.Info:
• The region of northwest Africa between the Atlantic and Libya, including Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, and Mauritania, along the Atlas Mountains and Mediterranean coast
  • Its name means “the west” in Arabic; the Atlas Mountains cross it

fields.Name: Levant
fields.Parent: Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine, and Jordan
fields.Info:
• The eastern Mediterranean region, including Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine, and Jordan, with Cyprus and parts of Turkey, and Egypt's Sinai
  • It has a narrow coastal plain, the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon mountains, and the Jordan Rift Valley

fields.Name: Great Plains
fields.Info:
• A broad grassland region of central North America, east of the Rocky Mountains, from Canada's Prairie Provinces to Texas
  • Rainfall decreases westward; the Ogallala Aquifer underlies it; the Missouri and Platte rivers cross it

fields.Name: Pampas
fields.Info:
• A fertile grassland plain in South America, in Argentina, Uruguay, and southern Brazil, between the Andes and the Atlantic
  • The Río de la Plata borders it; it is famed for cattle and gauchos

fields.Name: Fertile Crescent
fields.Parent: Turkey, Egypt, Cyprus, Iran, Iraq, Israel, and Jordan
fields.Info:
• A crescent-shaped region of fertile land in West Asia, from the Nile Valley through the Levant to the Tigris and Euphrates and the Persian Gulf
  • The cradle of early agriculture; it includes Mesopotamia
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Turkey, Egypt, Cyprus, Iran, Iraq, and 2 more

fields.Name: Soviet Union
fields.Info:
• Covered about one-sixth of Earth's land surface, stretching across Eastern Europe, the Caucasus, Central Asia, and Siberia to the Pacific, with 15 union republics
  • Its territory split into fifteen countries; Russia, the largest republic, held more than three-quarters of its area
fields.Now: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Estonia, and 10 more

fields.Name: Nazi Germany
fields.Info:
• Germany under the Third Reich, which by 1939 included Austria, the Sudetenland, and Memel Territory, and then occupied much of Europe
  • Its territory included East Prussia, separated from the rest by the Polish Corridor until 1939

fields.Name: Empire of Japan
fields.Info:
• Comprised the Japanese home islands, plus Korea, Taiwan, southern Sakhalin, Manchukuo (puppet state) and Pacific islands, and briefly much of East and Southeast Asia
  • At its height in 1942 it stretched from the Aleutians to the Solomons and Burma

fields.Name: Ottoman Empire
fields.Info:
• Spanned Anatolia, the Balkans, the Middle East, and North Africa around the eastern Mediterranean, with its capital at Constantinople (Istanbul)
  • It controlled the Bosporus and the Dardanelles; the Black Sea was in effect an Ottoman lake for a time
fields.Photo caption: The Süleymaniye Mosque, built for Suleiman the Magnificent, Istanbul

fields.Name: Confederate States of America
fields.Info:
• Eleven southern US states that seceded: South Carolina, Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Arkansas, Tennessee, and North Carolina
  • It stretched along the Gulf and southern Atlantic coasts from Texas to Virginia; the Mississippi River split it

fields.Name: Austria-Hungary
fields.Info:
• A dual monarchy in Central Europe, made up of Austria and Hungary with Bohemia, Galicia, Transylvania, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina
  • It occupied the Danube basin and had a short coast on the Adriatic; Vienna and Budapest were its two capitals
fields.Now: Austria, Hungary, Czechia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Poland, Romania, Ukraine, Italy, Serbia, and Montenegro
fields.Locator: Countries::Czechia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and 8 more##Countries::Czechia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and 8 more

fields.Name: Yugoslavia
fields.Info:
• A federation in the western Balkans of six republics: Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and Macedonia, with Vojvodina and Kosovo as provinces of Serbia
  • It stretched from the Alps to the Greek border and had a long Adriatic coast
fields.Now: Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Slovenia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Kosovo
fields.Locator: Countries::Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Slovenia, Montenegro, and 2 more##Countries::Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Slovenia, Montenegro, and 2 more

fields.Name: Czechoslovakia
fields.Info:
• A Central European state made up of Bohemia, Moravia, Slovakia and (until 1945) Subcarpathian Ruthenia
  • Split peacefully into the Czech Republic and Slovakia in 1993
fields.Photo caption: Prague Castle, seat of the Czechoslovak presidents

fields.Name: East Germany
fields.Info:
• The German Democratic Republic, in eastern Germany, bordering Poland, Czechoslovakia, and West Germany, with a Baltic coast; East Berlin was its capital
  • It included the Harz, Thuringian Forest, the Elbe valley, and the Baltic island of Rügen

fields.Name: West Germany
fields.Info:
• The Federal Republic of Germany, made up of the western part of Germany, bordering France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Denmark, Austria, and Switzerland, with West Berlin as an enclave
  • Its capital was Bonn, on the Rhine

fields.Name: South Vietnam
fields.Info:
• The southern half of Vietnam, south of the 17th parallel demarcation line, from the Ben Hai River to the Mekong Delta
  • Its capital was Saigon; it included the Central Highlands

fields.Name: Republic of China
fields.Info:
• The government of China from 1912; after 1949 it was confined to Taiwan and its small islands (Penghu, Kinmen, and Matsu)
  • Before 1949 it claimed all of China, plus Mongolia; the capital moved to Taipei

fields.Name: Rhodesia
fields.Info:
• A landlocked southern African state between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers, named for Cecil Rhodes; now Zimbabwe
  • Its capital was Salisbury (now Harare); Lake Kariba and Victoria Falls lay on its border with Zambia
fields.Photo caption: A jacaranda in bloom in suburban Salisbury, c. 1970s

fields.Name: Kingdom of Prussia
fields.Info:
• A kingdom of northern and eastern Germany centred on Brandenburg and East Prussia, at its height stretching from the Rhineland to the Neman River
  • It spread across the North European Plain; its capital was Berlin, and its former lands now lie in Germany, Poland, and Russia
fields.Locator: Countries::Germany, Poland, and Russia##Countries::Germany, Poland, and Russia

fields.Name: Russian Empire
fields.Info:
• Spread across Eastern Europe, the Caucasus, Central Asia, Siberia and, until 1867, Alaska, the world's third-largest empire
  • Its capital was Saint Petersburg; it included Finland, Poland, and the Baltic provinces
fields.Now: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Finland, Poland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Finland, and 12 more

fields.Name: Weimar Republic
fields.Info:
• Germany between 1918 and 1933, smaller than before World War I after losing Alsace-Lorraine, the Polish Corridor, and colonies
  • It kept East Prussia as an exclave separated from the rest by the Polish Corridor to Danzig

fields.Name: British Raj
fields.Info:
• British-ruled India, comprising the modern territory of India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh, and Burma until 1937
  • Its provinces and about 560 princely states covered the subcontinent; its capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911

fields.Name: French Indochina
fields.Info:
• A French colony on the eastern side of mainland Southeast Asia, made up of Vietnam (Tonkin, Annam, and Cochinchina), Cambodia, and Laos
  • Hanoi and Saigon were its main cities; the Mekong valley connected its parts
fields.Photo caption: Emperor Bảo Đại's pilgrimage to the Nguyễn ancestral tombs, Thanh Hóa, 1932
fields.Locator: Countries::Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia##Countries::Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia

fields.Name: Kingdom of Italy
fields.Info:
• The unified Italian state, covering the Italian Peninsula, Sicily, and Sardinia, plus overseas colonies in Libya, Eritrea, Somalia and, later, Ethiopia
  • Rome became its capital in 1871

fields.Name: Spanish Empire
fields.Info:
• Covered most of Central and South America (except Brazil), the Caribbean, the Philippines, and parts of North America, with outposts in Africa
  • Its viceroyalties included New Spain, Peru, New Granada, and the Río de la Plata
fields.Now: Spain, most of Latin America, and the Philippines

fields.Name: Dutch East Indies
fields.Info:
• A Dutch colony in Southeast Asia covering the islands of modern Indonesia, from Sumatra to western New Guinea
  • Batavia (Jakarta) on Java was its capital; the Spice Islands (Maluku) were its early prize

fields.Name: Union of South Africa
fields.Info:
• A dominion made up of the Cape Colony, Natal, Transvaal, and Orange Free State, covering modern South Africa
  • It also administered South West Africa (Namibia); Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein were its capitals

fields.Name: United Arab Republic
fields.Info:
• A union of Egypt and Syria, with Yemen briefly attached, forming one state between the Nile and the Euphrates
  • Its capital was Cairo; Syria left in 1961, but Egypt kept the name until 1971

fields.Name: Zaire
fields.Info:
• The name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997, covering the Congo Basin in Central Africa
  • It included the Katanga copper belt and the Kivu highlands; its capital was Kinshasa

fields.Name: Burma
fields.Info:
• The name of Myanmar until 1989, in mainland Southeast Asia between India and Thailand, on the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea
  • The Irrawaddy River flows through its centre; the capital was Rangoon (now Yangon)

fields.Name: Kingdom of Hawaii
fields.Info:
• A kingdom made up of the eight main Hawaiian islands in the mid-Pacific, united under Kamehameha I
  • Its capital moved from Lahaina to Honolulu on Oahu; the archipelago is now the US state of Hawaii

fields.Name: Republic of Texas
fields.Info:
• An independent state on the Gulf Coast, claiming territory west to the Rio Grande, including parts of what became New Mexico, Colorado, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Wyoming
  • Its capitals included Houston and Austin; its claim to land west of the Nueces River was disputed with Mexico

fields.Name: Gran Colombia
fields.Info:
• A South American republic covering modern Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, and Panama, and parts of northern Peru, Guyana, and Brazil
  • Bogotá was its capital; the Andes and the Orinoco basin ran through it

fields.Name: Ceylon
fields.Info:
• The name of Sri Lanka until 1972, an island off the southern tip of India, across the Palk Strait
  • The name derives from the Portuguese Ceilão; its capital was Colombo

fields.Name: Siam
fields.Info:
• The name of Thailand until 1939, in mainland Southeast Asia, centred on the Chao Phraya River basin
  • Its capital was Bangkok; it lay between British Burma and French Indochina
fields.Photo caption: Wat Phra Kaew, the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, Bangkok

fields.Name: Persia
fields.Info:
• The name used internationally for Iran until 1935, on the high Iranian plateau between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf
  • Its ancient empire stretched from the Indus to the Mediterranean; Persepolis was a ceremonial capital

fields.Name: Abyssinia
fields.Info:
• The old name for Ethiopia, a highland state in the Horn of Africa, including the Ethiopian Highlands and the source of the Blue Nile at Lake Tana
  • Its heartland lay around Aksum, Gondar, and later Addis Ababa

fields.Name: Transvaal
fields.Info:
• A province of South Africa in the northeast, north of the Vaal River (its name means “across the Vaal”), containing Pretoria and Johannesburg
  • Its Highveld and the Witwatersrand gold fields are in it; Kruger National Park lay in its east

fields.Name: Orange Free State
fields.Info:
• A Boer republic and later South African province in the interior, between the Orange and Vaal rivers
  • Bloemfontein was its capital; it was renamed Free State in 1995

fields.Name: Kingdom of Hungary
fields.Info:
• A Central European kingdom in the Carpathian Basin, extending across the Danube and Tisza plains, and including Transylvania, Slovakia, Croatia, and the Banat
  • After 1920 it lost about two-thirds of its territory under the Treaty of Trianon

fields.Name: Kingdom of Poland
fields.Info:
• A kingdom on the North European Plain, in the Vistula and Oder basins, later joined with Lithuania
  • Its early capitals were Gniezno, Poznań, and Kraków

fields.Name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
fields.Info:
• A state that spread from the Baltic to the Black Sea, covering modern Lithuania, Belarus, Ukraine, and parts of Poland and Russia
  • Its capital was Vilnius; at its height it reached from the Baltic to near Moscow
fields.Locator: Countries::Belarus, Ukraine, and 1 more##Countries::Belarus, Ukraine, and 1 more

fields.Name: Republic of Venice
fields.Info:
• A maritime republic based on the lagoon islands at the head of the Adriatic, with a mainland empire in Veneto and colonies along the Dalmatian coast and the eastern Mediterranean
  • It held Crete and Cyprus for centuries; the Doge's Palace was its seat

fields.Name: Papal States
fields.Info:
• Territories in central Italy under the pope's direct rule, from the Adriatic to the Tyrrhenian coast, including Rome, Lazio, Umbria, Marche, and Romagna
  • Italy annexed Rome in 1870, and the Lateran Treaty of 1929 left the pope Vatican City
fields.Photo caption: Melozzo da Forlì, Sixtus IV Appointing Platina as Prefect of the Vatican Library, 1477

fields.Name: Holy Roman Empire
fields.Info:
• A collection of states in central Europe, mostly in what is now Germany, Austria, Czechia, and northern Italy, with Switzerland and the Low Countries
  • It had no fixed capital; imperial diets met at Regensburg, and emperors were crowned at Aachen or Frankfurt
fields.Now: Germany, Austria, Czechia, Slovenia, Switzerland, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, and Liechtenstein
fields.Locator: Countries::Germany, Austria, Czechia, Slovenia, Switzerland, and 4 more##Countries::Germany, Austria, Czechia, Slovenia, Switzerland, and 4 more

fields.Name: Byzantine Empire
fields.Info:
• The eastern Roman Empire, centred on Constantinople, at its height including Anatolia, the Balkans, Italy, and North Africa
  • By the end it was reduced to the city and a few parts of Greece

fields.Name: Mughal Empire
fields.Info:
• An empire in the Indian subcontinent, with core lands in the Indo-Gangetic plain around Delhi, Agra, and Lahore
  • At its height under Aurangzeb it extended over almost all of South Asia except the far south
fields.Photo caption: The Taj Mahal, Agra, built for Shah Jahan

fields.Name: Qing dynasty
fields.Info:
• The last imperial dynasty of China, from Manchuria, which controlled China proper, Mongolia, Tibet, and Xinjiang, and Taiwan until 1895
  • Its capital was Beijing; its Manchu homeland lay in Manchuria beyond the Great Wall

fields.Name: Kingdom of Portugal
fields.Info:
• A kingdom on the western Iberian Peninsula, from the Minho River to the Algarve, with the Atlantic islands of the Azores and Madeira
  • It ran a maritime empire in Brazil, Africa, and Asia; Lisbon was its capital

fields.Name: Republic of Genoa
fields.Info:
• A maritime republic on the Ligurian coast of northwestern Italy, with colonies across the Mediterranean and Black Sea, including Corsica
  • The port of Genoa faced the Ligurian Sea; its territory was a narrow coastal strip backed by the Apennines

fields.Name: Duchy of Savoy
fields.Info:
• A state in the western Alps, straddling France and Italy, covering Savoy, Piedmont, and Nice, with its capital at Chambéry then Turin
  • It controlled the Alpine passes between France and Italy; its House of Savoy later became Italy's royal family

fields.Name: Manchukuo
fields.Info:
• A puppet state that Japan set up in Manchuria (Northeast China) and Inner Mongolia, including Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang, and parts of Inner Mongolia
  • Its capital was Hsinking (now Changchun); Harbin and Mukden were its main cities

fields.Name: South Yemen
fields.Info:
• A state in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, on the Gulf of Aden, with Aden as its capital
  • It included the Hadhramaut and the island of Socotra; it joined North Yemen in 1990

fields.Name: Mesopotamia
fields.Info:
• The land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, mostly in modern Iraq and with parts in Syria, Turkey, and Iran
  • Its name means “between the rivers” in Greek; Sumer, Babylon, and Assyria arose here
fields.Now: Iraq, with parts in Syria, Turkey, and Iran
fields.Photo caption: Statue of Gudea, ruler of Lagash, c. 2090 BCE

fields.Name: Gaul
fields.Info:
• The Roman name for the region of Western Europe covering modern France, Belgium, Luxembourg, and parts of Switzerland, the Netherlands, and Germany west of the Rhine
  • Transalpine Gaul lay north of the Alps, Cisalpine Gaul in northern Italy
fields.Photo caption: Gaul in Caesar's time, from a historical atlas

fields.Name: Bohemia
fields.Info:
• The western part of the Czech Republic, a basin ringed by mountains including the Ore, Bohemian Forest, and Giant Mountains, drained by the Vltava and Elbe
  • Prague lies on the Vltava; it borders Germany and Poland

fields.Name: Silesia
fields.Info:
• A historical region of Central Europe around the upper Oder River, mostly in southwestern Poland with small parts in the Czech Republic and Germany
  • The Sudetes and Upper Silesian coalfield are in it; Wrocław is its largest city
fields.Now: Poland, with parts in Czech Republic and Germany
fields.Photo caption: Market Square of Wrocław's Old Town

fields.Name: Galicia
fields.Info:
• An autonomous community in the northwest corner of Spain, on the Atlantic, with a coast of deep inlets called rías
  • Its capital, Santiago de Compostela, is the end of the Camino de Santiago; Cape Finisterre is on its coast

fields.Name: Bengal
fields.Info:
• A region in the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta at the head of the Bay of Bengal, divided between Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal
  • Its low, flood-prone delta holds the Sundarbans; Dhaka and Kolkata are its chief cities
fields.Photo caption: Mangrove creek in the Sundarbans, Ganges–Brahmaputra delta

fields.Name: Manchuria
fields.Info:
• A region of northeastern China (Liaoning, Jilin, and Heilongjiang) and parts of Russia's Far East, bordered by Korea, Mongolia, and the Amur and Ussuri rivers
  • It includes the Songhua and Liao rivers; the Changbai Mountains lie along the Korean border

fields.Name: Thrace
fields.Info:
• A historical region of southeastern Europe, now divided among Bulgaria, Greece, and Turkey, between the Balkan Mountains and the Aegean Sea
  • The Maritsa River flows through it; Edirne, Turkey's European gateway, is here
fields.Photo caption: Selimiye Mosque and the Sinan statue, Edirne, Turkish Thrace

fields.Name: Dalmatia
fields.Info:
• A narrow coastal region of Croatia on the Adriatic Sea, stretching from Zadar to the Bay of Kotor, backed by the Dinaric Alps
  • It has over a thousand islands, including Hvar and Brač; Split and Dubrovnik are its main cities

fields.Name: Moravia
fields.Info:
• The eastern part of the Czech Republic, in the basin of the Morava River, between Bohemia and Slovakia
  • Brno is its main city; the Moravian Gate is a lowland pass to Poland

fields.Name: Pomerania
fields.Info:
• A historical region on the southern Baltic coast, now split between Poland and Germany, from the Oder to the Vistula
  • Its coast has Szczecin, Gdańsk, and the island of Rügen

fields.Name: Livonia
fields.Info:
• A historical region on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea, in what is now Latvia and Estonia, around the Gulf of Riga
  • It was the homeland of the Livonians; the Daugava River and the Livonian coast lie in it

fields.Name: Bessarabia
fields.Info:
• A historical region between the Dniester and Prut rivers and the Danube, now mostly in Moldova, with a southern part in Ukraine
  • It includes the Danube delta's northern arm; Chișinău is its main city
fields.Photo caption: The Akkerman fortress in Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi, Ukraine

fields.Name: Wallachia
fields.Info:
• A historical region of southern Romania between the Danube and the southern Carpathians, divided by the Olt River into Oltenia and Muntenia
  • Bucharest lies in it; the Danube forms its southern boundary with Bulgaria

fields.Name: Moldavia
fields.Info:
• A historical region of eastern Romania between the Carpathians and the Prut River, extended east to the Dniester
  • Iași is its main city; its painted monasteries are UNESCO sites

fields.Name: Ruthenia
fields.Info:
• A historical name for the eastern Slavic lands of modern Ukraine, Belarus, and Russia, and in particular the Carpathian region of Transcarpathia
  • Its heartland lay on the Dnieper River around Kyiv
fields.Now: Ukraine, with parts in Slovakia and Poland

fields.Name: Alsace-Lorraine
fields.Info:
• A territory on the Franco-German border, comprising Alsace and part of Lorraine, west of the Rhine and in the Vosges Mountains
  • It changed hands between France and Germany from 1871; Strasbourg and Metz were its main cities

fields.Name: Macedonia
fields.Info:
• A geographic region in the central Balkans, divided among Greece, North Macedonia, and Bulgaria, between the Aegean Sea and Lake Ohrid
  • The Vardar and Struma rivers flow through it; Thessaloniki and Skopje are its main cities
fields.Photo caption: The Stag Hunt mosaic from Pella, c. 300 BCE
fields.Locator: Countries::Greece, Bulgaria, and 1 more##Countries::Greece, Bulgaria, and 1 more

fields.Name: Epirus
fields.Info:
• A region in the northwestern part of Greece and southern Albania, between the Pindus Mountains and the Ionian Sea
  • Ioannina, on a lake, is its main city; the Vikos Gorge is in it

fields.Name: Phoenicia
fields.Info:
• An ancient maritime civilization on the eastern Mediterranean coast, in modern Lebanon and parts of Syria and Israel, with city-states such as Tyre, Sidon, and Byblos
  • Its colonies included Carthage in North Africa; the cedars of Lebanon were its timber
fields.Locator: Countries::Lebanon, Syria, and Israel##Countries::Lebanon, Syria, and Israel

fields.Name: Khorasan
fields.Info:
• A historical region spanning northeastern Iran, western and northern Afghanistan, and southern Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan; its name means “where the sun rises”
  • Its cities include Mashhad, Herat, and Nishapur; the Silk Road passed through it
fields.Locator: Countries::Iran, Afghanistan, and Turkmenistan##Countries::Iran, Afghanistan, and Turkmenistan

fields.Name: Sogdia
fields.Info:
• An ancient Iranian region in Central Asia, in the Zeravshan and Kashka Darya valleys, in modern Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, with cities such as Samarkand and Bukhara
  • Sogdian merchants dominated the Silk Road trade; it lay between the Amu Darya and Syr Darya
fields.Photo caption: Sogdian tribute bearers on the Apadana staircase, Persepolis

fields.Name: Deccan
fields.Info:
• A large plateau in southern India between the Western and Eastern Ghats, south of the Vindhya Range
  • The Godavari and Krishna rivers cross it; it lies in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh
fields.Photo caption: Ruins of Hampi, capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, Karnataka

fields.Name: Sindh
fields.Info:
• A province in southeastern Pakistan, on the Arabian Sea, along the lower Indus River and its delta
  • Karachi is its capital and largest city; the Thar Desert borders it on the east, and Mohenjo-daro lies in the province
fields.Photo caption: Tomb of Sultan Ibrahim, Makli Necropolis, Thatta

fields.Name: Punjab
fields.Info:
• A region in the northwest of the Indian subcontinent, in the plains of the Indus and its five tributaries, divided between India and Pakistan
  • Its name means “five waters”: the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej rivers; Lahore and Amritsar are in it

fields.Name: Indochina
fields.Parent: Singapore, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam
fields.Info:
• The peninsula of mainland Southeast Asia east of India and south of China, including Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Myanmar, and Peninsular Malaysia
  • The Mekong, Irrawaddy, and Chao Phraya rivers drain it
fields.Photo caption: The Mekong at Luang Prabang, Laos, from Mount Phou Si
fields.Waters: Gulf of Tonkin, South China Sea, Gulf of Thailand, Gulf of Martaban, Andaman Sea, and Bay of Bengal
fields.Locator: ##Countries::Singapore, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, and 2 more

fields.Name: Formosa
fields.Info:
• The historical name for Taiwan, from the Portuguese Ilha Formosa, “beautiful island”, in the western Pacific off the southeast coast of China
  • It is separated from the mainland by the Taiwan Strait; the Central Mountain Range runs down the island

fields.Name: Siberia
fields.Info:
• A vast region of northern Asia from the Ural Mountains to the Pacific, in Russia, covering most of the northern part of the country
  • It holds the Ob, Yenisei, and Lena rivers, Lake Baikal, and permafrost; the Trans-Siberian Railway crosses it

fields.Name: Aquitaine
fields.Info:
• A historical region of southwestern France between the Atlantic, the Garonne basin, and the Pyrenees, with Bordeaux its main city
  • The Gironde estuary and the landes forest lie in it; it is now part of Nouvelle-Aquitaine

fields.Name: Burgundy
fields.Info:
• A historical region of eastern France in the Saône and upper Seine valleys, along the Côte d'Or wine slopes
  • Dijon is its main city; it is now part of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté

fields.Name: Normandy
fields.Info:
• A historical region of northwestern France on the English Channel, around the lower Seine, with the Cotentin Peninsula
  • Its D-Day beaches, Mont-Saint-Michel, and the chalk cliffs at Étretat are in it
fields.Photo caption: Cliffs and beach at Étretat, on the Alabaster Coast

fields.Name: Bavaria
fields.Info:
• The largest state of Germany by area, in the southeast, bordering Austria and the Czech Republic, with the Bavarian Alps and the Danube
  • Its capital Munich is on the Isar; Zugspitze is Germany's highest peak

fields.Name: Saxony
fields.Info:
• A state in eastern Germany bordering Poland and the Czech Republic, in the Elbe valley between the Ore Mountains and Lusatia
  • Its capital Dresden lies on the Elbe; Leipzig is its largest city
fields.Photo caption: The Bastei in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains

fields.Name: Swabia
fields.Info:
• A historical region in southwestern Germany, mostly in Baden-Württemberg and Bavaria, between the Rhine, the Danube, and Lake Constance
  • The Swabian Jura and Black Forest are in it; Stuttgart and Augsburg are its main cities
fields.Photo caption: The Blautopf spring at Blaubeuren, in the Swabian Jura

fields.Name: Franconia
fields.Info:
• A historical region in central Germany, mostly in northern Bavaria and parts of Baden-Württemberg and Hesse, on the Main River
  • Nuremberg and Würzburg are its main cities; the Franconian Jura lies in it
fields.Photo caption: The Plönlein, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

fields.Name: Tuscany
fields.Info:
• A region of central Italy on the Tyrrhenian Sea, between the Apennines and the coast, with the Arno river valley
  • Its hills and cypress-lined roads are iconic; the Chianti wine region lies in it
fields.Photo caption: Chapel of the Madonna di Vitaleta, Val d'Orcia

fields.Name: Lombardy
fields.Info:
• A region of northern Italy, the most populous, from the Alps on the Swiss border to the Po plain, with the great lakes Como, Maggiore, and Garda
  • Milan is its capital; the Po River forms its southern boundary

fields.Name: Latium
fields.Info:
• A region of central Italy on the Tyrrhenian Sea, around the Tiber, with Rome its capital
  • Its hills include the Alban Hills and the Sabine mountains; the Pontine Marshes were drained in the 1930s

fields.Name: Attica
fields.Info:
• A region of Greece, a peninsula projecting into the Aegean Sea, containing Athens and its port Piraeus
  • It is bounded by the Saronic Gulf and the Euboean Gulf; the Acropolis is its landmark, and Mount Parnitha rises to its north
fields.Photo caption: The Temple of Poseidon at Sounion

fields.Name: Peloponnese
fields.Info:
• A large peninsula in southern Greece, joined to the mainland by the Isthmus of Corinth, cut by the Corinth Canal
  • Sparta, Olympia, and Mycenae are in it; the Taygetus range rises in the south

fields.Name: Cappadocia
fields.Info:
• A historical region in central Anatolia in Turkey, with volcanic rock formations, fairy chimneys, and underground cities
  • The Göreme valley and the rock-cut churches are UNESCO sites; Mount Erciyes rises above it

fields.Name: Assyria
fields.Info:
• An ancient Mesopotamian empire in the upper Tigris valley, in northern Iraq, with capitals at Assur, Nimrud, and Nineveh
  • At its height it stretched from Egypt to Elam; it covered the Fertile Crescent
  • Assyria ran from about 2025 to 609 BCE in three phases; the map shows its height under the last of them, the Neo-Assyrian Empire (911–609 BCE)
fields.Photo caption: Lamassu from the North-West Palace at Nimrud, British Museum
fields.Locator: Countries::Iraq, Syria, and Turkey##Countries::Iraq, Syria, and Turkey

fields.Name: Beijing
fields.Info:
• China's capital municipality, in northern China on the North China Plain, backed by the Yan Mountains to the north and west
  • The Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, and the Summer Palace are landmarks; parts of the Great Wall lie north of it
fields.Photo caption: The Central Business District, with the CITIC Tower (China Zun)

fields.Name: Tianjin
fields.Info:
• A municipality in northern China, about 120 km southeast of Beijing, on the Bohai Gulf at the mouth of the Hai River
  • Its port is the largest in northern China, and the Grand Canal passes through it

fields.Name: Hebei
fields.Info:
• A province of northern China surrounding Beijing and Tianjin, on the Bohai Gulf, with the Taihang Mountains to the west and the Yan Mountains to the north
  • The Great Wall crosses it; Chengde has an imperial mountain resort

fields.Name: Shanxi
fields.Info:
• A province in northern China on the Loess Plateau, west of the Taihang Mountains and east of the Yellow River
  • Its name means “west of the mountains”; Mount Wutai and Pingyao's walled city are in it

fields.Name: Inner Mongolia
fields.Info:
• An autonomous region of northern China along the border with Mongolia and Russia, stretching from the northeast to the Gobi and the Ordos Plateau
  • Much of it is grassland and desert; the Yellow River makes a great bend in it

fields.Name: Liaoning
fields.Info:
• A province in northeastern China on the Liaodong Peninsula, on the Bohai Sea and the Yellow Sea, bordering North Korea
  • Its capital Shenyang was the Manchu capital; Dalian is a major port

fields.Name: Jilin
fields.Info:
• A province of northeastern China bordering North Korea and Russia, with the Changbai Mountains and Heaven Lake on its southeastern edge
  • Changchun is its capital; the Songhua River flows through it

fields.Name: Heilongjiang
fields.Info:
• China's northernmost and easternmost province, named for the Heilong (Amur) River, which forms its border with Russia
  • The Songhua, Nen, and Ussuri rivers flow through it; Harbin is its capital, known for its ice festival

fields.Name: Shanghai
fields.Info:
• A municipality on the eastern coast of China at the mouth of the Yangtze River, on the East China Sea
  • The Bund, Pudong's skyline, and the Oriental Pearl Tower are landmarks; Chongming Island lies in the estuary

fields.Name: Jiangsu
fields.Info:
• A province on China's east coast, in the Yangtze delta, north of Shanghai, with the Grand Canal crossing it
  • Nanjing is its capital; the classical gardens of Suzhou and Lake Tai are in it

fields.Name: Zhejiang
fields.Info:
• A province on China's southeastern coast, south of the Yangtze Delta, with the Qiantang River and a coastline of many islands
  • Hangzhou, on West Lake, is its capital; Ningbo is a major port
fields.Photo caption: Leifeng Pagoda across West Lake, Hangzhou

fields.Name: Anhui
fields.Info:
• A province in eastern China, spanning the Yangtze and Huai rivers, with the Huangshan (Yellow Mountains)
  • Hefei is its capital; Chao Lake is its largest lake
fields.Photo caption: Pines and granite peaks on Huangshan

fields.Name: Fujian
fields.Info:
• A province on China's southeastern coast facing Taiwan across the Taiwan Strait, mountainous with a heavily indented coastline
  • Fuzhou is its capital; Xiamen is a port, and the Wuyi Mountains produce tea

fields.Name: Jiangxi
fields.Info:
• A landlocked province of southeastern China, with the Gan River flowing into Poyang Lake, China's largest freshwater lake
  • Nanchang is its capital; Jingdezhen is famous for porcelain

fields.Name: Shandong
fields.Info:
• A province on China's eastern coast, projecting as the Shandong Peninsula between the Bohai Sea and the Yellow Sea
  • Mount Tai, one of China's five sacred mountains, and Confucius' birthplace Qufu are in it

fields.Name: Henan
fields.Info:
• A province of central China on the North China Plain, in the Yellow River's middle and lower course, with the Song and Funiu mountains
  • Zhengzhou is its capital; Luoyang, Kaifeng, and Anyang, ancient capitals, and the Shaolin Monastery are in it

fields.Name: Hubei
fields.Info:
• A province of central China around the middle Yangtze and the Han River, with the Three Gorges Dam
  • Wuhan, at the confluence of the Yangtze and Han, is its capital; Jingzhou and the Wudang Mountains are in it
fields.Photo caption: The Xiling Gorge of the Yangtze

fields.Name: Hunan
fields.Info:
• A province of south-central China, south of the Yangtze and Dongting Lake, named for being south of the lake
  • Changsha is its capital; the Xiang River and Zhangjiajie's sandstone pillars are in it

fields.Name: Guangdong
fields.Info:
• China's most populous province, on the southern coast, around the Pearl River Delta, facing the South China Sea, bordering Hong Kong and Macau
  • Guangzhou is its capital; Shenzhen is a special economic zone

fields.Name: Guangxi
fields.Info:
• An autonomous region of southern China bordering Vietnam, with a karst landscape around Guilin and the Li River
  • Nanning is its capital; the Zhuang are its largest ethnic group
fields.Photo caption: Karst peaks along the Li River near Yangshuo

fields.Name: Hainan
fields.Info:
• China's southernmost province, on Hainan Island in the South China Sea, separated from Guangdong by the Qiongzhou Strait
  • Haikou is its capital; Sanya is a beach resort

fields.Name: Chongqing
fields.Info:
• A municipality in southwestern China at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers, in the mountainous east of Sichuan Basin
  • It became a municipality in 1997; the Three Gorges begin near it
fields.Photo caption: Qiansimen Bridge, Hongya Cave, and the World Financial Centre

fields.Name: Sichuan
fields.Info:
• A province in southwestern China, centred on the fertile Sichuan Basin, ringed by the Tibetan Plateau to the west
  • Chengdu is its capital; Mount Emei, Leshan Giant Buddha, and giant pandas are in it
fields.Photo caption: Larix potaninii trees in autumn colour

fields.Name: Guizhou
fields.Info:
• A mountainous province of southwestern China on the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau, with a karst landscape
  • Guiyang is its capital; Huangguoshu Waterfall is one of the largest in Asia

fields.Name: Yunnan
fields.Info:
• A province in southwestern China bordering Myanmar, Laos, and Vietnam, on the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau
  • The Yangtze, Mekong, and Salween run through parallel gorges; Kunming is its capital

fields.Name: Tibet Autonomous Region
fields.Info:
• An autonomous region in southwestern China on the Tibetan Plateau, the highest region on Earth, bordering India, Nepal, Bhutan, and Myanmar
  • Lhasa is its capital; Mount Everest is on its border, and the Yarlung Tsangpo flows across it

fields.Name: Shaanxi
fields.Info:
• A province in northwestern China on the middle Yellow River, with the Loess Plateau in the north and the Qinling Mountains in the south
  • Xi'an is its capital; the Terracotta Army near it is a landmark

fields.Name: Gansu
fields.Info:
• A long, narrow province of northwestern China, along the Hexi Corridor between the Tibetan and Mongolian plateaus, an old Silk Road route
  • Lanzhou, on the Yellow River, is its capital; Dunhuang's Mogao Caves are in it

fields.Name: Qinghai
fields.Info:
• A province in western China on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau, the source of the Yellow, Yangtze, and Mekong rivers
  • Its name means “blue sea”, after Qinghai Lake, China's largest lake; Xining is its capital

fields.Name: Ningxia
fields.Info:
• A small autonomous region in northwestern China, on the upper Yellow River, between the Gobi and the Loess Plateau, home of the Hui
  • Yinchuan is its capital; the Helan Mountains rise on its west
