fields.Photo caption: Tomb of the Western Xia dynasty

fields.Name: Xinjiang
fields.Info:
• China's largest province-level region, an autonomous region in the far northwest, containing the Taklamakan Desert and the Tian Shan, Kunlun, and Altai mountains
  • Ürümqi is its capital; it borders eight countries, including Kazakhstan, Pakistan, and Mongolia
fields.Photo caption: Tianchi, the Heavenly Lake, in the Tian Shan

fields.Name: Pingyuan Province
fields.Info:
• A former province of China in the North China Plain, straddling the Yellow River, created in 1949 from parts of Henan, Shandong, and Hebei
  • Xinxiang was its capital; it was abolished in 1952

fields.Name: Xikang
fields.Info:
• A former province of western China, created in 1939 from the eastern Kham region of Tibet and western Sichuan, on the Tibetan Plateau's eastern edge
  • It was abolished in 1955, and its territory divided between Sichuan and Tibet; Kangding, then Ya'an, was its capital
fields.Photo caption: Kangding, the former provincial capital, from above

fields.Name: Arunachal Pradesh
fields.Info:
• India's northeasternmost state, bordering Bhutan, Tibet (China) and Myanmar, rising to the eastern Himalayas
  • The Brahmaputra enters India here as the Dihang; Tawang Monastery is its landmark, and the McMahon Line marks its northern border

fields.Name: Assam
fields.Info:
• A state in northeastern India in the Brahmaputra valley, between the Himalayan foothills and the Meghalaya plateau
  • Known for its tea gardens; Majuli, the world's largest river island, and Kaziranga National Park are in it
fields.Photo caption: Talatal Ghar, the Ahom palace at Sivasagar

fields.Name: Bihar
fields.Info:
• A landlocked state in eastern India on the Gangetic plain, with the Ganges flowing west to east through it and Nepal to the north
  • The Kosi River, called the “sorrow of Bihar” for its floods, crosses it; Bodh Gaya and Nalanda are in the state

fields.Name: Chhattisgarh
fields.Info:
• A landlocked state in central India, a plateau with forests, on the upper Mahanadi basin
  • Chitrakote Falls, the widest in India, and the Bastar region are in it

fields.Name: Goa
fields.Info:
• India's smallest state by area, on the Konkan coast of the Arabian Sea, between the Western Ghats and the sea
  • Its beaches and Old Goa's churches are landmarks; the Mandovi and Zuari rivers cross it
fields.Photo caption: The Terekhol River on the Maharashtra border

fields.Name: Gujarat
fields.Info:
• A state on India's western coast on the Arabian Sea, with the Kathiawar peninsula, the Gulf of Kutch, and the Gulf of Khambhat
  • It contains the Rann of Kutch salt marsh and the Gir Forest, home of the Asiatic lion

fields.Name: Haryana
fields.Info:
• A state in northern India surrounding Delhi on three sides, on the plains between the Yamuna and the Ghaggar rivers
  • Kurukshetra, the battlefield of the Mahabharata, is in it; the Aravalli hills rise in the south

fields.Name: Himachal Pradesh
fields.Info:
• A Himalayan state in northern India, bordering Tibet, with valleys such as Kullu and Kangra and the Pir Panjal range
  • The Beas, Sutlej, and Ravi rivers rise here; Shimla, the old summer capital of British India, is in it
fields.Photo caption: A village near Trilokinath temple, Lahaul

fields.Name: Jammu and Kashmir
fields.Flag Symbolism: The flag of the former state, in use until 2019, when Jammu and Kashmir became a union territory: a white plough on red, with three stripes for Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, and Ladakh
fields.Info:
• A former state, now a union territory, in the far north of India in the western Himalayas, including the Kashmir Valley and the Jammu plains
  • The Jhelum River and Dal Lake lie in the Kashmir Valley; its territory is disputed with Pakistan and China

fields.Name: Jharkhand
fields.Info:
• A state in eastern India on the Chota Nagpur Plateau, rich in coal, iron, and other minerals
  • Its rivers include the Damodar and Subarnarekha; Ranchi and Jamshedpur are its major cities

fields.Name: Karnataka
fields.Info:
• A state in southwestern India on the Arabian Sea coast, with the Western Ghats and the Deccan plateau
  • The Kaveri and Tungabhadra rivers cross it; Hampi's ruins and Bengaluru, the tech centre, are in it

fields.Name: Kerala
fields.Info:
• A narrow state on India's southwestern Malabar Coast, between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea
  • Known for its backwaters, coconut groves, and spices; Vembanad Lake is the longest lake in India

fields.Name: Madhya Pradesh
fields.Info:
• The second-largest state of India by area, in the centre of the country, on the Malwa and Vindhya plateaus, with the Narmada River
  • It has many tiger reserves; Khajuraho and Sanchi are in it, and the Vindhya and Satpura ranges cross it

fields.Name: Maharashtra
fields.Info:
• A state in western India on the Arabian Sea, with the Western Ghats and the Deccan plateau, and the Godavari and Krishna rivers rising in it
  • Mumbai is its capital; the Ajanta and Ellora caves are in it

fields.Name: Manipur
fields.Info:
• A hilly state in northeastern India on the border with Myanmar, surrounding the Imphal Valley
  • Loktak Lake has floating islands (phumdis) and Keibul Lamjao National Park, home of the brow-antlered deer

fields.Name: Meghalaya
fields.Info:
• A state in northeastern India on a plateau above Bangladesh, made up of the Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia hills
  • Its name means “abode of clouds”; Mawsynram is one of the wettest places on Earth

fields.Name: Mizoram
fields.Info:
• A hilly state in northeastern India bordering Myanmar and Bangladesh, on the Lushai Hills
  • Its highest peak is Phawngpui; the Tlawng and Tuivawl rivers cross it

fields.Name: Nagaland
fields.Info:
• A hilly state in northeastern India bordering Myanmar, with the Naga Hills
  • Mount Saramati is its highest peak; Kohima is its capital and the Hornbill Festival is held there

fields.Name: Odisha
fields.Info:
• A state on India's east coast on the Bay of Bengal, with the Mahanadi delta and Chilika Lake, Asia's largest brackish lagoon
  • The Konark Sun Temple and Puri's Jagannath Temple are landmarks; it is prone to cyclones

fields.Name: Rajasthan
fields.Info:
• India's largest state by area, in the northwest, covering most of the Thar Desert and crossed by the Aravalli Range
  • Mount Abu is its only hill station; Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, and Jaisalmer are its historic cities

fields.Name: Sikkim
fields.Info:
• A small Himalayan state in northeastern India, bordering Nepal, Bhutan, and Tibet, with Kangchenjunga, India's highest peak, on its border with Nepal
  • Its Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La pass are in it
fields.Photo caption: Statue of Guru Padmasambhava, the patron saint

fields.Name: Tamil Nadu
fields.Info:
• A state on India's southeastern tip, on the Bay of Bengal and Indian Ocean, on the Coromandel Coast, with the Kaveri delta
  • Kanyakumari, the southern tip of the mainland, and the Nilgiri Hills are in it
fields.Photo caption: Tea plantations against serried ranges of the Nilgiris

fields.Name: Tripura
fields.Info:
• A small hilly state in northeastern India, almost surrounded by Bangladesh, with only a narrow link to the rest of India
  • Its Jampui Hills and Unakoti rock carvings are in it; the Gumti River crosses it

fields.Name: Uttar Pradesh
fields.Info:
• India's most populous state, in the north on the Gangetic plain, with the Ganges and Yamuna rivers meeting at Prayagraj
  • The Taj Mahal at Agra and holy Varanasi lie in it; Nepal is to its north
fields.Photo caption: The ghats of Varanasi on the Ganges

fields.Name: Uttarakhand
fields.Info:
• A Himalayan state in northern India bordering Nepal and Tibet, where the Ganges and Yamuna rise
  • Nanda Devi, in it, is India's second-highest mountain; Haridwar and Rishikesh lie on the Ganges

fields.Name: West Bengal
fields.Info:
• A state in eastern India in the Ganges delta, from the Himalayan foothills at Darjeeling to the Bay of Bengal, bordering Bangladesh
  • The Sundarbans mangrove forest lies in its south; Kolkata is on the Hooghly

fields.Name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
fields.Info:
• A union territory in the Bay of Bengal, an archipelago of about 570 islands, closer to Myanmar and Indonesia than to India
  • Sri Vijaya Puram (formerly Port Blair) is its capital; the Ten Degree Channel separates the Andamans from the Nicobars
fields.Locator: Capital::Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair)##Country::India|Capital::Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair)

fields.Name: Chandigarh
fields.Info:
• A union territory and city in northern India, the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana, at the foot of the Shivalik Hills
  • Designed by Le Corbusier; its Rock Garden and Capitol Complex are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: The Capitol Complex, by Le Corbusier

fields.Name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli district
fields.Info:
• A former union territory of western India, made up of two enclaves inland from the Arabian Sea between Gujarat and Maharashtra, on the Daman Ganga River
  • Silvassa was its capital; it merged with Daman and Diu in 2020

fields.Name: Lakshadweep
fields.Info:
• A union territory of India, a group of coral atolls and islands in the Laccadive Sea off the Malabar Coast, about 200–440 km from Kerala
  • Kavaratti is its capital; the smallest territory of India by area

fields.Name: Delhi
fields.Info:
• A union territory and India's capital region, on the Yamuna River between the Thar Desert and the Gangetic plain
  • Old Delhi holds the Red Fort and Jama Masjid; New Delhi holds Rashtrapati Bhavan and India Gate

fields.Name: Puducherry
fields.Info:
• A union territory of four small former French enclaves, on the Coromandel Coast, the Malabar Coast, and the Godavari delta
  • Puducherry town has a French quarter; the other enclaves are Karaikal, Yanam, and Mahé

fields.Name: Daman and Diu
fields.Info:
• A former union territory on the Gujarat coast of western India, made up of Daman on the mainland and Diu, an island, separated by the Gulf of Khambhat
  • It merged with Dadra and Nagar Haveli in 2020; Diu Fort is its landmark

fields.Name: Telangana
fields.Info:
• A state in southern India on the Deccan Plateau, formed in 2014 from Andhra Pradesh, on the Godavari and Krishna rivers
  • Hyderabad, on the Musi River, is its capital; the Charminar is a landmark

fields.Name: Andhra Pradesh
fields.Info:
• A state on India's southeastern coast, on the Bay of Bengal, from the Godavari–Krishna deltas to the Eastern Ghats, with the second-longest coastline of any Indian state
  • Visakhapatnam is a major port; the Tirumala hills hold the Venkateswara Temple

fields.Name: Ladakh
fields.Info:
• A union territory in the far north of India on the Tibetan Plateau, between the Karakoram and the Himalayas, at high altitudes
  • Leh is its capital; the Indus River and Pangong Lake are in it
fields.Photo caption: Rangdum Monastery in the Suru Valley

fields.Name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
fields.Info:
• A union territory of western India formed in 2020 by merging two smaller ones, made up of three separate parts on the coast of Gujarat and inland
  • Daman and Diu are on the Arabian Sea; Silvassa lies inland on the Daman Ganga

fields.Name: Mexico City
fields.Info:
• Mexico's capital, in the high Valley of Mexico at about 2,240 m, built on the drained lake bed of Lake Texcoco, surrounded by volcanoes
  • It is prone to earthquakes and sinking; the Zócalo and Chapultepec Park are landmarks

fields.Name: Aguascalientes
fields.Info:
• A small state in central Mexico on the high plateau, named for its hot springs
  • It lies in the Bajío region; the Aguascalientes River crosses it

fields.Name: Baja California
fields.Info:
• The northern state of the Baja California peninsula in northwestern Mexico, bordering California, between the Pacific and the Gulf of California
  • Tijuana and Mexicali lie on the US border; the Sierra de Juárez and San Pedro Mártir range run down its spine

fields.Name: Baja California Sur
fields.Info:
• The southern state of the Baja California peninsula, between the Pacific and the Gulf of California, ending at Cabo San Lucas
  • Its Sea of Cortés coast has La Paz; the Vizcaíno desert lies in the north

fields.Name: Campeche
fields.Info:
• A state on the western Yucatán Peninsula, on the Gulf of Mexico, bordering Guatemala
  • The fortified port of Campeche and Maya ruins such as Calakmul are in it

fields.Name: Chiapas
fields.Info:
• Mexico's southernmost state, on the Pacific, bordering Guatemala, with the Sierra Madre de Chiapas and the Lacandon rainforest
  • The Sumidero Canyon and Palenque's Maya ruins are in it

fields.Name: Chihuahua
fields.Info:
• Mexico's largest state by area, in the north, bordering Texas and New Mexico, in the Sierra Madre Occidental and the Chihuahuan Desert
  • The Copper Canyon system is bigger than the Grand Canyon; the Conchos River flows through it

fields.Name: Coahuila
fields.Info:
• A large state in northern Mexico bordering Texas at the Rio Grande, in the Chihuahuan Desert
  • Its Cuatro Ciénegas basin has rare pools; Saltillo is its capital
fields.Photo caption: Dunes and sierra in the Coahuila desert

fields.Name: Colima
fields.Info:
• A small state on the Pacific coast of western Mexico, with the Volcán de Colima, one of the most active in the country
  • It shares its name with its capital; its coast has Manzanillo, a major port

fields.Name: Durango
fields.Info:
• A state in northwestern Mexico in the Sierra Madre Occidental, high plateau, and desert
  • It has been a film location for many westerns; the Mezquital and Nazas rivers cross it

fields.Name: Guanajuato
fields.Info:
• A state in central Mexico in the Bajío, on a high plateau, with a rich silver-mining history
  • Its capital, Guanajuato city, has colourful hillside houses and tunnels; San Miguel de Allende is in it

fields.Name: Guerrero
fields.Info:
• A state on Mexico's Pacific coast in the south, between the Sierra Madre del Sur and the ocean
  • Acapulco is its main resort; the Balsas River crosses it
fields.Photo caption: Taxco and the church of Santa Prisca

fields.Name: Hidalgo
fields.Info:
• A state in central Mexico, north of Mexico City, in the Sierra Madre Oriental and the Mezquital Valley
  • Its Tula ruins with giant Atlantean figures and Pachuca's silver mines are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: Houses in Real del Monte, a silver-mining town

fields.Name: Jalisco
fields.Info:
• A state in western Mexico on the Pacific, with Lake Chapala, Mexico's largest lake, and the volcanic Sierra Madre Occidental
  • Guadalajara is its capital, and Puerto Vallarta is a resort; the town of Tequila gave its name to the drink
fields.Photo caption: The Santa María de los Ángeles aqueduct, begun in 1787

fields.Name: State of Mexico
fields.Info:
• A state in central Mexico surrounding Mexico City on three sides, containing the volcano Nevado de Toluca and Teotihuacan
  • It is Mexico's most populous state; Toluca is its capital
fields.Photo caption: The crater lake of the Nevado de Toluca

fields.Name: Michoacán
fields.Info:
• A state in western Mexico on the Pacific, with the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt and Lake Pátzcuaro
  • Each winter, monarch butterflies migrate to its Oyamel fir forests; the Balsas River forms part of its southern border

fields.Name: Morelos
fields.Info:
• A small state in central Mexico south of Mexico City, in a warm valley on the southern slopes of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt
  • Cuernavaca, its capital, is called the city of eternal spring; Tepoztlán is a pilgrimage site
fields.Photo caption: Xochicalco, a Mesoamerican hilltop ruin, Morelos

fields.Name: Nayarit
fields.Info:
• A state on Mexico's Pacific coast in the west, with the Sierra Madre Occidental inland and a coast of mangroves and beaches
  • The Islas Marías and Marismas Nacionales lagoons are on its coast

fields.Name: Nuevo León
fields.Info:
• A state in northeastern Mexico bordering Texas, in the Sierra Madre Oriental, with an industrial economy
  • Monterrey is its capital, and Cerro de la Silla overlooks it
fields.Photo caption: The town of Carmen, near Monterrey

fields.Name: Oaxaca
fields.Info:
• A state in southern Mexico on the Pacific, in the Sierra Madre del Sur, one of the most ethnically diverse in Mexico
  • Its Monte Albán and Mitla ruins and the Isthmus of Tehuantepec are landmarks

fields.Name: Puebla
fields.Info:
• A state in east-central Mexico, on a high plateau, including the volcano Popocatépetl on its western border and Pico de Orizaba nearby
  • The Great Pyramid of Cholula, the largest pyramid by volume, and the city of Puebla are in it

fields.Name: Querétaro
fields.Info:
• A state in central Mexico in the Bajío region, on the Central Plateau, with the Sierra Gorda in the north
  • The Peña de Bernal monolith and the aqueduct of Querétaro city are landmarks

fields.Name: Quintana Roo
fields.Info:
• A state on the eastern Yucatán Peninsula on the Caribbean coast, bordering Belize and Guatemala
  • Cancún, Cozumel, Isla Mujeres, and the ruins of Tulum are in it
fields.Photo caption: Temple of the Wind God, Tulum

fields.Name: San Luis Potosí
fields.Info:
• A state in central-northern Mexico, spanning the Central Plateau and the Huasteca region
  • Its silver-mining ghost town Real de Catorce and the surreal gardens of Las Pozas are in it
fields.Photo caption: Las Pozas, Xilitla, San Luis Potosí

fields.Name: Sinaloa
fields.Info:
• A state on Mexico's northwest Pacific coast, on the Gulf of California, between the Sierra Madre Occidental and the coastal plain
  • A major farming region; the Fuerte and Culiacán rivers cross it and Mazatlán is a resort

fields.Name: Sonora
fields.Info:
• Mexico's second-largest state, in the northwest, bordering Arizona, with the Sonoran Desert and a coast on the Gulf of California
  • The Pinacate volcanic field and Hermosillo are in it
fields.Photo caption: El Pinacate y Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve

fields.Name: Tabasco
fields.Info:
• A flat, humid state in southeastern Mexico on the Gulf of Mexico, crossed by the Grijalva and Usumacinta rivers
  • It is a major oil producer; the Olmec site of La Venta is in it
fields.Photo caption: An Olmec colossal head at La Venta Park, Villahermosa

fields.Name: Tamaulipas
fields.Info:
• A state in northeastern Mexico on the Gulf of Mexico, bordering Texas at the Rio Grande, with the Sierra Madre Oriental
  • Tampico is its oil port; the Laguna Madre coast is a lagoon

fields.Name: Tlaxcala
fields.Info:
• Mexico's smallest state, in the central highlands, on the slopes of La Malinche volcano
  • The Cacaxtla ruins hold well-preserved murals; its capital, also Tlaxcala, has some of the oldest colonial churches in the Americas

fields.Name: Veracruz
fields.Info:
• A long, narrow state along Mexico's Gulf coast, from the coastal plain to the Sierra Madre Oriental, including Pico de Orizaba, Mexico's highest peak
  • Its port of Veracruz is Mexico's oldest; the Papaloapan and Coatzacoalcos rivers cross it

fields.Name: Yucatán
fields.Info:
• A state on the northern Yucatán Peninsula on the Gulf of Mexico, a flat limestone plain with cenotes and no surface rivers
  • Chichén Itzá and Uxmal are in it; the Chicxulub crater lies partly beneath it
fields.Photo caption: The Pyramid of the Magician, Uxmal

fields.Name: Zacatecas
fields.Info:
• A state in north-central Mexico on the high plateau, with the Sierra Madre Occidental to the west
  • Its historic silver-mining city Zacatecas is a UNESCO site
fields.Photo caption: Stream in the Sierra de Cardos, part of the Sierra Madre Occidental

fields.Name: Abruzzo
fields.Info:
• A mountainous region of central Italy between the Apennines and the Adriatic coast, with the Gran Sasso and Majella massifs
  • Corno Grande is the highest peak of the Apennines; L'Aquila is its capital

fields.Name: Basilicata
fields.Info:
• A region of southern Italy in the “instep” of the boot, with mountain interiors and short coasts on the Tyrrhenian and Ionian seas
  • Matera's Sassi cave dwellings are a UNESCO site; Potenza is its capital

fields.Name: Calabria
fields.Info:
• A region at the “toe” of the Italian boot, between the Tyrrhenian and Ionian seas, separated from Sicily by the Strait of Messina
  • It is mountainous, including the Sila and Aspromonte massifs; Reggio Calabria lies on the strait

fields.Name: Campania
fields.Info:
• A region of southern Italy on the Tyrrhenian coast, including the Bay of Naples, Mount Vesuvius, and the Amalfi Coast
  • Naples is its capital; Pompeii, Herculaneum, and Capri are in it

fields.Name: Emilia-Romagna
fields.Info:
• A region of northern Italy in the Po plain, from the Apennines to the Adriatic coast, with the Via Emilia crossing it
  • Bologna is its capital; Ravenna's Byzantine mosaics and the Po delta are in it

fields.Name: Friuli Venezia Giulia
fields.Info:
• A region of northeastern Italy bordering Austria and Slovenia, between the Alps and the Adriatic, including the Gulf of Trieste
  • Trieste, on the Adriatic, is its largest city; the Carnic and Julian Alps rise in the north
fields.Photo caption: The abbey of San Gallo above the Fella, Moggio Udinese

fields.Name: Lazio
fields.Info:
• A region of central Italy on the Tyrrhenian Sea, around the Tiber, with Rome its capital and the Alban Hills nearby
  • Its coastline is flat, while the Apennines rise in the east

fields.Name: Liguria
fields.Info:
• A crescent-shaped region of northwestern Italy on the Ligurian Sea, between the Maritime Alps, the Apennines, and the sea, with the Italian Riviera
  • Genoa is its capital; the Cinque Terre villages are on its coast

fields.Name: Marche
fields.Info:
• A region of central Italy between the Apennines and the Adriatic Sea, with steep hills descending to a straight coast
  • The Conero peninsula, near Ancona, is a coastal cape; San Marino is enclaved nearby

fields.Name: Molise
fields.Info:
• A small region of southern Italy between the Apennines and the Adriatic, the newest and second-smallest region, split from Abruzzo in 1963
  • Campobasso is its capital; the Matese mountains rise on its border with Campania, and Termoli is its port

fields.Name: Piedmont
fields.Info:
• A region of northwestern Italy at the foot of the Alps, bordering France and Switzerland, with the upper Po basin, Monte Rosa, and the Gran Paradiso
  • Its name means “foot of the mountain”; Turin is its capital

fields.Name: Apulia
fields.Info:
• A region at the “heel” of Italy, on the Adriatic and Ionian seas, mostly flat with the Gargano peninsula and Salento
  • It is famed for olive groves, the trulli of Alberobello, and Castel del Monte; Bari is its capital

fields.Name: Trentino-South Tyrol
fields.Info:
• An autonomous region in northern Italy in the Dolomites and the eastern Alps, bordering Austria and Switzerland
  • It is made up of the provinces of Trentino and South Tyrol (Bolzano); the Brenner Pass crosses it
fields.Photo caption: The Zay valley below the Suldenferner and Königspitze

fields.Name: Umbria
fields.Info:
• A landlocked region of central Italy in the Apennines, along the upper Tiber, known as the “green heart of Italy”
  • Perugia and Assisi are its main cities; Lake Trasimeno is the largest lake in central Italy

fields.Name: Aosta Valley
fields.Info:
• The smallest region of Italy, in the northwest Alps, bordering France and Switzerland, with Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn on its border
  • It has its own French-speaking culture; Aosta is its capital and the Great St Bernard Pass crosses it

fields.Name: Veneto
fields.Info:
• A region of northeastern Italy from the Dolomites to the Adriatic, including the Venetian Lagoon and Lake Garda's eastern shore
  • Venice is its capital; the Po delta touches its south
fields.Photo caption: The Rialto Bridge on the Grand Canal, Venice

fields.Name: Alsace
fields.Info:
• A region of northeastern France on the west bank of the Rhine, bordering Germany and Switzerland, between the Rhine and the Vosges Mountains
  • Strasbourg is its largest city; the Alsace wine route runs along the Vosges foothills

fields.Name: Upper Normandy
fields.Info:
• A former region of northern France on the English Channel, around the lower Seine, with the chalk cliffs of the Alabaster Coast
  • Rouen, on the Seine, was its capital; Étretat and Le Havre are on its coast
fields.Photo caption: The Aiguille and Porte d'Aval, Étretat

fields.Name: Auvergne
fields.Info:
• A former region of central France in the Massif Central, with a chain of extinct volcanoes, the Chaîne des Puys
  • Puy de Dôme is a landmark; Clermont-Ferrand is its main city

fields.Name: Lower Normandy
fields.Info:
• A former region of northwestern France on the English Channel, with the Cotentin Peninsula and the D-Day beaches
  • Mont-Saint-Michel lies on its border with Brittany; Caen is its main city

fields.Name: Brittany
fields.Info:
• A region of northwestern France on a large peninsula between the English Channel and the Bay of Biscay
  • Its rocky coasts and Celtic culture are distinctive; Carnac's megaliths and the islands of Ouessant are in it

fields.Name: Centre-Val de Loire
fields.Info:
• A region of north-central France around the middle Loire River, known for its châteaux
  • Chambord, Chenonceau, and Chartres Cathedral are in it; Orléans is on the Loire

fields.Name: Champagne-Ardenne
fields.Info:
• A former region of northeastern France, on the Marne and Aube rivers, with the Ardennes highlands in the north
  • Reims and Épernay are its main champagne towns

fields.Name: Franche-Comté
fields.Info:
• A former region of eastern France on the Swiss border, in the Jura Mountains and the Saône valley
  • Besançon is its main city; the Doubs River loops around it

fields.Name: Île-de-France
fields.Info:
• A region in northern France, the country's most populous, around Paris, in the Paris Basin, bounded by the Seine, Marne, and Oise
  • Versailles and Fontainebleau are in it; its name means “island of France”
fields.Photo caption: Eiffel Tower from the Tour Montparnasse, Paris

fields.Name: Limousin
fields.Info:
• A former region of central France, in the western Massif Central, with the Millevaches plateau
  • Limoges is its capital, known for porcelain

fields.Name: Languedoc-Roussillon
fields.Info:
• A former region of southern France on the Mediterranean, between the Rhône delta and the Pyrenees
  • Its Canal du Midi and the walled city of Carcassonne are landmarks; Montpellier is its main city

fields.Name: Lorraine
fields.Info:
• A former region of northeastern France on the Belgian, Luxembourg, and German borders, along the Moselle and Meuse
  • Nancy and Metz are its main cities; the Vosges Mountains are to its southeast

fields.Name: Midi-Pyrénées
fields.Info:
• A former region of southwestern France, the country's largest by area, in the Garonne basin and reaching the Pyrenees
  • Toulouse is its main city; the Cirque de Gavarnie is in the Pyrenees

fields.Name: Nord-Pas-de-Calais
fields.Info:
• A former region of the far north of France on the North Sea and the Strait of Dover, bordering Belgium
  • Its coal-mining basin and the port of Calais are in it; Lille is its capital

fields.Name: Pays de la Loire
fields.Info:
• A region of western France along the lower Loire, on the Atlantic Ocean
  • Nantes is on the Loire; the Vendée coast and Anjou's châteaux are in it

fields.Name: Picardy
fields.Info:
• A former region of northern France north of Paris, in the Somme valley, with the English Channel coast
  • The Somme battlefields and Amiens Cathedral, the tallest complete cathedral in France, are here

fields.Name: Poitou-Charentes
fields.Info:
• A former region of western France on the Atlantic coast, north of Bordeaux, between the Loire and Gironde
  • Île de Ré, La Rochelle, and the Cognac vineyards are in it

fields.Name: Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
fields.Info:
• A region of southeastern France on the Mediterranean, bordering Italy, between the Rhône delta and the Alps
  • Marseille, Nice, and the Riviera are in it; Mont Ventoux and the Camargue are also here

fields.Name: Rhône-Alpes
fields.Info:
• A former region of southeastern France between the Rhône and the Alps, bordering Switzerland and Italy
  • Lyon is its capital; Mont Blanc and Chamonix are in it
fields.Photo caption: A TGV crossing the Cize–Bolozon viaduct

fields.Name: French Southern and Antarctic Lands
fields.Info:
• A French overseas territory made up of scattered islands in the southern Indian Ocean and Antarctica, including the Kerguelen, Crozet, and Amsterdam islands
  • It also includes Adélie Land, a claimed sector of Antarctica, and the Scattered Islands near Madagascar

fields.Name: Saint Barthélemy
fields.Info:
• A small French Caribbean island in the Leeward Islands, southeast of Saint Martin
  • Its harbour town Gustavia is a luxury resort; the island is volcanic with white beaches
fields.Photo caption: The island's coves, seen from the air

fields.Name: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
fields.Info:
• A French archipelago in the North Atlantic, about 25 km off the south coast of Newfoundland, Canada
  • Its islands include Saint-Pierre, Miquelon, and Langlade

fields.Name: Grand Est
fields.Info:
• A region of northeastern France formed in 2016 from Alsace, Lorraine, and Champagne-Ardenne, bordering Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, and Switzerland
  • Strasbourg is its capital; the Rhine, Moselle, and the Vosges are in it

fields.Name: Nouvelle-Aquitaine
fields.Info:
• The largest region of France by area, in the southwest, on the Atlantic coast, stretching from the Loire to the Pyrenees
  • Bordeaux is its capital; the Dune du Pilat and Saint-Émilion are in it

fields.Name: Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes
fields.Info:
• A region of southeastern France formed in 2016, combining Auvergne and Rhône-Alpes, in the Massif Central and the Alps
  • Lyon is its capital; Mont Blanc, the highest peak in the Alps, is in it
fields.Photo caption: Roc Cornafion seen from Côte 2000, Villard-de-Lans

fields.Name: Bourgogne-Franche-Comté
fields.Info:
• A region of eastern France formed in 2016 from Burgundy and Franche-Comté, in the Saône valley, between the Massif Central and the Jura
  • Dijon is its capital; Burgundy's vineyards lie along the Côte d'Or

fields.Name: Occitania
fields.Info:
• A region of southern France formed in 2016 from Languedoc-Roussillon and Midi-Pyrénées, between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean, bordering Spain and Andorra
  • Toulouse is its capital; the Pyrenees, the Cévennes, and the Canal du Midi are in it

fields.Name: Hauts-de-France
fields.Info:
• A region in the far north of France formed in 2016 from Nord-Pas-de-Calais and Picardy, on the North Sea and the English Channel, bordering Belgium
  • Lille is its capital; the Somme and the Channel Tunnel entrance at Calais are in it

fields.Name: Clipperton Island
fields.Info:
• An uninhabited coral atoll in the eastern Pacific, about 1,100 km southwest of Mexico, a French possession
  • A ring of coral encloses a stagnant, brackish lagoon; Clipperton Rock, an old volcanic outcrop, is its highest point
fields.Photo caption: Clipperton atoll and its enclosed lagoon, from orbit

fields.Name: Baden-Württemberg
fields.Info:
• A state in southwestern Germany, bordering France and Switzerland, containing the Black Forest and the source of the Danube
  • Lake Constance forms its southern border; Stuttgart is its capital, on the Neckar

fields.Name: Berlin
fields.Info:
• Germany's capital and a city-state, surrounded entirely by Brandenburg, on the Spree and Havel rivers in the northeast
  • Its Brandenburg Gate and Museum Island are landmarks; the Tiergarten and Grunewald forest lie within the city
fields.Photo caption: The city from the Victory Column

fields.Name: Bremen
fields.Info:
• A city-state of northwestern Germany on the Weser River, made up of the cities Bremen and Bremerhaven, about 60 km from the North Sea
  • It is surrounded by Lower Saxony; its town musicians and Roland statue are famous

fields.Name: Hamburg
fields.Info:
• A city-state of northern Germany on the Elbe River, about 100 km from the North Sea, Germany's largest port
  • Its Speicherstadt warehouses and Elbphilharmonie are landmarks; the Alster lakes lie in its centre
fields.Photo caption: From the tower of St. Nikolai

fields.Name: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
fields.Info:
• A state in northeastern Germany on the Baltic coast, bordering Poland, with thousands of lakes in the Mecklenburg Lake District
  • Its islands include Rügen, Germany's largest, and Usedom; the capital is Schwerin
fields.Photo caption: Schwerin Palace on its island in Lake Schwerin, from the air

fields.Name: Lower Saxony
fields.Info:
• A state in northwestern Germany, the second-largest by area, with a North Sea coast, the Lüneburg Heath, and the Harz Mountains
  • Its capital is Hanover; the Frisian Islands and Wadden Sea are on its coast

fields.Name: North Rhine-Westphalia
fields.Info:
• The most populous state of Germany, in the west, bordering the Netherlands and Belgium, on the Rhine and Ruhr
  • It includes the Ruhr industrial area; Düsseldorf is its capital and Cologne its largest city

fields.Name: Rhineland-Palatinate
fields.Info:
• A state in western Germany bordering France, Luxembourg, and Belgium, on the Rhine and Moselle rivers
  • The Rhine Gorge and Moselle wine valleys are UNESCO sites; Mainz is its capital
fields.Photo caption: The Rhine Gorge from the Loreley

fields.Name: Saarland
fields.Info:
• The smallest non-city state of Germany, in the southwest, bordering France and Luxembourg, along the Saar River
  • Its economy grew from the Saar coalfield and steelworks; the Saar makes a large loop at Mettlach

fields.Name: Saxony-Anhalt
fields.Info:
• A state in east-central Germany, on the middle Elbe River, extending to the Harz Mountains
  • Its capital is Magdeburg; Dessau's Bauhaus building and Wittenberg, where Martin Luther posted his theses, lie in it

fields.Name: Schleswig-Holstein
fields.Info:
• Germany's northernmost state, on the Jutland peninsula between the North Sea and the Baltic Sea, bordering Denmark
  • The Kiel Canal crosses it; the North Frisian Islands, including Sylt, lie off its west coast

fields.Name: Thuringia
fields.Info:
• A state in central Germany called the “green heart of Germany” for its forests; the Thuringian Forest crosses its south
  • Its capital Erfurt and the Wartburg castle near Eisenach are landmarks; Weimar is in it
fields.Photo caption: Erfurt Cathedral and the Church of St Severus

fields.Name: Brandenburg
fields.Info:
• A state in northeastern Germany surrounding Berlin, bordering Poland along the Oder and Neisse rivers, with many lakes and pine forests
  • Its capital Potsdam has the palaces of Sanssouci; the Spreewald is a wetland area

fields.Name: Hesse
fields.Info:
• A state in central-western Germany, on the Main and Rhine, with the Taunus and Rhön hills
  • Frankfurt, its largest city, is Germany's financial centre; Wiesbaden is the capital

fields.Name: Württemberg-Baden
fields.Info:
• A former state in the American occupation zone of southwestern Germany, formed in 1945 from northern Württemberg and northern Baden
  • It merged with South Baden and Württemberg-Hohenzollern in 1952 to form Baden-Württemberg; Stuttgart was its capital

fields.Name: South Baden
fields.Info:
• A former state in the French occupation zone of southwestern Germany, formed in 1947 from the southern part of Baden along the Rhine, bordering Switzerland
  • It merged with two other states in 1952 to form Baden-Württemberg; its capital was Freiburg im Breisgau

fields.Name: Württemberg-Hohenzollern
fields.Info:
• A former state in the French occupation zone of southwestern Germany, formed in 1947 from southern Württemberg and Hohenzollern
  • It merged into Baden-Württemberg in 1952; its capital was Tübingen

fields.Name: Australian Capital Territory
fields.Info:
• A small federal territory in southeastern Australia, an enclave within New South Wales, on the Molonglo River, about 280 km southwest of Sydney
  • Canberra, the capital, is built around the artificial Lake Burley Griffin

fields.Name: New South Wales
fields.Info:
• Australia's most populous state, on the southeastern coast, from the Pacific coast across the Great Dividing Range to the western plains
  • The Blue Mountains and the Snowy Mountains are in it; the Murray River forms its southern border

fields.Name: Northern Territory
fields.Info:
• A territory in north-central Australia, from Arnhem Land on the Timor and Arafura seas to the red centre
  • Uluru and Kata Tjuta, Kakadu National Park, and Darwin, on the Timor Sea, are in it

fields.Name: Queensland
fields.Info:
• The second-largest Australian state, in the northeast, with the tropical Cape York Peninsula and the Great Barrier Reef along its Coral Sea coast
  • The Great Dividing Range runs parallel to its coast; Brisbane, its capital, lies in the southeast

fields.Name: South Australia
fields.Info:
• A state in south-central Australia, on the Great Australian Bight, mostly arid, with Lake Eyre in the north
  • Adelaide is on the Gulf St Vincent; the Flinders Ranges and Kangaroo Island are in it
fields.Photo caption: Rawnsley Bluff in the Flinders Ranges

fields.Name: Victoria
fields.Info:
• The smallest mainland state of Australia, in the southeast, on Bass Strait, with the Great Dividing Range and the Murray River on its northern border
  • Melbourne is its capital; the Great Ocean Road follows its southwest coast

fields.Name: Western Australia
fields.Info:
• The largest Australian state, occupying the western third of the continent, from the Indian Ocean coast to the Great Sandy and Great Victoria deserts
  • Perth is its capital; the Pilbara, Kimberley, and Nullarbor Plain are in it
fields.Photo caption: Gales Bay, Exmouth Gulf, from the air

fields.Name: Christmas Island
fields.Info:
• An Australian territory in the Indian Ocean, about 350 km south of Java, a plateau ringed by cliffs and coral reefs
  • The annual red crab migration to the sea is famous
fields.Photo caption: Flying Fish Cove, the island's settlement

fields.Name: Ashmore and Cartier Islands
fields.Info:
• An uninhabited Australian territory of small islands and reefs in the Timor Sea, off northwestern Australia
  • They are a nature reserve on the edge of the continental shelf

fields.Name: Australian Antarctic Territory
fields.Info:
• The sector of Antarctica claimed by Australia, covering about 42 percent of the continent, between 45° E and 160° E, excluding Adélie Land
  • Mawson, Davis, and Casey are Australian research stations; the claim is suspended under the Antarctic Treaty

fields.Name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
fields.Info:
• An Australian territory of two coral atolls in the Indian Ocean, about midway between Australia and Sri Lanka
  • The Cocos Malay community lives on Home Island; West Island has the airstrip

fields.Name: Coral Sea Islands
fields.Info:
• An Australian territory of tiny reefs and islets in the Coral Sea, east of the Great Barrier Reef
  • It includes cays such as Willis Island, which hosts a weather station
fields.Photo caption: Willis Island and its weather station from the air

fields.Name: Heard Island and McDonald Islands
fields.Info:
• An Australian territory of uninhabited volcanic islands in the southern Indian Ocean, about 4,000 km southwest of Perth
  • Mawson Peak on Big Ben, the volcano on Heard, is Australia's highest peak
fields.Photo caption: Big Ben, the volcano on Heard Island

fields.Name: Jervis Bay Territory
fields.Info:
• A small Australian territory on the coast of New South Wales, on Jervis Bay, which serves as the naval base and the seaport for Canberra
  • Booderee National Park covers most of it
fields.Photo caption: Booderee National Park and Botanic Gardens

fields.Name: Norfolk Island
fields.Info:
• An Australian territory in the Pacific between Australia, New Zealand, and New Caledonia, with tall Norfolk Island pines
  • Kingston's colonial ruins are a UNESCO site; the island is about 8 km long

fields.Name: Ontario
fields.Info:
• The most populous province of Canada, in the centre-east, bordering the Great Lakes and the Canadian Shield
  • Toronto is its capital; Niagara Falls, Hudson Bay's southern coast, and Ottawa, the national capital, are in it
fields.Photo caption: Algonquin Park in autumn, from the Cache Lake lookout

fields.Name: Quebec
fields.Info:
• The largest province of Canada by area, in the east, from the Saint Lawrence Valley north to Hudson Bay and Ungava Bay
  • The Saint Lawrence River runs through its populated south; Quebec City and Montreal are its main cities

fields.Name: Nova Scotia
fields.Info:
• A Canadian province on the Atlantic coast, almost an island, made up of a peninsula and Cape Breton Island, joined to New Brunswick by the Isthmus of Chignecto
  • It borders the Bay of Fundy; Halifax's harbour and the Cabot Trail are in it

fields.Name: New Brunswick
fields.Info:
• A Canadian province on the Atlantic coast, bordering Maine and Quebec, on the Bay of Fundy and the Gulf of Saint Lawrence
  • The Saint John River flows through it; the Hopewell Rocks are its landmark

fields.Name: Manitoba
fields.Info:
• A Canadian prairie province at the geographic centre of North America, from the US border to Hudson Bay
  • Lake Winnipeg, Lake Manitoba, and Churchill, on Hudson Bay, are in it
fields.Photo caption: Canadian Museum for Human Rights, Winnipeg

fields.Name: Prince Edward Island
fields.Info:
• Canada's smallest province, an island in the Gulf of Saint Lawrence, with red sandy soil and a mostly flat landscape
  • The Confederation Bridge links it to New Brunswick; Charlottetown is its capital

fields.Name: Saskatchewan
fields.Info:
• A Canadian prairie province between Alberta and Manitoba, with the Athabasca Basin in the north
  • The Saskatchewan River crosses it; Regina and Saskatoon are its main cities
fields.Photo caption: Canola and flax fields on the prairie

fields.Name: Alberta
fields.Info:
• A Canadian province between British Columbia and Saskatchewan, from the Rocky Mountains to the prairies
  • Banff and Jasper national parks, the oil sands near Fort McMurray, and Edmonton are in it
fields.Photo caption: Lake Louise, Banff National Park, Alberta

fields.Name: Northwest Territories
fields.Info:
• A Canadian territory in the northwest, from the Mackenzie Valley to the Arctic Ocean, with Great Slave Lake and Great Bear Lake
  • Yellowknife, on Great Slave Lake, is its capital
fields.Photo caption: Third Canyon on the Nahanni River

fields.Name: Nunavut
fields.Info:
• Canada's largest and northernmost territory, in the Arctic, including most of the Arctic Archipelago, Baffin Island, and the west coast of Hudson Bay
  • Iqaluit, on Baffin Island, is its capital; most of it lies north of the Arctic Circle
fields.Photo caption: A glacier reaching the sea on Baffin Island's northeast coast

fields.Name: British Columbia
fields.Info:
• Canada's westernmost province, on the Pacific, between the Rockies and the coast, with Vancouver Island and the Coast Mountains
  • Victoria, on Vancouver Island, is its capital; Vancouver is its largest city

fields.Name: Acre
fields.Info:
• A state in the far west of Brazil in the Amazon, bordering Peru and Bolivia, mostly rainforest
  • The Acre and Purus rivers drain it; it is part of the region known as the Amazon's “arc of deforestation”
fields.Photo caption: The Palácio Rio Branco, seat of the state government, in Rio Branco

fields.Name: Bahia
fields.Info:
• A large state on Brazil's northeastern Atlantic coast, with a long coastline and the São Francisco River in the west
  • Salvador, its capital, lies on All Saints' Bay; the Chapada Diamantina is in it
fields.Photo caption: Chapada Diamantina from Morro do Pai Inácio

fields.Name: Maranhão
fields.Info:
• A state in northeastern Brazil on the Atlantic, at the edge of the Amazon, with the Lençóis Maranhenses dunes
  • São Luís, its capital, is on an island; the Parnaíba River forms its eastern border
fields.Photo caption: Rainwater pools among the dunes of Lençóis Maranhenses

fields.Name: Minas Gerais
fields.Info:
• A large state in southeastern Brazil, inland, on the highlands of the Brazilian Plateau, with the São Francisco River and its many mines
  • Ouro Preto is a baroque mining town; Belo Horizonte is its capital

fields.Name: Rio de Janeiro
fields.Info:
• A state in southeastern Brazil on the Atlantic coast, with the Serra do Mar mountains close to the sea and the bay of Guanabara
  • Its capital of the same name has Sugarloaf Mountain and Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado

fields.Name: São Paulo
fields.Info:
• Brazil's most populous state, in the southeast, on the Atlantic coast and on the Paraná River basin
  • The city of São Paulo is on a plateau above the Serra do Mar; Santos is South America's busiest port

fields.Name: Paraná
fields.Info:
• A state in southern Brazil, between the Atlantic and the Paraná River, bordering Paraguay and Argentina
  • Iguazu Falls and the Itaipú Dam are in the west; Curitiba is its capital
fields.Photo caption: Pico Paraná, the highest peak, from Caratuva

fields.Name: Catalonia
fields.Info:
• An autonomous community in northeastern Spain on the Mediterranean, bordered by France and Andorra, with the Pyrenees to the north
  • Its Costa Brava and Montserrat are well-known; the Ebro River enters the sea in its south

fields.Name: Basque Country
fields.Info:
• An autonomous community of northern Spain on the Bay of Biscay, at the western end of the Pyrenees, bordering France
  • Bilbao, on the Nervión River, holds the Guggenheim Museum, and San Sebastián has La Concha beach

fields.Name: Aragon
fields.Info:
• An autonomous community of northeastern Spain, with the Pyrenees in the north and the central Ebro valley
  • The Ebro flows through Zaragoza; Aneto, the highest peak of the Pyrenees, rises in its north

fields.Name: Asturias
fields.Info:
• An autonomous community on Spain's north coast on the Bay of Biscay, backed by the Cantabrian Mountains and the Picos de Europa
  • Its rainy, green coast is part of “Green Spain”, and it is known for its cider
fields.Photo caption: Basilica of Covadonga, Picos de Europa

fields.Name: Balearic Islands
fields.Info:
• An autonomous archipelago in the western Mediterranean off Spain's east coast, made up of Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza, and Formentera
  • The Serra de Tramuntana range is on Mallorca; Palma is the capital
fields.Photo caption: Cala Barques, on the Mallorca coast

fields.Name: Navarre
fields.Info:
• An autonomous community of northern Spain bordering France, in the western Pyrenees, with the Ebro basin in the south
  • Pamplona, on the Arga River, is known for the Running of the Bulls; the Pass of Roncesvalles is in its north

fields.Name: Ceuta
fields.Info:
• A Spanish autonomous city on the north coast of Morocco, on the Strait of Gibraltar, one of Spain's two North African exclaves
  • It stands on a peninsula and faces Gibraltar; Monte Hacho is its landmark hill
fields.Photo caption: Ceuta from the Isabel II viewpoint

fields.Name: Hokkaido
fields.Info:
• The northernmost and second-largest main island of Japan, north of Honshu across the Tsugaru Strait, with a cold climate and volcanic mountains
  • Sapporo is its capital; the Seikan Tunnel links it to Honshu, and the Ainu are its indigenous people

fields.Name: Miyagi Prefecture
fields.Info:
• A prefecture on the Pacific coast of northern Honshu, in the Tōhoku region, with the island-filled Matsushima Bay
  • Sendai is its capital; the 2011 tsunami struck its coast
fields.Photo caption: Matsushima Bay from Saigyō Modoshi no Matsu Park

fields.Name: Tokyo
fields.Info:
• Japan's capital metropolis, on Tokyo Bay on the Kantō Plain of eastern Honshu, including the Izu and Ogasawara island chains
  • The Sumida and Tama rivers cross it; the Imperial Palace occupies the former Edo Castle
fields.Photo caption: Shinjuku skyscrapers, with Mount Fuji behind

fields.Name: Dagestan
fields.Info:
• A republic on the western shore of the Caspian Sea in the North Caucasus, bordering Azerbaijan and Georgia, with the Greater Caucasus in the south
  • Derbent, on its coast, is one of Russia's oldest cities; it has dozens of languages

fields.Name: Karelia
fields.Info:
• A republic of northwestern Russia bordering Finland, between the White Sea and lakes Ladoga and Onega
  • It is a land of forests and lakes; Kizhi island's wooden churches and the Valaam Monastery are landmarks

fields.Name: Chechnya
fields.Info:
• A republic of the North Caucasus in southern Russia, bordering Georgia, on the northern slopes of the Greater Caucasus
  • Its lowlands are along the Terek River; the Argun Gorge cuts the mountains

fields.Name: Moscow
fields.Info:
• Russia's capital and largest city, on the Moskva River in the centre of the East European Plain, around the Kremlin
  • The ring roads and the Moscow Metro serve it; the Volga–Moscow Canal links it to the Volga

fields.Name: Saint Petersburg
fields.Info:
• A port city at the mouth of the Neva River on the Gulf of Finland, built on islands and canals on Peter the Great's orders
  • The Hermitage, Nevsky Prospekt, and the Peter and Paul Fortress are landmarks; it was the imperial capital until 1918

fields.Name: Aceh
fields.Info:
• A special region at the northern tip of Sumatra in Indonesia, at the entrance to the Strait of Malacca
  • The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami devastated it; Banda Aceh is its capital

fields.Name: Jakarta
fields.Info:
• Indonesia's capital, a special region on the northwest coast of Java, on Jakarta Bay at the mouth of the Ciliwung River
  • It is sinking as groundwater is pumped and floods often, which is why the capital is being moved to Nusantara

fields.Name: Kalimantan
fields.Info:
• The Indonesian part of the island of Borneo, made up of five provinces, with large rainforests, rivers, and coal mines
  • The Kapuas and Mahakam rivers flow through it; the Muller and Schwaner mountains are in its centre

fields.Name: Kyoto
fields.Info:
• Lies in a basin on the island of Honshu, ringed by mountains on three sides, with the Kamo and Katsura rivers flowing through it
  • Japan's capital from 794 until 1868; its Kiyomizu-dera, Kinkaku-ji, and Fushimi Inari shrine are landmarks

fields.Name: Osaka
fields.Info:
• Japan's third-largest city, a port on Osaka Bay at the mouth of the Yodo River on Honshu
  • Known for its canals and Osaka Castle; it forms the Keihanshin metropolitan area with Kyoto and Kobe

fields.Name: Xi'an
fields.Info:
• Lies on the Wei River plain in central China's Shaanxi Province, an eastern end of the Silk Road, protected by the Qinling Mountains to the south
  • Site of the Terracotta Army near Mount Li, and a Ming-era city wall

fields.Name: Guangzhou
fields.Info:
• A port on the Pearl River in southern China, near the Pearl River Delta, about 120 km from Hong Kong
  • Once known to Europeans as Canton; it hosts the Canton Fair

fields.Name: Mumbai
fields.Info:
• Built on a group of islands on the Konkan coast of western India, facing the Arabian Sea and joined into a single peninsula through land reclamation
  • India's financial centre; it has the Gateway of India and Elephanta Caves in its harbour
fields.Photo caption: The Taj Mahal Palace hotel and the Gateway of India

fields.Name: Kolkata
fields.Info:
• A port on the Hooghly River, a distributary of the Ganges, in the delta of eastern India
  • Once the capital of British India; the Howrah Bridge crosses the Hooghly here

fields.Name: Varanasi
fields.Info:
• A city on the left bank of the Ganges in northern India, known for its ghats, steps leading down to the river
  • One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities and a holy Hindu city; Sarnath, where the Buddha preached, is nearby
fields.Photo caption: The ghats seen from the Ganges

fields.Name: Jaipur
fields.Info:
• The capital of Rajasthan, in northwestern India on the edge of the Thar Desert, surrounded by the Aravalli hills
  • Called the Pink City for its buildings; the Amber Fort and Hawa Mahal are landmarks

fields.Name: Karachi
fields.Info:
• Pakistan's largest city, a port on the Arabian Sea near the mouth of the Indus
  • Its harbour is sheltered by Manora Island; it was Pakistan's capital until 1959

fields.Name: Lahore
fields.Info:
• A city in Punjab in eastern Pakistan, on the Ravi River near the Indian border at Wagah
  • Site of the Lahore Fort and Badshahi Mosque, and once a Mughal capital

fields.Name: Isfahan
fields.Info:
• An oasis city on the Zayandeh River on the central Iranian plateau, at the foot of the Zagros Mountains
  • Famous for Naqsh-e Jahan Square and the Si-o-se-pol bridge; a capital of Safavid Persia
fields.Photo caption: Shah Mosque and Naqsh-e Jahan Square

fields.Name: Shiraz
fields.Info:
• A city in the Zagros Mountains of southwestern Iran, about 55 km from Persepolis
  • Known for its gardens and the tombs of the poets Hafez and Saadi; the Nasir al-Mulk Mosque is a landmark

fields.Name: Samarkand
fields.Info:
• A city on the Silk Road in southeastern Uzbekistan, in the fertile Zeravshan River valley
  • Its Registan square is framed by three madrasas; the Gur-e-Amir mausoleum and the Shah-i-Zinda necropolis are landmarks

fields.Name: Bukhara
fields.Info:
• An oasis city on the Silk Road in southern Uzbekistan, on the Zeravshan River delta at the edge of the Kyzylkum Desert
  • Its Kalyan Minaret and Ark fortress are landmarks; it was a centre of Islamic learning
fields.Photo caption: The Kalyan Minaret and the Po-i-Kalyan complex

fields.Name: Aleppo
fields.Info:
• A city in northern Syria on the Queiq River, between the Euphrates and the Mediterranean, at the western end of Silk Road routes
  • Its Citadel and covered souks are landmarks; it is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities

fields.Name: Petra
fields.Info:
• An ancient city in southern Jordan carved into rose-red cliffs, in a valley of the Wadi Musa near the Dead Sea–Aqaba rift
  • The capital of the Nabataeans, entered via a narrow gorge called the Siq; its Treasury (Al-Khazneh) is famous

fields.Name: Jerusalem
fields.Info:
• A city in the Judean Mountains between the Mediterranean and the Dead Sea, holy to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam
  • The Old City contains the Western Wall, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, and the Dome of the Rock; its status is disputed
fields.Photo caption: Dome of the Rock seen from the Mount of Olives

fields.Name: Mecca
fields.Info:
• A city in the Hejaz region of western Saudi Arabia, in a narrow desert valley about 70 km inland from the Red Sea
  • The holiest city of Islam, it holds the Kaaba in the Masjid al-Haram; non-Muslims may not enter

fields.Name: Medina
fields.Info:
• A city in the Hejaz of western Saudi Arabia, in an oasis about 210 km inland from the Red Sea
  • The second-holiest city of Islam, with the Prophet's Mosque containing the tomb of Muhammad

fields.Name: Dubai
fields.Info:
• The largest city of the United Arab Emirates, on the southeast coast of the Persian Gulf, on a flat desert plain at the mouth of Dubai Creek
  • Home of the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, and the artificial Palm Jumeirah
fields.Photo caption: Downtown and the Burj Khalifa from the air

fields.Name: Lhasa
fields.Info:
• The capital of Tibet, at about 3,650 m on the Lhasa River in the Tibetan Plateau, one of the highest major cities on Earth
  • The Potala Palace and Jokhang Temple are its landmarks

fields.Name: Vladivostok
fields.Info:
• A port on the Sea of Japan at the Golden Horn Bay, near the Chinese and North Korean borders in Russia's Far East
  • The eastern terminus of the Trans-Siberian Railway; the Russky Bridge links it to Russky Island

fields.Name: Novosibirsk
fields.Info:
• Russia's largest city in Siberia, on the Ob River, where the Trans-Siberian Railway crosses the river
  • Its Akademgorodok science centre lies on the Ob Sea reservoir

fields.Name: Ho Chi Minh City
fields.Info:
• Vietnam's largest city, on the Saigon River in the Mekong Delta region of southern Vietnam
  • Formerly called Saigon; its landmarks include Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica and the Ben Thanh Market

fields.Name: Angkor
fields.Info:
• The site of the Khmer Empire's capital, north of the Tonlé Sap lake in northwestern Cambodia near Siem Reap
  • Its temples, including Angkor Wat, Bayon, and Ta Prohm, form the world's largest religious monument complex
fields.Photo caption: Angkor Wat at sunrise, reflected in the pool before the west entrance

fields.Name: Kandy
fields.Info:
• A city in the central hills of Sri Lanka, at about 500 m on the shores of an artificial lake
  • The Temple of the Tooth Relic is its landmark; it was the last capital of the Sinhalese kings

fields.Name: Busan
fields.Info:
• South Korea's second-largest city and its largest port, on the southeastern tip of the Korean Peninsula at the mouth of the Nakdong River
  • Faces the Korea Strait toward Japan's Tsushima Island; Haeundae is its famous beach
fields.Photo caption: The observation tower in Yongdusan Park

fields.Name: Hiroshima
fields.Info:
• A city on the Ōta River delta on the Seto Inland Sea coast of Honshu
  • Its Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome) commemorates the atomic bombing of 1945; Itsukushima Shrine's torii on Miyajima is nearby
fields.Photo caption: The Atomic Bomb Dome beside the Motoyasu River

fields.Name: Nara
fields.Info:
• A city in the Nara Basin of central Honshu, at the foot of low hills, near Kyoto and Osaka
  • Home of Tōdai-ji, with the Great Buddha, and Kasuga Shrine; its deer roam Nara Park

fields.Name: Chennai
fields.Info:
• A port city on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal in southeast India
  • Its Marina Beach is one of the world's longest urban beaches; formerly known as Madras

fields.Name: Barcelona
fields.Info:
• A port on the Mediterranean coast of northeastern Spain, between the Llobregat and Besòs river deltas and the Collserola hills
  • The city of Antoni Gaudí, with the Sagrada Família and Park Güell; Montjuïc hill rises above its harbour
fields.Photo caption: The Eixample grid, with the Torre Glòries

fields.Name: Seville
fields.Info:
• The largest city of southern Spain, on the Guadalquivir River, about 80 km from the Atlantic
  • Its Giralda tower, cathedral, and Real Alcázar are landmarks; it is a river port

fields.Name: Granada
fields.Info:
• A city in southern Spain at the foot of the Sierra Nevada, at the meeting of the Darro and Genil rivers
  • The Alhambra palace stands on a hill overlooking the city
fields.Photo caption: The Alhambra, with the Sierra Nevada behind

fields.Name: Milan
fields.Info:
• Italy's financial centre, on the Po Plain in Lombardy, between the Ticino and Adda rivers
  • Its Duomo is one of the largest Gothic cathedrals; the Navigli canals were once its waterways
fields.Photo caption: The cathedral and the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II

fields.Name: Venice
fields.Info:
• A city built on more than 100 small islands in the Venetian Lagoon on the northwest Adriatic coast, linked by canals and bridges
  • The Grand Canal, Rialto Bridge, and Saint Mark's Square are landmarks; it is sinking and floods at high tide (acqua alta)

fields.Name: Florence
fields.Info:
• A city on the Arno River in Tuscany, in central Italy, in a basin between the Apennines
  • The Duomo, Ponte Vecchio, and Uffizi are landmarks

fields.Name: Naples
fields.Info:
• A port on the Bay of Naples in southern Italy, in the shadow of Mount Vesuvius
  • Its historic centre is a UNESCO site; the islands of Capri and Ischia lie in the bay

fields.Name: Turin
fields.Info:
• A city on the upper Po River in northwestern Italy, at the foot of the Alps
  • The home of Fiat and the centre of Italy's car industry; its Mole Antonelliana is a landmark

fields.Name: Pisa
fields.Info:
• A city on the Arno River near the Ligurian Sea coast in Tuscany, about 10 km from the sea
  • Its Piazza dei Miracoli holds the Leaning Tower, the cathedral, and the baptistery

fields.Name: Munich
fields.Info:
• The largest city of Bavaria, on the Isar River on a high plateau north of the Alps in southern Germany
  • Its Marienplatz, Frauenkirche, and Englischer Garten are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: The Frauenkirche and the New Town Hall above the old town

fields.Name: Cologne
fields.Info:
• A city on the Rhine River in western Germany, in the Rhineland
  • Its Gothic cathedral, begun in 1248 and finished in 1880, dominates the skyline
fields.Photo caption: The cathedral and the Hohenzollern Bridge over the Rhine

fields.Name: Frankfurt
fields.Info:
• A city on the Main River in Hesse, central Germany, near the confluence with the Rhine
  • Germany's financial centre; its airport is a major hub and Römerberg its old town square
fields.Photo caption: The old town, with the skyline behind

fields.Name: Dresden
fields.Info:
• A city on the Elbe River in eastern Germany, in a valley between the Ore Mountains and Saxon Switzerland
  • Its Frauenkirche and Zwinger palace are landmarks; the city was heavily bombed in 1945

fields.Name: Marseille
fields.Info:
• France's largest Mediterranean port, on the Gulf of Lion, east of the Rhône delta
  • The Vieux-Port, the Notre-Dame de la Garde basilica and the Calanques are its landmarks

fields.Name: Lyon
fields.Info:
• A city at the confluence of the Rhône and Saône rivers in east-central France
  • Its Fourvière hill holds a basilica and Roman theatres; it is known for its gastronomy

fields.Name: Bordeaux
fields.Info:
• A port on the Garonne River in southwestern France, about 100 km from the Atlantic
  • The centre of a major wine region, with the Pont de Pierre bridging the Garonne
fields.Photo caption: Place de la Bourse and the Miroir d'eau

fields.Name: Strasbourg
fields.Info:
• A city on the Rhine in Alsace, France, on the border with Germany
  • Its cathedral, with a single Gothic spire, and the European Parliament seat are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: The Ponts Couverts, with the cathedral spire behind

fields.Name: Manchester
fields.Info:
• A city in northwest England at the foot of the Pennines, on the River Irwell
  • The world's first industrial city; the Manchester Ship Canal (1894) made it an inland port

fields.Name: Liverpool
fields.Info:
• A port on the estuary of the River Mersey in northwest England, facing the Irish Sea
  • Its Albert Dock and Royal Liver Building are landmarks on the waterfront

fields.Name: Oxford
fields.Info:
• A university city at the confluence of the Thames (called the Isis locally) and the Cherwell in southern England
  • Known for its “dreaming spires” and the Radcliffe Camera

fields.Name: Cambridge
fields.Info:
• A university city on the River Cam in eastern England, on the southern edge of the Fens
  • King's College Chapel and the “Backs”, the college lawns along the river, are landmarks; punts ply the Cam

fields.Name: Edinburgh
fields.Info:
• Scotland's capital, on the Firth of Forth on the east coast, built on volcanic crags including Arthur's Seat
  • Its Castle Rock and the Royal Mile link the castle and Holyrood Palace

fields.Name: Glasgow
fields.Info:
• Scotland's largest city, on the River Clyde in the Central Lowlands
  • Shipyards once lined the Clyde; the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum and Glasgow Cathedral are landmarks

fields.Name: Rotterdam
fields.Info:
• Europe's largest port, on the Nieuwe Maas in the Rhine–Meuse delta of the Netherlands, near the North Sea
  • Its Erasmus Bridge and Cube Houses are landmarks; it was rebuilt after bombing in 1940
fields.Photo caption: Erasmus Bridge over the Nieuwe Maas

fields.Name: Antwerp
fields.Info:
• A port on the Scheldt River in northern Belgium, about 80 km from the North Sea
  • A diamond-trading centre; its Cathedral of Our Lady and Grote Markt are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: The city from the Museum aan de Stroom rooftop

fields.Name: Bruges
fields.Info:
• A medieval city in northwestern Belgium in West Flanders, criss-crossed by canals and linked to the sea at Zeebrugge
  • Its Belfry and old town are UNESCO sites

fields.Name: Ghent
fields.Info:
• A city in Flanders, Belgium, at the confluence of the Scheldt and the Lys rivers
  • Its Gravensteen castle and the Ghent Altarpiece in Saint Bavo's Cathedral are landmarks

fields.Name: Salzburg
fields.Info:
• A city on the Salzach River in northern Austria at the edge of the Alps, near the German border
  • Its Hohensalzburg Fortress dominates; the birthplace of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
fields.Photo caption: The old town beneath the Hohensalzburg fortress

fields.Name: Krakow
fields.Info:
• A city on the Vistula River in southern Poland, at the foot of the Carpathian foothills
  • Its Wawel Castle and Main Market Square are landmarks; it was Poland's capital until 1596
fields.Photo caption: Wawel Castle and Cathedral above the Vistula, Kraków

fields.Name: Gdansk
fields.Info:
• A port on the Baltic Sea at the mouth of the Vistula in northern Poland
  • The historic Hanseatic city has the Long Market and Neptune's Fountain; the Free City of Danzig from 1920 to 1939
fields.Photo caption: The medieval crane on the Motława, Gdańsk

fields.Name: Thessaloniki
fields.Info:
• A port on the Thermaic Gulf of the Aegean in northern Greece, the country's second-largest city
  • Its White Tower and Roman Rotunda are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: The White Tower and the seafront

fields.Name: Porto
fields.Info:
• A port on the Douro River near its Atlantic mouth in northern Portugal
  • The Dom Luís I Bridge spans the Douro; port wine ages in cellars at Vila Nova de Gaia
fields.Photo caption: The Ribeira district on the Douro

fields.Name: Gothenburg
fields.Info:
• Sweden's main port, on the Kattegat coast at the mouth of the Göta älv river on the west coast
  • Its harbour and canals were designed by Dutch engineers; the Gothenburg archipelago lies offshore
fields.Photo caption: Stora Hamnkanalen and the German Church (Christinae kyrka)

fields.Name: Bergen
fields.Info:
• A port on Norway's west coast, surrounded by seven mountains and reached by the Bergen Railway
  • Its wooden Bryggen wharf is a UNESCO site; it is a gateway to the western fjords

fields.Name: Nizhny Novgorod
fields.Info:
• A city at the confluence of the Oka and Volga rivers in central Russia
  • Its Kremlin stands on a bluff above the confluence; it hosted a famous trade fair

fields.Name: Kazan
fields.Info:
• A city on the Volga at the confluence with the Kazanka river in Russia, the capital of Tatarstan
  • Its Kazan Kremlin includes the Kul Sharif Mosque

fields.Name: Lviv
fields.Info:
• A city in western Ukraine near the Polish border, on the watershed between the Baltic and Black Sea basins
  • Its historic centre is UNESCO-listed; it was known as Lemberg under Austria and Lwów under Poland

fields.Name: Odesa
fields.Info:
• A port on the Black Sea coast of southern Ukraine, on a bay between the Dniester and Dnieper estuaries
  • Its Potemkin Stairs and opera house are landmarks

fields.Name: Cork
fields.Info:
• Ireland's second-largest city, on the River Lee, which splits around an island in the centre
  • Its harbour is one of the largest natural harbours in the world; Blarney Castle is nearby

fields.Name: Geneva
fields.Info:
• A city at the western end of Lake Geneva in Switzerland, where the Rhône exits the lake, near the French border
  • Its Jet d'Eau fountain is a landmark; it hosts the UN's European headquarters and the Red Cross

fields.Name: Zurich
fields.Info:
• Switzerland's largest city, at the northern end of Lake Zurich where the Limmat River flows out
  • It is a financial centre; the Grossmünster and Fraumünster are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: Zunfthaus zur Meisen, Münsterbrücke, and St. Peter's Church, Zürich

fields.Name: Basel
fields.Info:
• A city on the Rhine on Switzerland's border with France and Germany, where the river turns north
  • Its Münster and its Rhine river ferries are landmarks; it has many art museums

fields.Name: Alexandria
fields.Info:
• Egypt's second-largest city and main Mediterranean port, on the western edge of the Nile Delta, on a strip between the sea and Lake Mariout
  • Founded by Alexander the Great; its ancient Pharos lighthouse was one of the Seven Wonders

fields.Name: Luxor
fields.Info:
• A city on the east bank of the Nile in Upper Egypt, on the site of ancient Thebes
  • Luxor and Karnak temples lie on the east bank; the Valley of the Kings is on the west
fields.Photo caption: The temple on the east bank

fields.Name: Marrakesh
fields.Info:
• A city in western Morocco at the foot of the High Atlas Mountains, on the Haouz plain
  • Its Jemaa el-Fnaa square and Koutoubia Mosque are landmarks; called the Red City

fields.Name: Casablanca
fields.Info:
• Morocco's largest city, a port on the Atlantic coast
  • Its Hassan II Mosque, one of the largest in the world, stands on a rock over the ocean

fields.Name: Timbuktu
fields.Info:
• A city in Mali on the southern edge of the Sahara, about 15 km north of the Niger River
  • A historic trans-Saharan trade and Islamic learning centre with the Djinguereber Mosque

fields.Name: Lagos
fields.Info:
• Nigeria's largest city, a port on the Gulf of Guinea, built around a lagoon and on islands
  • Lagos Island and the Third Mainland Bridge are its features; Abuja replaced it as capital in 1991

fields.Name: Kano
fields.Info:
• A city in northern Nigeria on the Sahel edge, historically a trans-Saharan trade centre
  • Its ancient walls and the Gidan Makama museum are landmarks; the Kano River flows near it

fields.Name: Mombasa
fields.Info:
• Kenya's main port, on a coral island in the Indian Ocean linked to the mainland by bridges and a causeway
  • Fort Jesus, built by the Portuguese in 1593, is its landmark

fields.Name: Zanzibar City
fields.Info:
• The main city of Zanzibar, on the west coast of Unguja island in the Indian Ocean off Tanzania
  • Its Stone Town is a UNESCO site, with narrow alleys and carved doors

fields.Name: Cape Town
fields.Info:
• A port near the southwestern tip of South Africa, on Table Bay beneath Table Mountain
  • The Cape of Good Hope and Robben Island lie nearby; the city is the legislative capital
fields.Photo caption: Lion's Head, the city, and Robben Island offshore

fields.Name: Johannesburg
fields.Info:
• South Africa's largest city, on the high plateau of the Witwatersrand (“white waters ridge”) at about 1,750 m
  • Built on gold; the Soweto township lies to its southwest

fields.Name: Durban
fields.Info:
• A port on the Indian Ocean coast of South Africa, on a natural harbour
  • South Africa's busiest port; its Golden Mile is a beachfront

fields.Name: Timgad
fields.Info:
• A ruined Roman colonial city in the Aurès Mountains of northeastern Algeria, on a high plateau near Batna
  • Founded around 100 CE; its grid layout, triumphal arch, and library are well preserved

fields.Name: Benghazi
fields.Info:
• Libya's second-largest city, a Mediterranean port in Cyrenaica on the eastern shore of the Gulf of Sidra
  • The ancient Greek city of Euesperides, later Berenice, lies beneath it; the Jebel Akhdar uplands rise to the northeast

fields.Name: Lalibela
fields.Info:
• A town in the highlands of northern Ethiopia at about 2,500 m in the Lasta mountains
  • Its rock-hewn churches, including the cross-shaped Church of Saint George, are a UNESCO site
fields.Photo caption: Church of Saint George, hewn from the rock

fields.Name: Great Zimbabwe
fields.Info:
• A ruined stone city in southeastern Zimbabwe, on a hill and in a valley on the plateau between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers
  • Its Great Enclosure and conical tower were built between the 11th and 15th centuries; it gave the country its name
fields.Photo caption: The conical tower inside the Great Enclosure

fields.Name: Chicago
fields.Info:
• The largest city of the Midwest, on the southwestern shore of Lake Michigan at the mouth of the Chicago River
  • Its river was reversed in 1900 to flow away from the lake; its skyline includes the Willis Tower

fields.Name: Los Angeles
fields.Info:
• A city on the Pacific coast of southern California, in a basin ringed by the San Gabriel and Santa Monica mountains
  • The San Andreas Fault runs about 60 km to the northeast; Hollywood and Santa Monica are parts of the metropolitan area
fields.Photo caption: Downtown beneath the San Gabriel Mountains

fields.Name: San Francisco
fields.Info:
• A city at the tip of a peninsula between the Pacific and San Francisco Bay, linked by the Golden Gate Bridge to Marin County
  • Alcatraz Island lies in the bay; the San Andreas Fault runs just to the west
fields.Photo caption: From the Marin Headlands during a superbloom

fields.Name: Boston
fields.Info:
• A port on Massachusetts Bay at the mouth of the Charles River in New England
  • Beacon Hill, Boston Common, and the Freedom Trail are landmarks

fields.Name: New Orleans
fields.Info:
• A port on the Mississippi River near its mouth, on the Gulf of Mexico, largely below sea level and protected by levees
  • Lake Pontchartrain lies to the north; the French Quarter is its old centre

fields.Name: Seattle
fields.Info:
• A city on Puget Sound in the Pacific Northwest, between Elliott Bay and Lake Washington, in view of Mount Rainier
  • Its Space Needle is a landmark; the Olympic Mountains rise across the Sound to the west
fields.Photo caption: With the Space Needle and Mount Rainier

fields.Name: Philadelphia
fields.Info:
• A city on the Delaware River at its confluence with the Schuylkill in Pennsylvania
  • Independence Hall, where the Declaration of Independence was signed, is its landmark

fields.Name: Detroit
fields.Info:
• A city on the Detroit River, which links Lake St. Clair and Lake Erie, opposite Windsor, Ontario
  • Its name comes from the French for “strait”; it is the centre of the US auto industry
fields.Photo caption: The skyline and the Renaissance Center

fields.Name: Toronto
fields.Info:
• Canada's largest city, on the northwestern shore of Lake Ontario, with the Toronto Islands sheltering its harbour
  • The CN Tower is a landmark; Niagara Falls lies about 130 km to the south

fields.Name: Montreal
fields.Info:
• A city on an island at the confluence of the Saint Lawrence and Ottawa rivers in Quebec
  • Mount Royal gave the city its name; the Notre-Dame Basilica is a landmark

fields.Name: Vancouver
fields.Info:
• A port city on Burrard Inlet at the southwestern corner of mainland British Columbia, backed by the Coast Mountains
  • Stanley Park and Granville Island are landmarks; Vancouver Island lies across the Strait of Georgia

fields.Name: Quebec City
fields.Info:
• A city on a cape above the Saint Lawrence River where it narrows, in eastern Canada
  • Its Château Frontenac and walled Old Town are landmarks; the Plains of Abraham lie beside them

fields.Name: Guadalajara
fields.Info:
• Mexico's second-largest city, on a plain in the western highlands of Jalisco, on the Atemajac Valley
  • Known as the birthplace of tequila and mariachi; its cathedral and Hospicio Cabañas are landmarks

fields.Name: Monterrey
fields.Info:
• A city in northeastern Mexico at the foot of the Sierra Madre Oriental, with the Cerro de la Silla rising above it
  • An industrial centre near the US border; the Santa Catarina River runs through it
fields.Photo caption: Cerro de la Silla above the city

fields.Name: Oaxaca City
fields.Info:
• A city in a highland valley of the Sierra Madre del Sur in southern Mexico, at about 1,550 m
  • Its Santo Domingo church and nearby Monte Albán ruins are landmarks

fields.Name: Teotihuacan
fields.Info:
• An ancient city in the Valley of Mexico, about 40 km northeast of Mexico City
  • Its Pyramid of the Sun, Pyramid of the Moon, and the Avenue of the Dead are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: Pyramid of the Sun, with the Avenue of the Dead and the Pyramid of the Moon

fields.Name: Chichen Itza
fields.Info:
• A Maya city on the Yucatán Peninsula, near cenotes (sinkholes) in the flat limestone plain
  • Its pyramid El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcán) and ball court are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: El Castillo (pyramid of Kukulcán) in Chichén Itzá

fields.Name: Havana
fields.Info:
• Cuba's capital, a port on the northwest coast on a bay with a narrow entrance, facing the Straits of Florida
  • The Malecón seawall runs along the shore; La Cabaña fortress and El Morro guard the harbour

fields.Name: Salvador
fields.Info:
• A city on Bahia's Atlantic coast in northeastern Brazil, on a peninsula at the mouth of All Saints' Bay, split into an upper and lower town by a cliff
  • Its Pelourinho quarter is a UNESCO site; the Elevador Lacerda links the towns

fields.Name: Cusco
fields.Info:
• A city in the southeastern Andes of Peru at about 3,400 m, in a valley of the Huatanay River
  • The former capital of the Inca Empire; the Sacsayhuamán fortress lies above it

fields.Name: Machu Picchu
fields.Info:
• An Inca citadel on a ridge at about 2,430 m above the Urubamba River valley in the Peruvian Andes, northwest of Cusco
  • Its Intihuatana stone and terraces are landmarks; it is reached by rail or the Inca Trail

fields.Name: Valparaiso
fields.Info:
• A port on the Pacific coast of central Chile, built on steep hills rising from a crescent bay
  • Its funiculars (ascensores), colourful houses and the historic quarter are UNESCO-listed

fields.Name: Cartagena
fields.Info:
• A port on the Caribbean coast of Colombia, in a bay, protected by a ring of colonial walls and forts
  • Its Castillo San Felipe de Barajas and Old City are UNESCO-listed

fields.Name: Medellin
fields.Info:
• Colombia's second-largest city, in the Aburrá Valley of the Andes at about 1,500 m
  • Known for its Metrocable cable cars and the sculptures of Fernando Botero in Plaza Botero
fields.Photo caption: Metrocable cable cars above the hillside comunas

fields.Name: Cordoba
fields.Info:
• A city in central Argentina on the Suquía River at the foot of the Sierras de Córdoba
  • Its Jesuit Block and Estancias are UNESCO-listed; the National University of Córdoba is one of the oldest in the Americas

fields.Name: Sydney
fields.Info:
• A port on Port Jackson, a natural harbour on Australia's southeast coast, backed by the Blue Mountains
  • Its Opera House and Harbour Bridge are landmarks; Botany Bay lies to the south

fields.Name: Melbourne
fields.Info:
• A city on Port Phillip Bay at the mouth of the Yarra River in southeastern Australia
  • Its Royal Exhibition Building and Flinders Street Station are landmarks; the Dandenong Ranges lie to the east
fields.Photo caption: The CBD from the Shrine of Remembrance

fields.Name: Brisbane
fields.Info:
• A city on the Brisbane River in southeastern Queensland, near Moreton Bay
  • Its South Bank and Story Bridge are landmarks; the Great Dividing Range lies to the west
fields.Photo caption: The skyline from Kangaroo Point Cliffs

fields.Name: Perth
fields.Info:
• A city on the Swan River in southwestern Australia, one of the most isolated major cities in the world
  • Its Kings Park and Rottnest Island are landmarks
fields.Photo caption: Elizabeth Quay and the city centre

fields.Name: Auckland
fields.Info:
• New Zealand's largest city, on a narrow isthmus between the Waitematā Harbour and Manukau Harbour on the North Island
  • Built on a volcanic field with about 50 cones, including Rangitoto; its Sky Tower is a landmark
fields.Photo caption: The skyline and Sky Tower across the harbour

fields.Name: Christchurch
fields.Info:
• A city on the eastern coast of New Zealand's South Island, on the Canterbury Plains near the Avon River
