  • The Port Hills and Banks Peninsula lie to the south; a 2011 earthquake damaged its cathedral

fields.Name: Thames
fields.Info:
• Flows through Oxford, Windsor, and London, passing Tower Bridge and Westminster before the Thames Estuary
  • The longest river entirely in England; the Thames Barrier protects London from tidal surges
fields.Photo caption: The Thames at Westminster, with the London Eye

fields.Name: Lake Tahoe
fields.Info:
• A large alpine lake on the California–Nevada line, famed for its clarity and high elevation
  • The writer Mark Twain called it “the fairest picture the whole earth affords”; the 1960 Winter Olympics were held nearby at Squaw Valley
fields.Photo caption: The north shore from the air
fields.Locator: Region::California and Nevada##Country::United States|Region::California and Nevada

fields.Name: Tigris
fields.Info:
• With the Euphrates, one of the two great rivers of Mesopotamia
  • Nineveh, Baghdad, and Samarra stood on it; it flows from Lake Hazar in Turkey and merges with the Euphrates in the Shatt al-Arab
fields.Photo caption: The Tigris valley in southeastern Turkey

fields.Name: Elbe
fields.Info:
• Rises in the Czech Krkonoše and flows through Dresden, Magdeburg, and Hamburg to the North Sea
  • Was part of the border between East and West Germany; the Vltava, which flows through Prague, joins it at Mělník

fields.Name: Seine
fields.Info:
• Flows through Paris, where the Île de la Cité and Notre-Dame stand on it, to the English Channel at Le Havre
  • Navigable by ocean ships to Rouen; the painter Claude Monet lived at Giverny beside it
fields.Photo caption: The Seine in Paris, with the Pont des Invalides and the Eiffel Tower

fields.Name: Vistula
fields.Info:
• Poland's longest river, flowing through Kraków and Warsaw to the Gdańsk Bay of the Baltic Sea
  • Its delta near Gdańsk splits into several branches

fields.Name: Lhotse
fields.Info:
• The fourth-highest mountain on Earth, in the Himalayas on the Nepal–China border, south of Mount Everest
  • It is connected to Everest by the South Col; its name means “south peak” in Tibetan
fields.Photo caption: The south face of Lhotse, Nepal
fields.Locator: Region::Koshi Province and Tibet##Countries::Nepal and China|Region::Koshi Province and Tibet

fields.Name: Makalu
fields.Info:
• The fifth-highest mountain on Earth, in the Mahalangur Himalayas on the Nepal–China border about 19 km southeast of Mount Everest
  • An isolated peak shaped like a four-sided pyramid
fields.Locator: Region::Koshi Province and Tibet##Countries::Nepal and China|Region::Koshi Province and Tibet

fields.Name: Mount Kilimanjaro
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain in Africa, a dormant volcano in northeastern Tanzania near the Kenyan border
  • Its three volcanic cones are Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira; its glaciers are shrinking rapidly; the highest point is Uhuru Peak on Kibo

fields.Name: Vinson Massif
fields.Info:
• The highest mountain in Antarctica, in the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains
  • One of the Seven Summits; it was first climbed in 1966

fields.Name: Patagonian Desert
fields.Info:
• The largest desert in Argentina and the seventh-largest in the world, in Patagonia east of the Andes
  • It is a cold desert of steppe and plateaus, cut by rivers such as the Río Negro and the Santa Cruz
fields.Photo caption: Steppe of the Patagonian Desert at dawn

fields.Name: Great Basin Desert
fields.Info:
• The largest desert in the United States, in Nevada and Utah, between the Sierra Nevada and the Wasatch Range
  • Its rivers drain inward and never reach the sea; Great Salt Lake is a remnant of ancient Lake Bonneville
fields.Photo caption: Bristlecone pines in Great Basin National Park, Nevada

fields.Name: Great Sandy Desert
fields.Info:
• A desert in northwestern Australia, in Western Australia and the Northern Territory, south of the Kimberley
  • The Gibson Desert lies to the south and the Tanami Desert to the east
fields.Photo caption: The Bungle Bungle Range, Western Australia

fields.Name: Kyzylkum Desert
fields.Info:
• A large desert in Central Asia between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya, in Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and Turkmenistan
  • Its name means “red sand”; Bukhara and Samarkand lie on its edges

fields.Name: Newfoundland and Labrador
fields.Info:
• Canada's easternmost province, the island of Newfoundland plus mainland Labrador, joined to Canada in 1949
  • Gros Morne National Park, the Grand Banks, and the Norse site at L'Anse aux Meadows are in it
fields.Photo caption: Cabot Tower on Signal Hill, above the harbour at St. John's

fields.Name: Yukon
fields.Info:
• The westernmost Canadian territory, bordering Alaska, created in 1898 out of the Northwest Territories after the Klondike Gold Rush
  • Mount Logan, Canada's highest point, and the Klondike goldfields at Dawson City are in it
fields.Photo caption: Kathleen Lake in Kluane National Park

fields.Name: Hawaii (island)
fields.Info:
• The largest and southeasternmost Hawaiian island, bigger than all the others combined, and still growing
  • Holds Mauna Kea, the tallest mountain from base to summit, and the active volcanoes Mauna Loa and Kīlauea in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park
fields.Waters: Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Maui
fields.Info:
• The second-largest Hawaiian island, formed by two volcanoes joined by an isthmus that gives it the name the Valley Isle
  • Haleakalā, a dormant volcano of about 3,055 m, fills its eastern half; the old whaling capital Lahaina is on the west coast
fields.Photo caption: The crater of Haleakalā at sunrise
fields.Waters: Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Oahu
fields.Info:
• The third-largest island but home to about two-thirds of the state's population, and the site of the capital, Honolulu
  • Pearl Harbor, Waikiki, Diamond Head, and the North Shore surf breaks are all on it
fields.Waters: Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Kauai
fields.Info:
• The oldest and northwesternmost of the main islands, heavily eroded and densely vegetated, hence the Garden Isle
  • Holds Waimea Canyon, the Na Pali coast cliffs, and Mount Waiʻaleʻale, among the wettest places on Earth
fields.Waters: Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Molokai
fields.Info:
• A long, thin island between Oʻahu and Maui, with the highest sea cliffs in the world along its north coast
  • The Kalaupapa peninsula held the leprosy settlement where Father Damien worked from 1873
fields.Photo caption: The sea cliffs above Kalaupapa, Molokaʻi
fields.Waters: Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Lanai
fields.Info:
• The smallest publicly accessible main island, once a single vast Dole pineapple plantation, hence the Pineapple Isle
  • Almost the whole island was bought by Larry Ellison in 2012
fields.Photo caption: Lānaʻi City, in the island's uplands
fields.Waters: Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Niihau
fields.Info:
• Privately owned since 1864 and closed to outsiders, which is why it is called the Forbidden Isle
  • Hawaiian remains the first language of its few residents
fields.Waters: Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Kahoolawe
fields.Info:
• The smallest of the eight main islands, uninhabited and without fresh water
  • Used as a US Navy bombing range from 1941 until 1990 and still being cleared of ordnance
fields.Waters: Pacific Ocean

fields.Name: Mount Erebus
fields.Info:
• The southernmost active volcano on Earth, on Ross Island in Antarctica
  • Holds one of the few long-lived lava lakes; named for one of James Clark Ross's ships

fields.Name: Kilauea
fields.Info:
• A shield volcano on the southeast of the island of Hawaii, among the most active on Earth
  • Its Halemaʻumaʻu crater is the traditional home of the goddess Pele
fields.Photo caption: Lava fountains in the summit crater

fields.Name: Mauna Loa
fields.Info:
• The largest active volcano on Earth by volume, on the island of Hawaii
  • A shield volcano whose gentle slopes rise about 4,169 m above sea level
fields.Photo caption: The 2022 eruption on the Northeast Rift Zone

fields.Name: Mount Pinatubo
fields.Info:
• A volcano on Luzon whose 1991 eruption was the second largest of the 20th century
  • It cooled global temperatures by about 0.5 °C and buried Clark Air Base in ash
fields.Photo caption: The crater lake left by the 1991 eruption

fields.Name: Mount Saint Helens
fields.Info:
• A Cascade volcano in Washington whose 18 May 1980 eruption removed its north face
  • The lateral blast flattened forest for miles and cut about 400 m off its summit

fields.Name: Limpopo
fields.Info:
• Rises near Johannesburg and loops north and east to the Indian Ocean at Xai-Xai
  • Forms much of South Africa's borders with Botswana and Zimbabwe

fields.Name: Okavango
fields.Info:
• Flows from Angola into the Kalahari and ends in an inland delta rather than a sea
  • The Okavango Delta's seasonal flood supports one of Africa's great concentrations of game

fields.Name: Orange
fields.Info:
• The longest river in South Africa, rising in the Drakensberg and reaching the Atlantic
  • Forms the border with Namibia and passes the Augrabies Falls

fields.Name: Suez Canal
fields.Info:
• Runs about 193 km across the Isthmus of Suez from Port Said on the Mediterranean to Suez on the Red Sea, without locks
  • It passes through Lake Timsah and the Great Bitter Lake; opened in 1869, it separates Africa from the Sinai Peninsula in Asia
fields.Photo caption: The canal's southern end at Suez, from orbit

fields.Name: Gulf of Aqaba
fields.Info:
• The eastern arm of the Red Sea, between the Sinai Peninsula and Arabia
  • Borders Egypt, Israel, Jordan, and Saudi Arabia; Eilat and Aqaba sit at its head
fields.Photo caption: The Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba from orbit, either side of the Sinai

fields.Name: Bight of Biafra
fields.Info:
• The eastern bight of the Gulf of Guinea, from the Niger delta to Cape Lopez
  • Also called the Bight of Bonny; Bioko and São Tomé lie within it
fields.Photo caption: The bight from orbit, with the island of Bioko

fields.Name: Gulf of Sidra
fields.Info:
• A wide bay of the Mediterranean on the Libyan coast, between Tripolitania and Cyrenaica
  • Libya's claim to it as internal waters led to clashes with the US Navy in the 1980s
fields.Photo caption: The gulf from orbit, with dust blowing off the Libyan coast

fields.Name: Rub' al-Khali
fields.Info:
• The Empty Quarter, the largest continuous sand desert in the world
  • Covers much of southern Saudi Arabia and parts of Oman, Yemen, and the UAE
fields.Photo caption: The Arabian Peninsula from orbit; the sand sea fills its southern third

fields.Name: Painted Desert
fields.Info:
• A badlands of banded red and purple mudstone in northern Arizona
  • Adjoins Petrified Forest National Park; named by Coronado's expedition
fields.Photo caption: Badlands of the Painted Desert, Arizona

fields.Name: Negev
fields.Info:
• A triangular desert covering over half of Israel, its point at the Gulf of Aqaba
  • Its Makhtesh Ramon is a huge erosion crater; Beersheba is its largest city, and Eilat lies at its southern tip
fields.Photo caption: Eroded hills in the central Negev

fields.Name: Mount Mitchell
fields.Info:
• The highest peak in mainland North America east of the Mississippi, at 2,037 m
  • In the Black Mountains of North Carolina; named for Elisha Mitchell, who died surveying it
fields.Photo caption: The view from the summit trail on Mount Mitchell

fields.Name: Columbia
fields.Info:
• Rises in British Columbia and reaches the Pacific at Astoria, the largest river by volume flowing to the Pacific from North America
  • Dammed at Grand Coulee and Bonneville; cuts the Columbia River Gorge

fields.Name: Saint Lawrence
fields.Info:
• Drains the Great Lakes to the Atlantic through a broad estuary
  • The Seaway opened the Lakes to ocean shipping in 1959
fields.Photo caption: The St. Lawrence from the air

fields.Name: Hudson
fields.Info:
• Rises at Lake Tear of the Clouds in the Adirondacks and reaches the sea at New York
  • Linked to the Great Lakes by the Erie Canal in 1825; named for Henry Hudson
fields.Photo caption: The Hudson from the Bear Mountain Bridge

fields.Name: Red River of the South
fields.Info:
• Rises in the Texas Panhandle and joins the Atchafalaya and Mississippi in Louisiana
  • Forms part of the Texas–Oklahoma border; named for its red silt
fields.Photo caption: The Red River from the air

fields.Name: Snake
fields.Info:
• The largest tributary of the Columbia, rising in Wyoming near Yellowstone
  • Cuts Hells Canyon, the deepest river gorge in North America
fields.Photo caption: Ansel Adams, The Tetons and the Snake River, 1942

fields.Name: Potomac
fields.Info:
• Flows past Washington, D.C. to Chesapeake Bay
  • Great Falls lies upstream; Harpers Ferry sits at its junction with the Shenandoah
fields.Photo caption: The Great Falls of the Potomac

fields.Name: Rhine
fields.Info:
• Rises in the Swiss Alps and reaches the North Sea through the Dutch delta
  • Passes the Lorelei rock and the Ruhr; the Rhine Gorge is a World Heritage Site

fields.Name: Tagus
fields.Info:
• The longest river of the Iberian Peninsula, reaching the Atlantic at Lisbon
  • Called the Tejo in Portugal and the Tajo in Spain; passes Toledo
fields.Photo caption: The Tagus at Toledo, below the Puente de San Martín

fields.Name: Rhone
fields.Info:
• Rises at the Rhône Glacier, runs through Lake Geneva and Lyon to a Mediterranean delta
  • Its delta is the Camargue; Avignon and Arles stand on it

fields.Name: Po
fields.Info:
• The longest river in Italy, crossing the north from the Alps to the Adriatic
  • Its plain is Italy's industrial and agricultural heartland; Turin stands on it
fields.Photo caption: The Po at Turin, with the Mole Antonelliana

fields.Name: Loire
fields.Info:
• The longest river in France, rising in the Massif Central and reaching the Atlantic at Saint-Nazaire
  • Its valley is lined with Renaissance châteaux including Chambord and Chenonceau

fields.Name: Shannon
fields.Info:
• The longest river in Ireland or Britain, dividing the west from the rest of Ireland
  • Widens into Lough Ree and Lough Derg; Limerick stands on its estuary

fields.Name: Oder
fields.Info:
• Rises in the Czech Republic and reaches the Baltic through the Szczecin Lagoon
  • The Oder–Neisse line has been the Germany–Poland border since 1945
fields.Photo caption: The Oder and its floodplain from the air
